ASAD-NOTES:3:intro/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:3:intro/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:3:intro/r3.claim: Jesus's deification by later followers exemplifies arbitrary interpretation; the surah presents Mary, Jesus, and Zachariah and stresses Jesus's humanity, mortality, and call to worship God alone.
ASAD-NOTES:3:intro/r3.anchor: The Qur'an takes issue with the Christian doctrine of the divinity of Jesus

ASAD-NOTES:3:intro/r4.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:3:intro/r4.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:3:intro/r4.claim: Asad says it is inconceivable that a human recipient of revelation, judgment, and prophethood would tell people to worship him beside God.

BURSEVI:v2p43#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p43#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p43#2/r1.claim: Many contemporary shaykhs claim states they have not attained and mislead people with false tales devoid of meaning and reality.
BURSEVI:v2p43#2/r1.anchor: وجدت أكثرهم مدعين ما لم يتحققوا به يضلون الناس بأكاذيب

BURSEVI:v2p43#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p43#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p43#2/r2.claim: The discerning should not be deceived by their appearance or imitate them, but distinguish truth from falsehood and the learned from the ignorant.
BURSEVI:v2p43#2/r2.anchor: فعلى العاقل أن لا يغتر بظاهرهم ولا يخرج عن المنهاج مقتفيا بآثارهم

BURSEVI:v2p43#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p43#2/r3.speaker: نصارى نجران
BURSEVI:v2p43#2/r3.claim: The Christians of Najran alleged that Jesus told them to take him as a lord; Bursevi rejects the allegation.
BURSEVI:v2p43#2/r3.anchor: حيث قال نصارى نجران إن عيسى عليه السلام أمرنا أن نتخذه ربا حاشاه عليه السلام

BURSEVI:v2p43#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p43#2/r4.speaker: رسول الله
BURSEVI:v2p43#2/r4.claim: When a Muslim asked whether they should prostrate to the Prophet as they greeted one another, he said God forbid worshipping or commanding worship of anyone besides God.
BURSEVI:v2p43#2/r4.anchor: يا رسول الله نسلم عليك كما يسلم بعضنا على بعض أفلا نسجد لك فقال : "معاذ الله أن نعبد غير الله

BURSEVI:v2p43#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p43#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p43#2/r5.claim: The wording “for a human” signals the reason for the ruling: being human is incompatible with the alleged command to worship him.
BURSEVI:v2p43#2/r5.anchor: فإن البشرية منافية للأمر الذي أسنده الكفرة إليهم

BURSEVI:v2p43#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p43#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p43#2/r6.claim: The revealed book speaks truth, commands tawhid, and forbids shirk; examples include the Torah, Gospel, and Quran.
BURSEVI:v2p43#2/r6.anchor: الناطق بالحق الآمر بالتوحيد الناهي عن الإشراك كالتوراة والإنجيل والقرآن

BURSEVI:v2p43#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p43#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p43#2/r7.claim: Hukm means understanding and knowledge, including wisdom as perfected knowledge and action; scholars of language and exegesis agree it means knowledge.
BURSEVI:v2p43#2/r7.anchor: وإيتاء الكتاب يستلزم إيتاء الحكم وهو الحكمة المعبر عنها باتقان العلم والعمل

BURSEVI:v2p43#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p43#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p43#2/r8.claim: The sequence is book revelation, the prophet’s grasp of its meaning and secrets, then his communication of that understanding to people as prophethood.
BURSEVI:v2p43#2/r8.anchor: فالكتاب السماوي ينزل أولا ثم إنه يحصل في عقل النبي فهم ذلك الكتاب وأسراره

BURSEVI:v2p43#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p43#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p43#2/r9.claim: In “servants of me,” min attaches to ʿibādan because that word carries the sense of an action.
BURSEVI:v2p43#2/r9.anchor: من متعلق بلفظ عبادا لما فيه من معنى الفعل

BURSEVI:v2p43#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p43#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p43#3/r1.claim: A non-emphatic nisba to a beard is called lahwi; the source contrasts this with the intensive rabbani form.
BURSEVI:v2p43#3/r1.anchor: وإذا نسب إلى اللحية من غير قصد المبالغة يقال لحوي

BURSEVI:v2p43#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p43#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p43#3/r2.claim: A rabbani is complete in knowledge and action and firmly adheres to obedience, God’s religion, and knowledge of God.
BURSEVI:v2p43#3/r2.anchor: فالرباني هو الكامل في العلم والعمل الشديد التمسك بطاعة الله تعالى ودينه

BURSEVI:v2p43#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p43#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p43#3/r3.claim: The command to become rabbani is grounded in persistent teaching and studying the book; teaching is mentioned first because it is more honorable.
BURSEVI:v2p43#3/r3.anchor: بسبب مثابرتكم على تعليم الكتاب ودراسته أي قراءته وتقديم التعليم على الدراسة لزيادة شرفه عليها

BURSEVI:v2p43#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p43#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p43#3/r8.claim: Knowledge and study are meant to produce firm obedience; learning without action is like a beautiful tree that bears no useful fruit.
BURSEVI:v2p43#3/r8.anchor: فكان مثل من غرس شجرة حسناء تؤنقه أي تعجبه بمنظرها ولا تنفعه بثمرها

BURSEVI:v2p43#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p43#3/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p43#3/r9.claim: Neither action without knowledge nor knowledge without action establishes a relationship with God; the scholar who does not act is as disconnected as an ignorant worker.
BURSEVI:v2p43#3/r9.anchor: فعلم أن العالم الذي لا يعمل بعلمه منقطع النسبة بينه وبين ربه كالعامل الجاهل

ELMALILI:3:79-81/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:79-81/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:79-81/r1.claim: Elmalılı renders the verse as denying prophets any right to demand worship, while their proper task is to raise rabbānīs through teaching and study.
ELMALILI:3:79-81/r1.anchor: Allah’tan beride bana kul olun” diyebilsin. Velâkin “kitab tâlim etmekte olduğunuz ve ders alıp vermekte bulunduğunuz için rabbânîler olunuz”

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r1.claim: All prophets call people to worship God alone and warn against shirk or claims of divinity; the People of the Book are rebuked for imagining prophets could claim godhood and are urged to reconsider through their own scriptures and study.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r1.anchor: bütün peygamberlerin yalnız Allah’a kulluk etme çağrısıyla görevlendirildiği

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r2.claim: Hukm lexically means deciding, governing, restraining, or preventing; philosophically it is an affirmative or negative relation between ideas or states and its apprehension, and it is classified by knowledge source and field.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r2.anchor: Sözlükte hüküm kelimesi “karar vermek, yönetmek, alıkoymak, engellemek” gibi anlamlara gelir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r3.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r3.claim: Razi says language and tafsir scholars agree that hukm here is the prophet's grasp of the revealed Book and the knowledge formed through that understanding.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r3.anchor: dil ve tefsir âlimlerinin bu âyette geçen hüküm kelimesiyle, Allah tarafından indirilen kitabın peygamber tarafından kavranmasının

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r4.speaker: İbn Atıyye
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r4.claim: Ibn Atiyya explains hukm here as wisdom.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r5.speaker: Muhammed Esed
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r5.claim: Muhammad Asad renders hukm as sound judgment.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r6.claim: The Qur'an uses hukm of God for absolute will, sovereignty, and authority to decide, and of prophets or people for settling legal disputes.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r6.anchor: mutlak irade, hâkimiyet ve karar yetkisi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r7.claim: Nubuwwa means prophethood; those assigned this office by God are called nabi (plural anbiya) and rasul (plural rusul).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r8.claim: One occasion report says the Prophet warned Quraysh against worshipping angels, Jews against Uzayr, and Christians against Jesus; they asked whether he wanted them to take him as lord, prompting revelation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r8.anchor: Kureyş müşriklerini meleklere, yahudileri Üzeyir’e, hıristiyanları da Îsâ’ya kulluk etmekten sakındırıyordu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r9.claim: Another report says a Muslim asked whether they could prostrate to the Prophet as a distinctive greeting, and the verses were revealed because of that request.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r9.anchor: Sana secde ederek farklı bir selâm versek olmaz mı?” dediği için bu âyetler indi.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r16.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r16.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r16.claim: The plural ibad rather than abid for abd signals that no object of worship besides God can promise or grant a person the status of being worshipped.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r16.anchor: abd kelimesinin abîd değil ibâd şeklindeki çoğulu kullanılarak Allah’tan başka hiçbir mâbudun insana bu mevkii vaad edemeyeceğine

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r17.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r17.speaker: İbn Atıyye
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r17.claim: Ibn Atiyya finds that Qur'anic ibad occurs in contexts that honor the servant's will to obey, without connotations of pity or contempt.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r17.anchor: ibâdın “acıma ve küçümseme” anlamıyla ilişkili olmayan, kulun itaat iradesine dikkat çeken

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r20.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r20.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r20.claim: The prophetic counsel is summarized as “Be rabbaniyyun.”
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r20.anchor: Bir peygamberin neyi söylemesinin düşünülemeyeceği belirtildikten sonra, peygamberlerin tavsiyesi şu şekilde özetlenmiştir: “Rabbânîler olun!”

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r21.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r21.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r21.claim: Arabic etymologies explain rabbaniyyun as those who know their Lord and strive to worship Him, learned people who teach and urge good, or educators who train people and guide society; some scholars instead derive it from Syriac or Hebrew.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r21.anchor: “Rabb”ini bilen ve daima O’na kulluk etme çabası gösterenler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r22.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r22.speaker: Ömer Faruk Harman
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r22.claim: In Hebrew, rab (rav) means great and later master or owner; rabbi means my master or teacher, and rabban is an intensified form; rabbaniyyun (rabbanim) are religious scholars, especially Torah scholars, who teach correct belief.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r22.anchor: Özetle İbrânîce’de rabbâniyyûn (rabbanîm), dinî ilimlerle ve bilhassa Tevrat’la meşgul olup halka doğru inanç öğreten din üstatları demektir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r23.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r23.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r23.claim: Rabbaniyyun occurs twice elsewhere beside ahbar, referring to Jewish scholars charged with preserving Torah rulings, teaching them, and ensuring Jews live by them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r23.anchor: Rabbâniyyûn kelimesi Kur’an-ı Kerîm’in iki âyetinde daha “yahudi din bilginleri” anlamına gelen “ahbâr” kelimesiyle birlikte geçmekte

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r24.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r24.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r24.claim: “Be rabbaniyyun” can call everyone to sincere worship of God or especially remind knowledge-bearers and social leaders to teach truth and guide people to salvation; the following reference to teaching and studying supports the latter reading.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r24.anchor: Bu öğütün “öğretmekte olduğunuz kitap ve yapmakta olduğunuz incelemeler gereğince” şeklinde bir dayanağa bağlanması ikinci anlamı teyit etmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r25.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r25.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r25.claim: When leaders truly dedicate themselves to God's path and recognize their duty, those needing guidance have no opening to elevate them to lordly status.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r25.anchor: bu sorumluluğun bilincinde olmaları halinde, yol gösterilmeye muhtaç kişilerin yukarıda değinilen çarpık telakkiye

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r26.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r26.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r26.claim: The verse links knowledge to action: knowledge gains real value through practice, and people should avoid words and behavior that contradict what they have studied and taught.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:79/r26.anchor: ilmin, ancak hayata yansıtılmakla ve aksiyon haline getirilmekle kuru bilgi olmaktan kurtulup gerçek değerini bulabileceği

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p54/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p54/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p54/r1.claim: At a gathering of Jewish and Christian scholars from Najran, Abu Rafi asked whether they should worship Muhammad as Christians worship Jesus; the Prophet sought refuge in God and the passage was revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p54/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال قال أبو رافع القرظي حين اجتمعت الأحبار من اليهود والنصارى من أهل نجران عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p54/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p54/r2.speaker: الحسن
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p54/r2.claim: A man asked whether they could greet the Prophet and prostrate to him; he forbade prostration to anyone besides God, and the passage was revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p54/r2.anchor: عن الحسن قال بلغني أن رجلا قال يا رسول الله نسلم عليك كما يسلم بعضنا على بعض أفلا نسجد لك

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p111/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p111/r4.speaker: الضحاك ومقاتل
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p111/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak and Muqatil say the verse concerned Christians of Najran worshipping Jesus; “human” refers to Jesus and “the Book” to the Gospel.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p111/r4.anchor: قال الضحاك ومقاتل: نزلت في نصارى نجران عبدوا عيسى، وقوله: {لبشر} يعني عيسى

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p111/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p111/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p111/r5.claim: Abu Rafi' and a Christian leader from Najran asked Muhammad whether he wanted them to worship him; he rejected that idea, and the verse was revealed.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p111/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس في رواية الكلبي وعطاء: إن أبا رافع اليهودي والرئيس من نصارى نجران قالا

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p58#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p58#2/r1.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p58#2/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, and Abū ʿAmr read تعلمون lightly, with ungeminated lām.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p58#2/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو: تعلمون بإسكان العين ونصب اللام

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p58#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p58#2/r2.speaker: عاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p58#2/r2.claim: ʿĀṣim, Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī read تعلمون with gemination.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p58#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي: تعلمون مثقلا

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p58#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p58#2/r3.speaker: سيبويه
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p58#2/r3.claim: Sībawayh distinguishes علمت, meaning I taught, from أعلمت, meaning I informed.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p58#2/r3.anchor: قال سيبويه: علمت: أدبت، وأعلمت: آذنت

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p58#2/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p58#2/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p58#2/r4.claim: The preposition ب in بما كنتم attaches to كونوا in كونوا ربانيين, not to the reading verb تعلمون.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p58#2/r4.anchor: والباء في قوله: بما كنتم. متعلقة بقوله: كونوا من قوله: ولكن كونوا ربانيين بما كنتم

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p58#2/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p58#2/r5.speaker: طفيل
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p58#2/r5.claim: Ṭufayl’s line supplies a poetic parallel for attaching ب to an earlier verb.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p58#2/r5.anchor: قول طفيل : نزائع مقذوفا على سرواتها ... بما لم تخالسها الغزاة وتركب

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p58#2/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p58#2/r6.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p58#2/r6.claim: Abū ʿAlī also cites al-Aʿshā’s poetry as another parallel for the same construction.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p58#2/r6.anchor: قول طفيل : نزائع مقذوفا على سرواتها ... بما لم تخالسها الغزاة وتركب وقول الأعشى:

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p59/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p59/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p59/r1.claim: The fragment قالت بما قد أراه بصيرا continues the poetic evidence for the construction cited in the preceding segment as al-Aʿshā’s.

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p59/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p59/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p59/r2.claim: In both readings, ما with the verb forms a verbal noun, approximately بكونكم تعلمون; it has no resumptive pronoun.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p59/r2.anchor: فأما (ما) في كلتا القراءتين فهي التي مع الفعل بتأويل المصدر مثل أن الناصبة للفعل

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p59/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p59/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p59/r3.claim: A resumptive pronoun cannot refer back from كنتم or تعلمون because the predicate and the verb have already taken their required objects.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p59/r3.anchor: ولا عائد من الصلة إلى الموصول، يدلك على ذلك أنه لا يخلو الذكر إن عاد من أن يكون من قوله: كنتم أو من تعلمون

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p59/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p59/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p59/r4.claim: The same verbal-noun parsing appears in بما كانوا يكذبون and the phrase about forgetting the meeting of that Day and denying signs.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p59/r4.anchor: ومثل ذلك قوله: ولهم عذاب أليم بما كانوا يكذبون [البقرة/ 10] ومثله قوله: فاليوم ننساهم كما نسوا لقاء يومهم هذا وما كانوا بآياتنا يجحدون

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p59/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p59/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p59/r5.claim: In the light reading, تعلمون means know or recognize and takes one object, as shown by other Qurʾanic uses of علم.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p59/r5.anchor: فأما قوله: تعلمون: فهو من العلم الذي يراد به المعرفة فيتعدى إلى مفعول واحد

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p59/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p59/r6.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p59/r6.claim: With gemination, the verb becomes causative and takes two objects; the omitted second object is people or others, whom the addressees teach the Book.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p59/r6.anchor: فإذا ضعفت العين تعدى إلى مفعولين، كما أنك لو نقلت بالهمزة كان كذلك

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p59/r7.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p59/r7.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p59/r7.claim: Abū ʿAmr reportedly argues that the following phrase تدرسون supports the light reading تعلمون rather than a causative reading meaning teach.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p59/r7.anchor: أبا عمرو قال فيما زعموا: يصدقها : تدرسون ، ولم يقل: تدرسون

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p59/r8.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p59/r8.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p59/r8.claim: The heavy-reading argument is that teaching and studying repeatedly reveal subtleties that prompt scholars to adhere to and act on their knowledge.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p59/r8.anchor: ومن حجتها أن العالم الدارس قد يدرك بعلمه ودرسه مما يكون داعيا إلى التمسك بعلمه، والعمل به

FARISI-HUJJA:v3p59/r9.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p59/r9.speaker: أبو زيد
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p59/r9.claim: Abū Zayd’s point is that study is not truly study until one reads the material to another person.
FARISI-HUJJA:v3p59/r9.anchor: قال أبو زيد كلاما معناه: لا يكون الدرس درسا حتى تقرأه على غيرك

IBNMUJAHID:v1p212/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p212/r2.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p212/r2.claim: They read تعلمون with a light lām and open tāʾ, keeping the ʿayn unvowelled.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p212/r2.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو ﴿ تعلمون ﴾ بإسكان العين وفتح اللام والتاء خفيفا

IBNMUJAHID:v1p212/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p212/r3.speaker: عاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p212/r3.claim: They read تعلمون with a ḍamma on the tāʾ and a doubled lām.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p212/r3.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي ﴿ تعلمون ﴾ بضم التاء وتشديد اللام

QIRAAT-ER:3:79:12#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:3:79:12#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:3:79:12#1/r1.claim: The hamzated nubūʾa derives from n-b-ʾ, informing, rather than n-b-w, elevation, making the etymological fork phonologically explicit.
QIRAAT-ER:3:79:12#1/r1.anchor: deriving from n-b-ʾ (to inform) rather than n-b-w (to elevate) — etymological fork made phonologically explicit

QIRAAT-ER:3:79:30#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:3:79:30#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:3:79:30#1/r1.claim: Form I taʿlamūna means you know or learn, unlike Form II tuʿallimūna, you teach; the variant shifts the agents from teachers to learners.
QIRAAT-ER:3:79:30#1/r1.anchor: shifts agents from teachers to learners; changes the epistemic relationship entirely

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p125/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p125/r1.speaker: أبو رزين
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p125/r1.claim: Abu Razin glosses rabbaniyyun as forbearing scholars.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p125/r1.anchor: عن منصور بن المعتمر عن أبي رزين في قوله تعالى ﴿ كونوا ربانيين ﴾ قال حلماء علماء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p228/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p228/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p228/r5.claim: An unnamed report says Abū Rāfiʿ al-Quraẓī accused the Prophet, before Jewish scholars and the Najrān Christian delegation, of seeking worship like Jesus; the delegation leader endorsed the question, and the Prophet denied it before the verse was revealed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p228/r5.anchor: روي أن أبا رافع القرظي قال للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، حين اجتمعت الأحبار من يهود، والوفد من نصارى نجران

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p228/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p228/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p228/r6.claim: Another report says a man asked whether they should prostrate to the Prophet; he forbade prostration to anyone besides God and urged them to honor the Prophet and give rights their due.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p228/r6.anchor: لا ينبغي أن يسجد لأحد من دون الله، ولكن أكرموا نبيكم واعرفوا الحق لأهله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p228/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p228/r7.speaker: ابن عباس والربيع وابن جريج وجماعة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p228/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Rabīʿ, Ibn Jurayj, and others take the verse's reference to be Muḥammad and connect it with the reported occasion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p228/r7.anchor: فقال ابن عباس، والربيع، وابن جريج، وجماعة: الإشارة إلى محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، وذكروا سبب النزول المذكور

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p228/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p228/r8.speaker: النقاش وغيره
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p228/r8.claim: Al-Naqqāsh and others take the reference to be Jesus and read the verse as a rebuttal of Christians who claimed he was divine and that he commanded his own worship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p228/r8.anchor: وقال النقاش، وغيره: الإشارة إلى عيسى، والآية رادة على النصارى الذين قالوا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p229/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p229/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p229/r1.claim: The construction mā kāna li-basharin negates the predicate; negation can express rational impossibility or an impossibility appropriate to context, and this verse uses the first kind.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p229/r1.anchor: ومعنى ما كان لبشر أن يؤتيه الله وما جاء نحوه أنه ينفي عنه الكون، والمراد نفي الخبر، وذلك على قسمين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p229/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p229/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p229/r2.claim: The verse's absolute rational negation shows that God does not grant scripture, judgment, and prophecy to a liar who claims prophethood, and it supports the prophets' immunity from sin.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p229/r2.anchor: وهذه الآية من القسم الأول، لأنا نعلم أن الله لا يعطي الكذبة والمدعين النبوة، وفي هذه الآية دلالة على عصمة الأنبياء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p229/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p229/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p229/r3.claim: Al-kitāb is a generic noun; al-ḥukm is best understood as adjudication and judgment among people, following knowledge and preceding the higher rank of prophecy.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p229/r3.anchor: والكتاب: هنا اسم جنس، والحكم: قيل بمعنى الحكمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p229/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p229/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p229/r4.claim: Some interpret al-ḥukm as wisdom, with the saying that poetry contains wisdom offered as a parallel.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p229/r4.anchor: قيل بمعنى الحكمة، ومنه: «إن من الشعر لحكما»

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p229/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p229/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p229/r5.claim: Others take al-ḥukm to mean the Sunnah because it is set beside the Book.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p229/r5.anchor: وقيل: الحكم هنا السنة، يعنون لمقابلته الكتاب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p229/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p229/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p229/r6.claim: The apparent meaning is judgment and decision among people; the verse progresses from knowledge, to authority to judge, to the highest rank of prophethood.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p229/r6.anchor: والظاهر أن الحكم هنا القضاء والفصل بين الناس، وهذا من باب الترقي، بدأ أولا بالكتاب وهو العلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p229/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p229/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p229/r7.claim: Thumma marks a delay to magnify the forbidden claim: if it is impossible after such a great divine gift, it is even more so without a delay.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p229/r7.anchor: ثم يقول للناس: أتى بلفظ: ثم، التي هي للمهلة تعظيما لهذا القول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p229/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p229/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p229/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya lists ʿabīd and ʿabdā as plurals of ʿabd and reports differing claims about whether the forms mean the same, distinguish divine from human servants, or imply servitude by descent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p229/r8.anchor: قال ابن عطية: ومن جموعه: عبيد وعبدى. قال بعض اللغويين: هذه الجموع كلها بمعنى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p229/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p229/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p229/r9.claim: Some linguists distinguish ʿibād as God's servants from ʿabīd as human servants, while others reserve ʿabdā for descendants of slaves.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p229/r9.anchor: وقال قوم: العباد لله والعبيد للبشر. وقال قوم: العبدى إنما يقال في العبيد بني العبيد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p229/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p229/r10.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p229/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya's lexical observation is that ʿibād occurs in contexts of elevation and obedience without contempt, as in several Qurʾanic descriptions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p229/r10.anchor: والذي استقرئت في لفظة: العباد، أنه جمع عبد، متى سيقت اللفظة في مضمار الترفيع والدلالة على الطاعة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p230/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p230/r1.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p230/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says ʿabīd carries a belittling sense, citing Imruʾ al-Qays, Ḥamza, and the Qurʾanic phrase bẓallām lil-ʿabīd; he explains ʿibād as fitting the verse's sense of obedience.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p230/r1.anchor: وأما: العبيد، فيستعمل في التحقير، ومنه قول امرئ القيس: قولا لدودان عبيد العصا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p230/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p230/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p230/r2.claim: Abū Ḥayyān challenges Ibn ʿAṭiyya's generalization: ʿabīd is most properly a plural, while ʿabdā is a collective noun with a feminine-marked alif.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p230/r2.anchor: أما قوله: ومن جموعه: عبيد وعبدى، أما عبيد فالأصح أنه جمع. وقيل: اسم جمع، و: أما عبدى فاسم جمع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p230/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p230/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p230/r3.claim: The claim that ʿibād is elevated and ʿabīd contemptuous is not a sound induction; ʿibād is simply the regular plural pattern for ʿabd, unlike ʿabīd.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p230/r3.anchor: فليس باستقراء صحيح، وإنما كثر استعمال: عباد، دون: عبيد، لأن فعالا في جمع فعل غير اليائي العين قياس مطرد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p230/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p230/r4.speaker: سيبويه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p230/r4.claim: Sībawayh observes that faʿīl occasionally forms a plural but is rare, as in kalīb and ʿabīd.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p230/r4.anchor: قال سيبويه: وربما جاء فعيلا وهو قليل، نحو: الكليب والعبيد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p230/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p230/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p230/r5.claim: The nonstandard plural ʿabīd fits the phrase mā rabbuka bi-ẓallām lil-ʿabīd because it harmonizes with the surrounding verse endings; the same explains the wording in Sūrat Qāf.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p230/r5.anchor: وأما وما ربك بظلام للعبيد فحسن مجيئه هنا وإن لم يكن مقيسا أنه جاء لتواخي الفواصل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p230/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p230/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p230/r6.claim: Semantically, ʿabīd and ʿibād have the same meaning despite their different frequency and rhetorical fit.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r1.claim: In the cited poem, contempt comes from connecting the slaves to a stick and from the whole verse; Ḥamza's words are contemptuous because of the situation, not the word ʿabīd itself.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r1.anchor: وأما بيت امرئ القيس فلم يفهم التحقير من لفظ: عبيد، إنما فهم من إضافتهم إلى العصا، ومن مجموع البيت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r2.claim: Most readers use the subjunctive yaqūla, coordinated with yuʾtiyahu; Shibl from Ibn Kathīr and Maḥbūb from Abū ʿAmr use the indicative, with an implied huwa and a syntactic break.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r2.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: ثم يقول، بالنصب عطفا على: أن يؤتيه، وقرأ شبل عن ابن كثير، ومحبوب عن أبي عمرو: بالرفع على القطع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r3.claim: Most readers pronounce the possessive yāʾ in ʿibādan lī as quiescent, while ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar reads it with fatḥa.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r3.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: عبادا لي، بتسكين ياء الإضافة. وقرأ عيسى بن عمر: بفتحها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r4.claim: The phrase wa-lākin kūnū rabbāniyyīn has an implied verb of saying: but he says, be people of learning and care.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r4.anchor: ولكن كونوا ربانيين هذا على إضمار القول تقديره: ولكن يقول كونوا ربانيين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r5.speaker: قتادة وأبو رزين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r5.claim: Qatāda and Abū Razīn define rabbānī as a wise scholar; Qatāda and others also describe the quality as scholarly gentleness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r5.anchor: والرباني الحكيم العالم، قاله قتادة، وأبو رزين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r6.speaker: علي وابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r6.claim: ʿAlī, Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, and Mujāhid define rabbānī as a jurist; other formulations call the person a wise jurist or a learned jurist.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r6.anchor: أو: الفقيه، قاله علي، وابن عباس، والحسن، ومجاهد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd defines rabbānī as an authority who cultivates and reforms people.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r7.anchor: أو: والي الأمر يربيهم ويصلحهم، قاله ابن زيد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r8.speaker: ابن جبير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r8.claim: Ibn Jubayr defines rabbānī both as wise and pious and as a scholar who acts on his knowledge.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r8.anchor: أو: الحكيم التقي، قاله ابن جبير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r9.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r9.claim: Al-Zajjāj defines rabbānī as a teacher.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r10.speaker: المبرد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r10.claim: Al-Mubarrad defines rabbānī as a scholar.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r11.speaker: المؤرج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r11.claim: Al-Muʾarrij defines rabbānī as one who repents to his Lord.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r12.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r12.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī defines rabbānī as one firmly attached to God's religion and obedience.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r12.anchor: أو: الشديد التمسك بدين الله وطاعته، قاله الزمخشري

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r13.speaker: عطاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r13.claim: ʿAṭāʾ defines rabbānī as a learned, wise person who sincerely seeks the good of God's creatures.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r13.anchor: أو: العالم الحكيم الناصح لله في خلقه، قاله عطاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r14.claim: Abū Ḥayyān judges these definitions to be close in meaning.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r15.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r15.claim: Mujāhid ranks a rabbānī above a ḥibr: beyond scholarship, a rabbānī combines learning and jurisprudence with political administration and care for subjects' religious and worldly needs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r15.anchor: وقال مجاهد: الرباني فوق الحبر، لأن الحبر هو العالم، والرباني الذي جمع إلى العلم والفقه النظر بالسياسة والتدبير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r16.speaker: البخاري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r16.claim: Al-Bukhārī gives a definition of rabbānī as someone who teaches people small matters of knowledge before great ones.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r16.anchor: الرباني الذي يربي الناس بصغار العلم قبل كباره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r17.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r17.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya summarizes rabbānī as a scholar who judges accurately in words and actions undertaken among people.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r17.anchor: قال ابن عطية: فجملة ما يقال في الرباني: إنه العالم المصيب في التقدير من الأقوال والأفعال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r18.speaker: محمد بن الحنفية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r18.claim: When Ibn ʿAbbās died, Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyya called him the rabbānī of the community.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r18.anchor: ولما مات ابن عباس قال محمد بن الحنفية: اليوم مات رباني هذه الأمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r19.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r19.claim: The bāʾ in bi-mā is causal, and mā is most likely a verbal noun; light taʿlamūn takes one object, while intensive tuʿallimūn takes two with people as an omitted first object.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r19.anchor: الباء للسبب، و: ما، الظاهر أنها مصدرية، و: تعلمون، متعد لواحد على قراءة الحرميين وأبي عمرو

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r20.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r20.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r20.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects ranking the two canonical readings, since both are transmitted mutawātir Qurʾān readings.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p231/r20.anchor: وقد تقدم أني لا أرى شيئا من هذه التراجيح، لأنها كلها منقولة متواترة قرآنا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p233/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p233/r1.speaker: مجاهد والحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p233/r1.claim: Mujāhid and al-Ḥasan read taʿlamūn with fatḥa and gemination, treating it as a shortened form of tataʿallamūn; grammarians differ over which initial tāʾ was dropped.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p233/r1.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد، والحسن: تعلمون، بفتح التاء والعين واللام المشددة، وهو مضارع حذفت منه التاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p233/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p233/r2.speaker: أبو حيوة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p233/r2.claim: Abū Ḥaywa reads tadrusūn with a kasra on rāʾ and is also reported to read it with a geminated rāʾ, meaning that they teach others.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p233/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة: تدرسون بكسر الراء. وروي عنه: تدرسون، بضم التاء وفتح الدال وكسر الراء المشددة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p233/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p233/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p233/r3.claim: For the geminated tadrusūn reading, the doubling may mark causation or simply intensification.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p233/r3.anchor: أي: تدرسون غيركم العلم، ويحتمل أن يكون التضعيف للتكثير لا للتعدية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p233/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p233/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p233/r4.claim: Another reading derives tadrusūn from adrasa with the same meaning as darasa, like the paired forms akrama and karuma or anzala and nazala.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p233/r4.anchor: من أدرس بمعنى درس نحو: أكرم وكرم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p233/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p233/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p233/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says authority and leadership should arise from knowledge and study; he likens study without practice to a beautiful tree that bears no useful fruit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p233/r5.anchor: قال الزمخشري: أوجب أن تكون الرئاسة التي هي قوة التمسك بطاعة الله مسببة عن العلم والدراسة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p233/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p233/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p233/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī further says that someone who learns without acting has no connection with God, since only obedience establishes that relationship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p233/r6.anchor: وفيه أن من علم ودرس العلم ولم يعمل به فليس من الله في شيء، وأن السبب بينه وبين ربه منقطع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p233/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p233/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p233/r7.claim: Abū Ḥayyān detects a Muʿtazilī implication in al-Zamakhsharī's claim: that a person is not a believer or scholar without action and that action is a condition of sound faith.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p233/r7.anchor: وفيه دسيسة الاعتزال، وهو أنه: لا يكون مؤمنا عالما إلا بالعمل، وأن العمل شرط في صحة الإيمان

QASHANI:3:64/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:3:64/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:3:64/r2.claim: Prophetic commissioning follows sainthood and annihilation in unity: God effaces the prophet’s human self and grants luminous, Real existence fit for scripture and divine wisdom before he calls people.
QASHANI:3:64/r2.anchor: الاستنباء لا يكون إلا بعد مرتبة الولاية والفناء في التوحيد

QASHANI:3:64/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:3:64/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:3:64/r3.claim: A caller to himself remains veiled by ego, like Pharaoh and those who knew unity intellectually but did not experience it, attain direct vision, or taste annihilation.
QASHANI:3:64/r3.anchor: إذ الداعي إلى نفسه يكون محجوبا بالنفس كفرعون وأضرابه

QASHANI:3:64/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:3:64/r4.speaker: رسول الله
QASHANI:3:64/r4.claim: The Prophet calls the person whom the Resurrection overtakes while alive the worst of people.
QASHANI:3:64/r4.anchor: قال فيهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " شر الناس من قامت القيامة عليه وهو حي "

QASHANI:3:64/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:3:64/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:3:64/r5.claim: Being godly means being attributed to the Lord as lordship overwhelms the person and erases human selfhood; it is reached through knowledge, practice, teaching, reciting scripture, and sustained worship until light overcomes darkness.
QASHANI:3:64/r5.anchor: منسوبين إلى الرب لاستيلاء الربوبية عليهم وطمس البشرية بسبب كونهم عالمين عاملين معلمين تالين لكتب الله

QUSHAYRI:v1p154/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p154/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p154/r5.claim: God's chosen prophets and saints do not call people to themselves or their own interests; election to prophecy entails protection from such error, and messengers and friends call people to God.
QUSHAYRI:v1p154/r5.anchor: أي ليس من صفة من اختراناه للنبوة واصطفيناه للولاية أن يدعو الخلق إلى نفسه

QUSHAYRI:v1p154/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p154/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p154/r6.claim: Rabbani means that prophets and saints direct people to become devoted to the Lord.
QUSHAYRI:v1p154/r6.anchor: وهو معنى قوله تعالى : { ولكن كونوا ربانيين } أي إنما أشار بهم على الخلق بأن يكونوا ربانيين

QUSHAYRI:v1p154/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p154/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p154/r7.claim: Linguistically, rabbani is an adjective related to rabb, on the pattern of other nisba adjectives.
QUSHAYRI:v1p154/r7.anchor: والرباني منسوب إلى الرب كما يقال فلان دقياني ولحياني

QUSHAYRI:v1p154/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p154/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p154/r8.claim: A rabbani knows and is forbearing in God, has relinquished self-interest, and is absorbed in the realities of divine existence beyond awareness of personal states; he speaks, hears, and sees by God, effaced from all else.
QUSHAYRI:v1p154/r8.anchor: وهم العلماء بالله الحلماء في الله القائمون بفنائهم عن غير الله ، المستهلكة حظوظهم

QUSHAYRI:v1p154/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p154/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p154/r9.claim: It is said that a rabbani has risen above the shadow of self and lives under God's shadow.
QUSHAYRI:v1p154/r9.anchor: ويقال الرباني من ارتفع عنه ظل نفسه ، وعاش في كنف ظله - سبحانه

QUSHAYRI:v1p154/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p154/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p154/r10.claim: It is said that a rabbani affirms no one but his Lord and attributes no particle of annihilation or establishment to anyone else.
QUSHAYRI:v1p154/r10.anchor: ويقال الرباني الذي لا يثبت غير ربه موحدا ، ولا يشهد ذرة من المحو والإثبات لغيره أو من غيره

QUSHAYRI:v1p154/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p154/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p154/r11.claim: It is said that the rabbani is realized in God's existence yet effaced from witnessing himself, with God acting and directing all that concerns him.
QUSHAYRI:v1p154/r11.anchor: ويقال الرباني من هو محق في وجوده - سبحانه - ومحو عن شهوده ، فالقائم عنه غيره

ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r1.claim: The verse absolves God's prophets after the People of the Book's accusation against God; another view calls it a refutation of Jesus's worshippers.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r1.anchor: تنزيه لأنبياء الله تعالى عليهم الصلاة والسلام إثر تنزيه الله تعالى عن نسبة ما افتراه أهل الكتاب إليه

ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r2.claim: Another view treats the verse as a denial and refutation directed at those who worship Jesus.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r2.anchor: وقيل : تكذيب ورد على عبدة عيسى عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports through Ibn Isḥāq and others that Abū Rāfiʿ al-Quraẓī asked whether Muḥammad wanted them to worship him as Christians worship Jesus; a Najrān Christian leader asked the same, and the Prophet denied this and said he was not sent or commanded to call people to worship anyone but God; the verse was revealed.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r3.anchor: وأخرج ابن إسحق وغيره عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما قال قال أبو رافع القرظي حين اجتمعت الاحبار من اليهود والنصارى

ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r4.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan says a man asked whether they could greet the Prophet as they greeted one another and prostrate to him; the Prophet said to honor the prophet and give people their due, for none should be prostrated to besides God, and the verse was revealed.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r4.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد عن الحسن قال : بلغني أن رجلا قال : يا رسول الله نسلم عليك كما يسلم بعضنا على بعض افلا نسجد لك

ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r5.speaker: ابن أبي حاتم
ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r5.claim: A report transmitted by Ibn Abī Ḥātim says some Jews made people serve them by distorting scripture from its proper place, prompting this verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r5.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم قال : كان ناس من يهود يتعبدون الناس من دون ربهم بتحريفهم كتاب الله تعالى عن موضعه

ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r6.claim: The phrase mā kāna can mean that such conduct is not valid, not appropriate, or not permitted.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r6.anchor: والمعنى ما يصح وقيل : ما ينبغي وقيل : لا يجوز لأحد

ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r7.claim: Calling the person bashar hints at the reason for the ruling: human nature is incompatible with the claim the unbelievers attribute to those noble prophets.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r7.anchor: وعبر بالبشر إيذائا بعلة الحكم فان البشرية منافية للأمر الذي اسنده الكفرة إلى أولئك الكرام

ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r8.claim: The preposed lām phrase is the predicate of kāna and the clause with an is its subject; an implied conjunction is needed for sound meaning, since many humans received scripture and prophethood.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r8.anchor: والجاز خبر مقدم لكان والمنسبك من ( أن ) والفعل بعد اسمها ولا بد لاستقامة المعنى من ملاحظة العطف

ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r9.claim: Thumma emphasizes the enormity of a prophet making this claim after the divine gift: if it is impossible after a delay, it is even more impossible immediately.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r9.anchor: وعطف الفعل على منصوب ان بثم تعظيما لهذا القول فانه إذا انتقى بعد مهلة كان انتقاؤه بدونها اولى واحرى

ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r10.claim: Here ḥukm means wisdom, as explained earlier.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r10.anchor: والحكم بمعنى الحكمة وقد تقدم معناه

ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r11.speaker: القاضي
ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r11.claim: Al-Qāḍī says ʿibād is the plural of ʿabd in the sense of worship; ʿabīd instead denotes servitude that can belong to someone other than God.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r11.anchor: قال القاضي : وهو هنا من العبادة ولم يقل عبيدا لأنه من العبودية وهي لا تمتنع أن تكون لغير الله

ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r12.speaker: الجبائي
ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r12.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī explains min dūn Allāh as describing people who go beyond God by either associating others or singling them out; the phrase can be an additional adjective or circumstantial clause.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r12.anchor: كما قال الجبائي فان التجاوز متحقق فيهما حتما ثم إن هذا الايتاء في الآية حقيقة على الروايتين الأوليين

ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r13.claim: God's bestowal is literal according to the first two transmitted occasions, but metaphorical in the account about Jewish scholars distorting scripture.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p207/r13.anchor: ثم إن هذا الايتاء في الآية حقيقة على الروايتين الأوليين مجاز على الرواية الأخيرة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r1.claim: Wa-lākin kūnū rabbāniyyīn affirms what was denied: a prophet does not tell people to worship him but tells them to become learned, devout servants of God; the verb is coordinated in the subjunctive.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r1.anchor: إثبات لما نفي سابقا وهو القول المنصوب بأن كأنه قيل : ما كان لذلك البشر أن يقول ذلك لكن يقول كونوا ربانيين

ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r2.claim: Some allow the verb indicative based on the meaning “he does not say”; another analysis omits an implied saying and means they should not say that but should be rabbāniyyūn.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r2.anchor: وجوز رفعه على المعنى لأنه في معنى لا يقول وقيل ك يصح عدم تقدير القول على معنى لا تكونوا قائلين لذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r3.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r3.claim: ʿAlī and Ibn ʿAbbās define rabbānī as a learned jurist.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r3.anchor: وفسر علي كرم الله وجهه وابن عباس الرباني بالفقيه العالم

ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r4.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r4.claim: Qatāda and al-Suddī define rabbānī as a wise scholar.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r5.speaker: ابن جبير
ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r5.claim: Ibn Jubayr defines rabbānī as wise and God-fearing.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd defines rabbānī as one who manages the affairs of people; the author says these definitions are close.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r6.anchor: وابن زيد بالمدبر امر الناس وهي أقوال متقاربة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r7.claim: The word rabbānī is Arabic, not Syriac, according to the sounder view; Abū ʿUbaydah claims Arabs do not know it.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r7.anchor: وهو لفظ عربي لا سرياني على الصحيح + وزعم أبو عبيدة أن العرب لا تعرفه

ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r8.claim: The common derivation relates the word to rabb with emphatic nisba endings; another derives it from rabbān, “educator,” on the pattern of ʿaṭshān.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r8.anchor: وهو منسوب إلى الرب كالهي والألف والنون يزدادان في النسب للبالغة كثيرا

ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r9.claim: The bi-phrases explain why people should become rabbānī: they persist in teaching scripture and studying it; knowledge must be joined to practice, since neither alone counts.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r9.anchor: الباء السببية متعلقة بكونوا أي كونوا كذلك بسبب مثابرتكم على تعليمكم الكتاب ودراستكم له والمطلوب أن لا ينفك العلم عن العمل

ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r10.claim: Other syntactic analyses attach the cause phrase to rabbāniyyīn or treat it as an omitted modifier.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r10.anchor: متعلقة م بربانيين لان فيه معنى الفعل وقيل : بمحذوف وقع صفة له

ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r11.claim: Dirāsah means repetition and can also mean reading; repeating “because you were” marks teaching and reading as distinct, sustained causes of attaining rabbāni status.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r11.anchor: والدراسة التكرار يقال : درس الكتاب أي كرره وتطلق على القراءة وتكرير ( بما كنتم ) للإشعار باستقلال كل من استمرار التعليم واستمرار القراءة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r12.claim: The imperfect verb after kāna suggests continuing teaching and reading that cultivates rabbāni character; teaching is placed first for its greater honor or because the first audience were leaders and the second their subordinates.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r12.anchor: المشعربة جعل خبر ( كان ) مضارعا بالفضل وتحصيل الربانية وقدم تعليم الكتاب على دراسته لوفور شرفه عليها

ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r13.claim: A further interpretation takes the taught scripture as the Qurʾān and the studied material as fiqh; al-Ālūsī considers it quite remote, despite hints in some early authorities.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r13.anchor: وقيل : لأن متعلق التعليم الكتاب بمعنى القرآن ومتعلق الدراسة الفقه وفيه بعد بعيد

ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r14.speaker: نافع
ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r14.claim: Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, Yaʿqūb, Abū ʿAmr, and Mujāhid read taʿlamūn as “being knowledgeable.”
ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r14.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن كثير ويعقوب وابو عمرو ومجاهد ( تعلمون ) بمعنى عالمين

ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r15.claim: Tadrusūn is also read with doubled dāl or with hamza prefix; both convey the same sense, and the common form may likewise mean teaching it to people.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p208/r15.anchor: وقرئ ( تدرسون ) بالتشديد من التدريس وتدرسون من الإدراس بمعناه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r1.speaker: مقاتل والضحاك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r1.claim: Maqatil and al-Dahhak identify the human in the verse as Jesus, because Christians of Najran claimed he ordered them to worship him as lord.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل والضحاك: ما كان لبشر يعني: عيسى عليه السلام، وذلك أن نصارى نجران كانوا يقولون: إن عيسى أمرهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وعطاء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas and ʿAta identify the human as Muhammad and the scripture as the Qur'an; Abu Rafiʿ and a Najran leader accused Muhammad of wanting their worship, so the verse was revealed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وعطاء: {ما كان لبشر} يعني محمدا {أن يؤتيه الله الكتاب} أي القرآن،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r3.claim: The phrase means that it is not appropriate for a human to receive scripture, judgment, and prophethood and then tell people to worship him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r3.anchor: {ما كان لبشر} أي ما ينبغي لبشر، كقوله تعالى: " ما يكون لنا أن نتكلم بهذا "

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r4.claim: Bashar denotes all human beings and has no singular form from the same word; like qawm and jaysh it may refer to one person or a group.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r4.anchor: والبشر: جميع بني آدم لا واحد له من لفظه، كالقوم والجيش ويوضع موضع الواحد والجمع،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r5.claim: Al-ḥukm is glossed either as understanding and knowledge or as the authority to enact God's judgment; prophethood is the prophets' exalted rank.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r5.anchor: {أن يؤتيه الله الكتاب والحكم} الفهم والعلم وقيل: إمضاء الحكم عن الله عز وجل، {والنبوة} المنزلة الرفيعة بالأنبياء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r6.speaker: علي وابن عباس والحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r6.claim: Ali, Ibn Abbas, and al-Hasan define rabbaniyyun as jurists and learned scholars.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r6.anchor: قال علي وابن عباس والحسن: كونوا فقهاء علماء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r7.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r7.claim: Qatada defines rabbaniyyun as wise scholars.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r8.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r8.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr defines a rabbani as a scholar who acts on his knowledge.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r8.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: العالم الذي يعمل بعلمه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r9.speaker: سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r9.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas through Saʿid ibn Jubayr calls rabbaniyyun jurists who teach.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r9.anchor: وعن سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس: فقهاء معلمين.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r10.claim: Another explanation says rabbani teachers bring people along through basic knowledge before advanced knowledge.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r10.anchor: وقيل: الرباني الذي يربي الناس بصغار العلم قبل كباره،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r11.speaker: عطاء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r11.claim: ʿAta describes them as learned, wise, and sincerely advising God's creatures.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r11.anchor: وقال عطاء: علماء حكماء نصحاء لله في خلقه،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r12.speaker: أبو عبيدة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r12.claim: Abu ʿUbayda transmits a scholar's definition: a rabbani knows lawful and forbidden matters, commands and prohibitions, and the community's history and future.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r12.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: سمعت رجلا عالما يقول: الرباني العالم بالحلال والحرام والأمر والنهي،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r13.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r13.claim: One view ranks rabbaniyyun above the ahbar: ahbar are scholars, while rabbaniyyun combine knowledge with insight into governing people.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r13.anchor: وقيل: الربانيون فوق الأحبار، والأحبار: العلماء، والربانيون: الذين جمعوا مع العلم البصارة بسياسة الناس.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r14.speaker: المؤرج
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r14.claim: Al-Muʾarrij derives rabbani from lordship: it was originally rabbi, then an intensifying alif and a nūn were added, as in Ṣanʿani and Bahrani.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p59#2/r14.anchor: قال المؤرج: كونوا ربانيين تدينون لربكم، من الربوبية، كان في الأصل ربي فأدخلت الألف للتفخيم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p60/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p60/r1.speaker: المبرد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p60/r1.claim: Al-Mubarrad says rabbaniyyun are people of learning, named for cultivating knowledge and teaching students basic sciences before advanced ones.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p60/r1.anchor: وقال المبرد: هم أرباب العلم سموا به لأنهم يربون العلم، ويقومون به ويربون المتعلمين بصغار العلوم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p60/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p60/r2.speaker: المبرد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p60/r2.claim: Al-Mubarrad says anyone who repairs and completes something has 'raised' it; rabbani is formed from rabban with the nisba yāʾ, like laḥyani and raqbani.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p60/r2.anchor: وكل من قام بإصلاح شيء وإتمامه فقد ربه يربه، واحدها: "ربان"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p60/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p60/r3.speaker: علي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p60/r3.claim: A report from Ali defines a rabbani as one who nurtures his knowledge through practice.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p60/r3.anchor: وحكي عن علي رضي الله عنه أنه قال: هو الذي يرب علمه، بعمله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p60/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p60/r4.speaker: محمد بن الحنفية
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p60/r4.claim: When Ibn Abbas died, Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya called him the rabbani of this community.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p60/r4.anchor: قال محمد بن الحنفية لما مات ابن عباس: اليوم مات رباني هذه الأمة.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p60/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p60/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p60/r5.claim: In 'because you were teaching,' kuntum means 'you are,' as in the verse about the one in the cradle, meaning one who is in the cradle.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p60/r5.anchor: {بما كنتم} أي: بما أنتم، كقوله تعالى: " من كان في المهد صبيا "

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p60/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p60/r6.speaker: ابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p60/r6.claim: These readers pronounce taʿallamūna with a doubled lām, from the causative verb meaning to teach.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p60/r6.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي " تعلمون " بالتشديد من التعليم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p60/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p60/r7.speaker: الآخرون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p60/r7.claim: Other readers pronounce taʿlamūna lightly, from the verb meaning to know.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p60/r7.anchor: وقرأ الآخرون " تعلمون " بالتخفيف من العلم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p60/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p60/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p60/r8.claim: The phrase wa-bimā kuntum tadrusūn means 'and because you studied/read.'

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:79/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:79/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:79/r1.claim: The verse denies and rebuts the claim that Jesus is a deity to be worshipped.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:79/r1.anchor: تكذيب ورد على عبده عيسى عليه السلام.

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:79/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:79/r2.speaker: أبو رافع القرظي والسيد النجراني
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:79/r2.claim: They asked Muhammad whether he wanted them to worship him and take him as lord; he denied that he was sent to command worship of anyone but God, and the verse was revealed.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:79/r2.anchor: أن أبا رافع القرظي والسيد النجراني قالا: يا محمد أتريد أن نعبدك

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:79/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:79/r3.speaker: رجل
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:79/r3.claim: A man asked whether they should greet the Prophet as one another did and prostrate to him; he said no one should prostrate except God, but they should honor their Prophet and recognize rightful claims.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:79/r3.anchor: قال رجل يا رسول الله نسلم عليك كما يسلم بعضنا على بعض

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:79/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:79/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:79/r4.claim: A rabbānī is ascribed to the Lord with an added alif and nūn, like liḥyānī and raqibānī, and is complete in knowledge and action.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:79/r4.anchor: والرباني منسوب إلى الرب بزيادة الألف والنون

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:79/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:79/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:79/r5.claim: The phrase means that they became teachers of scripture and studied it; the purpose of teaching and learning is to know truth and good for belief and action.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:79/r5.anchor: بسبب كونكم معلمين الكتاب وبسبب كونكم دارسين له

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:79/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:79/r6.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو ويعقوب
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:79/r6.claim: They read taʿlamūn as meaning “being knowledgeable.”
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:79/r6.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو ويعقوب تعلمون بمعنى عالمين

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:79/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:79/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:79/r7.claim: The forms of tadrusūn may derive from teaching or from adrasa, meaning to study; the common reading can also mean teaching scripture to people.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:79/r7.anchor: من التدريس وتدرسون من أدرس بمعنى درس

SULAMI:v1p103#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p103#2/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p103#2/r1.claim: Al-Wasiti says the lordly possess things without being possessed by anything.
SULAMI:v1p103#2/r1.anchor: قال الواسطي : يملكون الأشياء ولا يملكهم شيء .

SULAMI:v1p103#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p103#2/r2.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p103#2/r2.claim: One explanation calls the lordly people learned in God and wise among His servants.
SULAMI:v1p103#2/r2.anchor: وقيل : كونوا ربانيين علماء بالله حكماء بين عباده .

SULAMI:v1p103#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p103#2/r3.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p103#2/r3.claim: Ibn Ata says people should witness the moments of their ordering so they can escape these spiritual afflictions.
SULAMI:v1p103#2/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء : عاينوا أوقات ترتيبكم لتتخلصوا من هذه الآفات كلها .

SULAMI:v1p103#2/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p103#2/r4.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v1p103#2/r4.claim: Jaafar says the lordly listen with the hearing of their hearts and see with the eyes of the unseen.
SULAMI:v1p103#2/r4.anchor: وقال جعفر في قوله : ﴿ كونوا ربانيين ﴾ قال : مستمعين بسمع القلوب وناظرين بأعين الغيوب .

SULAMI:v1p103#2/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p103#2/r5.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p103#2/r5.claim: Ibn Ata says this address lifts them beyond the prior description of servanthood.
SULAMI:v1p103#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : أخرجهم بهذا الخطاب عما خاطبهم به من العبودية .

SULAMI:v1p103#2/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p103#2/r6.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p103#2/r6.claim: Al-Wasiti says to witness one's pre-eternal ordering and decree: pride in descent from Adam or association with Muhammad is less than pride in the One who sanctified one before time.
SULAMI:v1p103#2/r6.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمة الله عليه : عاينوا أوقات ترتيبكم وتقديركم قبل آدم ومحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم والإنتساب إلى آدم

SULAMI:v1p103#2/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p103#2/r7.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p103#2/r7.claim: Al-Wasiti presents Abu Bakr's composure at Badr as an example of lordly trust: he told the Prophet to stop pleading because God would fulfill His promise.
SULAMI:v1p103#2/r7.anchor: وقال أيضا : ﴿ كونوا ربانيين ﴾ قال : كونوا كأبي بكر رضي الله عنه إذ ورد عليه فوادح الأمور لا يؤثر على سره حين قال للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يوم بدر

SULAMI:v1p103#2/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p103#2/r8.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p103#2/r8.claim: Al-Wasiti contrasts Abraham's command to surrender with Muhammad's command to know; lordliness joins manifest servanthood with knowledge of God and connection to pre-eternity and eternity.
SULAMI:v1p103#2/r8.anchor: وقال أيضا في هذه الآية : أمر إبراهيم صلى الله عليه وسلم بالإستسلام ، وأمر محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم بالعلم فقال : ﴿ فاعلم ﴾

SULAMI:v1p103#2/r9.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p103#2/r9.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p103#2/r9.claim: Al-Wasiti says this command draws people away from pride in earthly clay and toward pride in God.
SULAMI:v1p103#2/r9.anchor: وقال في قوله : ﴿ كونوا ربانيين ﴾ : جذبهم بهذا من الإفتخار بالطين إلى الإفتخار بالحق .

SULAMI:v1p103#2/r10.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p103#2/r10.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v1p103#2/r10.claim: Junayd says the address draws people out of created existence and toward God; spiritual stations are read from character and inner disposition, while one who boasts of servanthood may unknowingly contend in lordship.
SULAMI:v1p103#2/r10.anchor: وقال الجنيد رحمة الله عليه : أخرجهم من الكون جملة ، وجذبهم إلى الحق إشارة ، وإذا أردت أن تعرف مقامات الخلق ومواطنهم في الحقيقة

SULAMI:v1p103#2/r11.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p103#2/r11.speaker: بعض العراقيين
SULAMI:v1p103#2/r11.claim: Some Iraqis say the address detaches people from Adam so they forget servanthood and cease boasting of their descent from water and clay.
SULAMI:v1p103#2/r11.anchor: وقال بعض العراقيين : أخرجهم من آدم وبرأهم منه كي ينسوا العبودية ويتركوا الإفتخار بالماء والطين .

SULAMI:v1p104/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p104/r1.speaker: الشبلي
SULAMI:v1p104/r1.claim: Al-Shibli says a prophet who merits divine knowledge receives knowledge only from God and refers its explanation only to God.
SULAMI:v1p104/r1.anchor: وقال الشبلي في قوله تعالى : ﴿ كونوا ربانيين ﴾ قال : أخرجهم عما خاطبهم به من العبودية ، فمن استحق العلم به استحق علم الربانية

SULAMI:v1p104/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p104/r2.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p104/r2.claim: Al-Wasiti says it is better to be a child of pre-eternity and eternity than of water, clay, deeds, reckoning, and number.
SULAMI:v1p104/r2.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمة الله عليه في هذه الآية : ﴿ كونوا ربانيين ﴾ قال : لأن تكون ابن الأزل والأبد خير لك وأحسن من أن تكون من أبناء الماء والطين

SULAMI:v1p104/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p104/r3.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v1p104/r3.claim: Sahl defines the lordly person as one who knows God and His command and receives hidden, divinely bestowed knowledge.
SULAMI:v1p104/r3.anchor: وقال سهل : الرباني هو العالم بالله والعالم بأمر الله والمكاشف له من العلوم اللدنى ما غيبه عن غيره .

SULAMI:v1p104/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p104/r4.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v1p104/r4.claim: Sahl also says the lordly person does not prefer any state over his Lord.
SULAMI:v1p104/r4.anchor: وقال أيضا : الرباني الذي لا يختار على ربه حالا .

SULAMI:v1p104/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p104/r5.speaker: الجريري
SULAMI:v1p104/r5.claim: Al-Jurayri defines the lordly as hearing from God and speaking through God.
SULAMI:v1p104/r5.anchor: وقال الجريري : ﴿ كونوا ربانيين ﴾ أي سامعين من الله ناطقين بالله .

SULAMI:v1p104/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p104/r6.speaker: الفضل بن العباس
SULAMI:v1p104/r6.claim: Al-Fadl ibn al-Abbas says to emulate Abu Bakr, whose heart remained steady at the Prophet's death as he declared that God lives and never dies.
SULAMI:v1p104/r6.anchor: سمعت محمد بن عبد الله يقول : سمعت الفضل بن العباس يقول : في قوله عز وعلا : ﴿ كونوا ربانيين ﴾ قال : كونوا كأبي بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه

SULAMI:v1p104/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p104/r7.speaker: القاسم
SULAMI:v1p104/r7.claim: Al-Qasim says the lordly should embody God's qualities and be knowledgeable and forbearing.
SULAMI:v1p104/r7.anchor: وقال القاسم : ﴿ كونوا ربانيين ﴾ متخلقين بأخلاق الحق علماء حلماء .

SULAMI:v1p104/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p104/r8.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p104/r8.claim: One view calls the lordly detached servants who imitate their Master and acquire His qualities, attending neither to the cosmos nor to its momentary effacement.
SULAMI:v1p104/r8.anchor: وقال بعضهم : ﴿ كونوا ربانيين ﴾ أي : عبيدا منقطعين يقتدون بالسيد ويتخلقون بأخلاقه لا يلاحظون الكون بأسره

SULAMI:v1p104/r9.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p104/r9.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p104/r9.claim: Another view says the true lordly forget self, time, state, qualities, and provision through God's qualities, while the divine attributes are related to the essence and the essence possesses them.
SULAMI:v1p104/r9.anchor: وقال بعضهم : الرباني بحقه من نسي نفسه في نسيانه ، ونسي أوقاته بأوقاته ، ونسي حاله وصفاته وأرزاقه بصفاته

BIQAI-FULL:v2p117/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p117/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p117/r1.claim: Because people who conceal truth also lie about God and therefore about prophets, their fabrication implies that a prophet called people to worship the person falsely attributed with God's law.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p117/r1.anchor: لأنهم لا علم لهم بقول الله سبحانه وتعالى إلا بواسطة الأنبياء عليهم السلام

BIQAI-FULL:v2p117/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p117/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p117/r2.claim: After establishing attributes of Jesus that exclude divinity, the passage now comprehensively denies that Jesus or any human like him called people to worship him, which by itself refutes their claim.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p117/r2.anchor: من صفات عيسى عليه الصلاة والسلام المقتضية لنفي الإلهية عنه ما لا يخفى على ذي لب

BIQAI-FULL:v2p117/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p117/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p117/r3.claim: The denial applies to every person who shares Jesus's description, including Ezra and others, rather than addressing Jesus alone.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p117/r3.anchor: شرع يبين أنهم كاذبون فيما يدعونه في عيسى عليه الصلاة والسلام

BIQAI-FULL:v2p118/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p118/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p118/r1.claim: The phrase ma kāna means such a thing was neither valid nor conceivable in any way.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p118/r1.anchor: أي صح ولا تصور بوجه من الوجوه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p118/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p118/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p118/r2.claim: Bashar covers any human at all, including Jesus, Ezra, and others.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p118/r2.anchor: من البشر كائنا من كان من عيسى وعزير عليهما الصلاة والسلام وغيرهما

BIQAI-FULL:v2p118/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p118/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p118/r3.claim: Al-ḥukm is wisdom that equips one to judge: knowledge supported by action and action perfected by knowledge; its root denotes soundly putting each thing in its proper place.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p118/r3.anchor: الحكمة المهيئة للحكم , وهي العلم المؤيد بالعمل والعمل المتقن بالعلم

BIQAI-FULL:v2p118/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p118/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p118/r4.claim: Prophethood is God's report that grants the highest elevation, by which He appoints a person to call people to worship Him alone and abandon rivals.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p118/r4.anchor: وهي الخبر من الله سبحانه وتعالى المقتضي لأتم الرفعة

BIQAI-FULL:v2p118/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p118/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p118/r5.claim: It is irrational for a human endowed with prophecy and wisdom to claim divinity: human qualities, especially changing complexion that shows contingent states, each independently rule out such a claim.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p118/r5.anchor: لا سيما تغير بشرته الدالة على انفعالاته - مستقلة بالإبعاد عن هذه الدعوى

BIQAI-FULL:v2p118/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p118/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p118/r6.claim: A prophet's call to worship himself has no support in reason or revelation and contradicts the wisdom with which he is invested, so it is certainly excluded.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p118/r6.anchor: فلم يبق لهم مستند , لا من جهة عقل ولا من طريق نقل

BIQAI-FULL:v2p118/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p118/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p118/r7.claim: Rather, such a person tells people to be rabbānī: follow the Lord's way, combining complete knowledge with action; the added alif and nūn signal intense adherence and firmly rooted divine knowledge.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p118/r7.anchor: تابعين طريق الرب منسوبين إليه بكمال العلم المزين بالعمل

BIQAI-FULL:v2p118/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p118/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p118/r8.claim: A rabbānī is strongly attached to God's religion and obedience.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p118/r8.anchor: فإن الرباني هو الشديد التمسك بدين الله سبحانه وتعالى وطاعته

BIQAI-FULL:v2p118/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p118/r9.speaker: محمد بن الحنفية
BIQAI-FULL:v2p118/r9.claim: Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya said of Ibn Abbas after his death, He has died, the rabbānī of this community.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p118/r9.anchor: قال محمد بن الحنفية عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنها لما مات : مات رباني هذه الأمة

BIQAI-FULL:v2p118/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p118/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p118/r10.claim: Being knowledgeable in the Book, teaching it, and studying it lead to knowledge whose benefit is action, exhortation to good, and watchfulness toward the Creator.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p118/r10.anchor: فإن فائدة الدرس العلم , وفائدة العلم العمل

TUSTARI:3:79/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:3:79/r1.speaker: محمد بن سوار
TUSTARI:3:79/r1.claim: Muhammad ibn Sawwar defines a rabbani as one who chooses no one over his Lord; the term derives from lordship.
TUSTARI:3:79/r1.anchor: قال محمد بن سوار: الرباني الذي لا يختار على ربه أحدا سواه، وهو اسم مشتق من الربوبية

TUSTARI:3:79/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:3:79/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:3:79/r2.claim: Sahl defines rabbani scholars as those at a rank of knowledge about knowledge, and says they are attributed to the Lord because they know from His knowledge.
TUSTARI:3:79/r2.anchor: وقال سهل: الربانيون هم العالمون في الدرجة من العلم بالعلم

TUSTARI:3:79/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:3:79/r3.speaker: محمد بن الحنفية
TUSTARI:3:79/r3.claim: When Ibn Abbas died, Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya said that the rabbani of this community had died that day.
TUSTARI:3:79/r3.anchor: كما قال محمد بن الحنفية، لما مات عبدالله بن عباس رضي الله عنهما: لقد مات هذا اليوم رباني هذه الأمة

TUSTARI:3:79/r4.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:3:79/r4.speaker: author
TUSTARI:3:79/r4.claim: A person is called an informer because God taught him; anyone whose report agrees with the Book and Sunna is an informer in this sense.
TUSTARI:3:79/r4.anchor: وكل من أنبأك بخبر موافق للكتاب والسنة فهو منبئ

TUSTARI:3:79/r5.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:3:79/r5.speaker: author
TUSTARI:3:79/r5.claim: Scholars are classified as rabbani, nurani, and essential, the last having no intermediary between them and God and retaining a remnant from Him.
TUSTARI:3:79/r5.anchor: والعلماء ثلاث: رباني ونوراني وذاتي بلا واسطة بينه وبين الله تعالى فيه بقية من الله

TUSTARI:3:79/r6.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:3:79/r6.speaker: عمر بن واصل
TUSTARI:3:79/r6.claim: Umar ibn Wasel says rabbani scholars are a gathered body of learned people.
TUSTARI:3:79/r6.anchor: وقال عمر بن واصل: الربانيون هم المجموعون من العلماء

TUSTARI:3:79/r7.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:3:79/r7.speaker: علي
TUSTARI:3:79/r7.claim: Ali classifies people as a rabbani scholar, a learner on the path of salvation, or ignorant rabble who follow every caller.
TUSTARI:3:79/r7.anchor: كما قال علي رضي الله عنه: الناس ثلاثة: عالم رباني، ومتعلم على سبيل نجاة، وهمج رعاع أتباع كل ناعق

DURR-FULL:v2p249/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p249/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v2p249/r6.claim: When Abu Rafi al-Qurazi and a Christian Najran leader asked whether Muhammad wanted them to worship him like Christians worship Jesus, the Prophet rejected worshipping or commanding worship of anyone besides God; these verses were revealed in that context.
DURR-FULL:v2p249/r6.anchor: قال رسول اللله صلى الله عليه وسلم: معاذ الله أن نعبد غير الله أو نأمر بعبادة غيره ما بذلك بعثني ولا بذلك أمرني

DURR-FULL:v2p250/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p250/r1.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v2p250/r1.claim: Some Jews made people serve them instead of God by distorting scripture, then commanded what God had not revealed.
DURR-FULL:v2p250/r1.anchor: عن ابن جريج قال: كان ناس من يهود يتعبدون الناس من دون ربهم بتحريفهم كتاب الله عن موضعه

DURR-FULL:v2p250/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p250/r2.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v2p250/r2.claim: A man asked whether they should prostrate when greeting the Prophet; he forbade it, directing them to honor him and give each right its due, since none should be prostrated to besides God; the passage was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v2p250/r2.anchor: عن الحسن قال: بلغني أن رجلا قال: يا رسول الله نسلم عليك كما يسلم بعضنا على بعض أفلا نسجد لك قال: لا

DURR-FULL:v2p250/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p250/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p250/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Sa'id ibn Jubayr, glosses rabbaniyyin as jurists and teachers.
DURR-FULL:v2p250/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس في قوله {ربانيين} قال: فقهاء معلمين

DURR-FULL:v2p250/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p250/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p250/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Ikrima, says rabbaniyyin are forbearing, learned, and wise.
DURR-FULL:v2p250/r4.anchor: من طريق عكرمة عن ابن عباس في قوله {ربانيين} قال: حلماء علماء حكماء

DURR-FULL:v2p250/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p250/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p250/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas, through al-Dahhak, defines rabbaniyyin as learned jurists.
DURR-FULL:v2p250/r5.anchor: عن طريق الضحاك عن ابن عباس {ربانيين} قال: علماء فقهاء

DURR-FULL:v2p250/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p250/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p250/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas, through al-Awfi, defines rabbaniyyin as wise jurists.
DURR-FULL:v2p250/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس {ربانيين} قال: حكماء فقهاء

DURR-FULL:v2p250/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p250/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v2p250/r7.claim: Ibn Masud glosses rabbaniyyin as wise scholars.
DURR-FULL:v2p250/r7.anchor: عن ابن مسعود {ربانيين} قال: حكماء علماء

DURR-FULL:v2p250/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p250/r8.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v2p250/r8.claim: Mujahid calls rabbaniyyin jurists and scholars, above the ahbar.
DURR-FULL:v2p250/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد قال الربانيون الفقهاء العلماء وهم فوق الأحبار

DURR-FULL:v2p250/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p250/r9.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v2p250/r9.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says rabbaniyyin are wise and God-fearing.
DURR-FULL:v2p250/r9.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير {ربانيين} قال: حكماء أتقياء

DURR-FULL:v2p250/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p250/r10.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v2p250/r10.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies rabbaniyyin as governing authorities who nurture and oversee people, while ahbar are scholars; he cites the prohibition on rabbaniyyin and ahbar failing to forbid wrongdoing.
DURR-FULL:v2p250/r10.anchor: عن ابن زيد قال الربانيون الذين يربون الناس ولاة هذا الأمر يلونهم وقرأ (لولا ينهاهم الربانيون والأحبار)

DURR-FULL:v2p250/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p250/r11.speaker: الضحاك
