DURR-FULL:v2p250/r11.claim: Al-Dahhak says everyone who learns the Quran must become a jurist.
DURR-FULL:v2p250/r11.anchor: عن الضحاك في قوله {كونوا ربانيين بما كنتم تعلمون الكتاب} قال: حق على كل من تعلم القرآن أن يكون فقيها

DURR-FULL:v2p250/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p250/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p250/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to have recited the phrase with the form ta'lamun.
DURR-FULL:v2p250/r12.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه كان يقرأ {بما كنتم تعلمون}

DURR-FULL:v2p251/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p251/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v2p251/r1.claim: Mujahid recited tu'allimuna with a light form and accusative ta; Ibn Uyayna explains that they did not teach it until they had learned it.
DURR-FULL:v2p251/r1.anchor: أنه قرأ {بما كنتم تعلمون الكتاب} خفيفة بنصب التاء قال ابن عيينة: ما علموه حتى علموه

DURR-FULL:v2p251/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p251/r2.speaker: أبو بكر
DURR-FULL:v2p251/r2.claim: Abu Bakr reports that Asim recited tu'allimuna with a doubled form, nominative ta, and kasra on lam.
DURR-FULL:v2p251/r2.anchor: عن أبي بكر قال: كان عاصم يقرؤها {بما كنتم تعلمون الكتاب} مثقلة برفع التاء وكسر اللام

DURR-FULL:v2p251/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p251/r3.speaker: أبو بكر
DURR-FULL:v2p251/r3.claim: Abu Bakr glosses what they teach as the Quran and what they study as jurisprudence.
DURR-FULL:v2p251/r3.anchor: قال: القرآن {وبما كنتم تدرسون} قال: الفقه

DURR-FULL:v2p251/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p251/r4.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v2p251/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak says no man or woman, free or enslaved, is excused from learning as much Quran as possible; becoming rabbani means becoming a jurist and scholar.
DURR-FULL:v2p251/r4.anchor: عن الضحاك قال: لا يعذر أحد حر ولا عبد ولا رجل ولا امرأة لا يتعلم من القرآن جهده ما بلغ منه

DURR-FULL:v2p251/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p251/r5.speaker: أبو رزين
DURR-FULL:v2p251/r5.claim: Abu Razin says studying means mutually reviewing jurisprudence, as they discussed it together.
DURR-FULL:v2p251/r5.anchor: عن أبي رزين في قوله {وبما كنتم تدرسون} قال: مذاكرة الفقه كانوا يتذاكرون الفقه كما نتذاكره نحن

AKHFASH:v1p224/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p224/r3.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p224/r3.claim: In ثم يقول للناس, يقول is coordinated with أن يؤتيه الله under ما كان لبشر; ثم is a conjunction particle.
AKHFASH:v1p224/r3.anchor: قال تعالى {ثم يقول للناس} نصب على {ما كان لبشر أن يؤتيه الله} {ثم يقول للناس} لأن "ثم" من حروف العطف.

IBNABIHATIM:v2p690#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p690#2/r1.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v2p690#2/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan says no believer could be given scripture, judgment, and prophethood and then tell people to worship him instead of God.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p690#2/r1.anchor: سالت الحسن عن قوله : ما كان لبشر ان يؤتيه الله الكتاب والحكم والنبوة قال : ما كان لمؤمن ان يفعل ذلك .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p690#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p690#2/r2.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNABIHATIM:v2p690#2/r2.claim: Ibn Jurayj explains the statement as meaning that God would not give a prophet scripture and then have him do this.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p690#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن جريج في قوله : ما ان لبشر ان يؤتيه الله الكتاب يقول : ما كان لنبي ان يؤتيه الله الكتاب .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p690#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p690#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p690#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses judgment as knowledge.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p690#2/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس قال : الحكم : العلم .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p690#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p690#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v2p690#2/r4.claim: Mujāhid glosses judgment as intelligence or sound understanding.

IBNABIHATIM:v2p690#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p690#2/r5.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNABIHATIM:v2p690#2/r5.claim: Ibn Jurayj explains “then he says to the people” as commanding them contrary to what God revealed to him in scripture.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p690#2/r5.anchor: عن ابن جريج في قوله : ثم يقول للناس ثم يامر الناس بغير ما انزل الله عليه في كتابه .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p690#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p690#2/r6.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v2p690#2/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan says no believer would command people to take him as a lord instead of God; he adds that the people used to worship one another.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p690#2/r6.anchor: سالت الحسن عن قوله : ما كان لبشر ان يوتيه الله الكتاب والحكم والنبوة ثم يقول للناس

IBNABIHATIM:v2p690#2/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p690#2/r7.speaker: الربيع
IBNABIHATIM:v2p690#2/r7.claim: Al-Rabīʿ explains the phrase as a person commanding God's servants to take him as a lord instead of God.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p690#2/r7.anchor: عن الربيع قوله : ثم يقول للناس كونوا عبادا لي من دون الله يقول : يامر عباد الله ان يتخذوه ربا من دون الله .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p690#2/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p690#2/r8.speaker: ابن جريح
IBNABIHATIM:v2p690#2/r8.claim: Ibn Jurayj says some Jews worshipped people who led them astray by altering scripture away from what God had revealed.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p690#2/r8.anchor: عن ابن جريح في قوله : كونوا عبادا لي من دون الله قال : كان ناس من اليهود يعبدون الناس دون ردهم بتحريفهم كتاب الله

IBNABIHATIM:v2p691/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p691/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p691/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas defines the rabbaniyyun as jurists who teach.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p691/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، عن ابن عباس في هذه الاية : كونوا ربانيين قال : هم الفقهاء المعلمون

IBNABIHATIM:v2p691/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p691/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p691/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Ikrima, calls the rabbaniyyun patient, learned, and wise.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p691/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة ، عن ابن عباس كونوا ربانيين قال : حلماء علماء حكماء

IBNABIHATIM:v2p691/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p691/r3.speaker: أبو رزين
IBNABIHATIM:v2p691/r3.claim: Abu Razin is also reported to define them as learned and patient.

IBNABIHATIM:v2p691/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p691/r4.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v2p691/r4.claim: Al-Hasan says the rabbaniyyun are people devoted to worship and fearing God.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p691/r4.anchor: سالت الحسن عن قوله : ولكن كونوا ربانيين يقول : كونوا اهل عبادة ، واهل تقوى لله

IBNABIHATIM:v2p691/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p691/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p691/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak reports Ibn Abbas defining them as learned jurists; the author names several authorities who agree.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p691/r5.anchor: عن الضحاك ، عن ابن عباس قوله : ربانيين بما كنتم تعلمون الكتاب وبما كنتم تدرسون قال : العلماء الفقهاء

IBNABIHATIM:v2p691/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p691/r6.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v2p691/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak says anyone who recites the Qur’an must become a jurist.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p691/r6.anchor: سمعت الضحاك يقول في قوله : كونوا ربانيين بما كنتم تعلمون الكتاب وبما كنتم تدرسون قال : حق على من قرا القران ان يكون فقيها

IBNABIHATIM:v2p691/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p691/r7.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v2p691/r7.claim: Mujahid reads the clause as teaching what one has fully learned until one can teach it.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p691/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد بما كنتم تعلمون حقيقة ما علموه حتى علموا

IBNABIHATIM:v2p691/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p691/r8.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v2p691/r8.claim: Al-Dahhak says neither free person nor slave is excused from striving to learn as much Qur’an as possible.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p691/r8.anchor: عن الضحاك قال : لا يعذر رجل حر ولا عبد لا يتعلم جهده من القران فابلغ فيه

IBNABIHATIM:v2p691/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p691/r9.speaker: سفيان بن عيينه
IBNABIHATIM:v2p691/r9.claim: Sufyan ibn Uyayna says the phrase means: teach, teach, and keep teaching.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p691/r9.anchor: قال سفيان بن عيينه قال : من قراها بما كنتم تعلمون الكتاب قال : يقول علموا وعلموا ثم علموا

IBNABIHATIM:v2p692/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p692/r1.speaker: وكيع
IBNABIHATIM:v2p692/r1.claim: Waki says the Book in the verse is the Qur’an.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p692/r1.anchor: وكيعا يقول في هذه الاية : سمعنا بما كنتم تعلمون الكتاب قال : القران

IBNABIHATIM:v2p692/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p692/r2.speaker: أبو رزين
IBNABIHATIM:v2p692/r2.claim: Abu Razin explains studying the Book as mutual study of jurisprudence, as do Talha ibn Musarrif, al-Thawri, and Waki.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p692/r2.anchor: عن أبي رزين وبما كنتم تدرسون قال : مذاكرة الفقه كانوا يتذاكرون الفقه

IBNABIHATIM:v2p692/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p692/r3.speaker: طلحة بن مصرف ، وسفيان الثوري ، ووكيع
IBNABIHATIM:v2p692/r3.claim: The author reports these authorities interpreting studying as the study of jurisprudence.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p692/r3.anchor: وروى عن طلحة بن مصرف ، وسفيان الثوري ، ووكيع قالوا : دراية الفقه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p293#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p293#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p293#2/r1.claim: The construction denies that any person is entitled to make the forbidden statement; its lam marks entitlement, and negating the verbal noun intensifies the denial of the act itself.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p293#2/r1.anchor: نفي لاستحقاق أحد لذلك القول واللام فيه للاستحقاق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p293#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p293#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p293#2/r2.claim: The meaning is that no human has a right to tell people to worship him; the form is comparable to God's statement that one may not hunger in Paradise.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p293#2/r2.anchor: فمعنى الآية : ليس قول { كونوا عبادا لي } حقا لبشر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p293#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p293#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p293#2/r3.claim: The entitlement construction is the source of the emphatic lam of denial, as in the verse saying God would not punish them; that pattern emphatically disowns the act as incompatible with the subject's nature.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p293#2/r3.anchor: وهذه اللام هي أصل لام الجحود التي في نحو { وما كان الله ليعذبهم }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p293#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p293#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p293#2/r4.claim: Although the surface negates God's granting scripture, judgment, and prophethood, its actual focus is that an endowed person would tell people to worship him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p293#2/r4.anchor: مصب النفي هو المعطوف من قوله : { ثم يقول للناس كونوا عبادا لي }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p293#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p293#2/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p293#2/r5.claim: Ibn Atiyya says عباد is a plural of عبد without derogation, whereas عبيد carries a sense of abasement or servitude.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p293#2/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عطية : ( الذي استقريت في لفظ العباد أنه جمع عبد لا يقصد معه التحقير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p293#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p293#2/r6.speaker: ابن عطية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p293#2/r6.claim: Ibn Atiyya notes that Arab Christians in al-Hira were called العباد, while عبيد appears in degrading phrases such as slaves of the stick and the line attributed here to Hamza b. al-Muttalib.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p293#2/r6.anchor: وسمت العرب طوائف من العرب سكنوا الحيرة ودخلوا تحت حكم كسرى بالعباد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p293#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p293#2/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p293#2/r7.claim: Ibn Atiyya uses God's denial of injustice to the عبيد as a compassionate reassurance, and God's address to sinful servants as consolation through the obedient form العباد.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p293#2/r7.anchor: ومنه قول الله تعالى : { وما ربك بظلام للعبيد } ( فصلت : 46 ) ؛ لأنه مكان تشفيق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p294/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p294/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p294/r1.claim: The qualifier apart from God stigmatizes the demand to worship the speaker: servitude cannot be divided, so Christians who make Jesus lord and God's son have abandoned God's worship despite claiming both allegiances.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p294/r1.anchor: لأن حقيقة العبودية لا تقبل التجزئة لمعبودين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p294/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p294/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p294/r2.claim: Be godly means be affiliated with the Lord, God, an affiliation that implies special attachment; the intended sense is to be sincere to God alone.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p294/r2.anchor: أي ولكن يقول كونوا ربانيين أي كونوا منسوبين للرب ، وهو الله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p294/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p294/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p294/r3.claim: Rabbani is an irregular relational form from Lord, like lihyani for someone with a large beard and sha'rani for someone with much hair.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p294/r3.anchor: والرباني نسبة إلى الرب على غير قياس كما يقال اللحياني لعظيم اللحية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r1.claim: Knowledge of scripture should keep its possessors from associating partners in worship, since the purpose of knowledge is action.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r1.anchor: أي لأن علمكم الكتاب من شأنه أن يصدكم عن إشراك العبادة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r2.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r2.claim: The majority read تعلمون with an ungeminated form meaning you know or learn the scripture.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r2.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : بما كنتم تعلمون بفتح المثناة الفوقية وسكون العين وفتح اللام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r3.speaker: ابن عامر، وحمزة، وعاصم، والكسائي، وخلف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r3.claim: Ibn Amir, Hamza, Asim, al-Kisa'i, and Khalaf read تعلّمون with a geminated form meaning you teach the scripture.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r3.anchor: وقرأه ابن عامر ، وحمزة ، وعاصم ، والكسائي ، وخلف : بضم ففتح فلامم مشددة مكسورة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r4.claim: Study means repeated reading: the root evokes the repeated action that wears or affects something, as wind erases a trace and a book is read slowly for memory or reflection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r4.anchor: { وتدرسون } معناه تقرؤون أي قراءة بإعادة وتكرير : لأن مادة درس في كلام العرب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r5.claim: A Prophetic report transmitted by al-Tirmidhi says that people who recite and study God's book together receive serenity; the contrast makes study more specific than recitation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r5.anchor: رواه الترمذي فعطف التدارس على القراءة فعلم أن الدراسة أخص من القراءة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r6.claim: A report says the Prophet went with companions to the Jewish place of study, recited the Quran to them, and invited them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r6.anchor: إن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم خرج في طائفة من أصحابه حتى أتى مدراس اليهود

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r7.claim: Because the verb study presupposes mastery of its object, studying scripture is a figurative way to say understanding and mastering it; this explains its coordination with learning it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r7.anchor: ومادة درس تستلزم التمكن من المفعول فلذلك صار درس الكتاب مجازا في فهمه وإتقانه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r8.claim: The verb is from the nasara pattern; its common verbal noun is dars, while reading yields the regular dars and the activity noun dirasah, by analogy with crafts such as writing and trade.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r8.anchor: وفعله من باب نصر ، ومصدره في غالب معانيه الدرس ، ومصدر درس بمعنى قرأ يجيء على الأصل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r9.claim: The clause and he does not command you shifts from third-person reference to direct address.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r9.anchor: وفي قوله : { ولا يأمركم } التفات من الغيبة إلى الخطاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r10.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r10.claim: The majority read يأمركم in the nominative as a fresh clause; restarting negation after لكن makes the sense clear: a human neither tells people to worship him nor commands angel worship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r10.anchor: الجمهور ( يأمركم ) بالرفع على ابتداء الكلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r11.speaker: ابن عامر، وحمزة ويعقوب، وخلف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r11.claim: Ibn Amir, Hamza, Ya'qub, and Khalaf read يأمركم in the accusative, coordinating it with أن يقول; لا is emphatic, since making it governed by أن would reverse the intended meaning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r11.anchor: وقرأه ابن عامر ، وحمزة ويعقوب ، وخلف : بالنصب عطفا على أن يقول ولا زائدة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r12.speaker: الدوري عن أبي عمرو
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r12.claim: Al-Duri from Abu Amr gives the reading with a weakened, near-silent damma.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p295/r12.anchor: وقرأه الدوري عن أبي عمرو باختلاس الضمة إلى السكون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461/r1.claim: Mā kāna li-bashar means ‘for anyone’; bashar is a collective noun usable for one or many and has no singular form of its own.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى: ما كان لبشر معناه لأحد من الناس، والبشر اسم جنس يقع للكثير والواحد ولا مفرد له من لفظه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461/r2.claim: The wording is a complete negation whose force depends on context; unlike logical impossibilities, this verse categorically excludes God giving prophethood to liars and pretenders.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461/r2.anchor: وأما آيتنا هذه فإن النفي على الكمال لأنا نقطع أن الله تعالى لا يؤتي النبوة للكذبة والمدعين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461/r3.speaker: أبو بكر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461/r3.claim: Abū Bakr illustrates this absolute negative form by saying that it was not fitting for Ibn Abī Quḥāfa to pray before the Messenger.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461/r3.anchor: كقول أبي بكر رضي الله عنه: ما كان لابن أبي قحافة أن يصلي بين يدي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461/r4.claim: He contrasts this with other ‘it was not for’ constructions, including one expressing impossibility and one about bringing forth a tree.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461/r4.anchor: كقوله تعالى: وما كان لنفس أن تموت إلا بإذن الله [آل عمران: 145] وقوله تعالى: ما كان لكم أن تنبتوا شجرها [النحل: 60]

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461/r5.claim: Al-kitāb is a generic noun, and al-ḥukm means wisdom, as in the Prophetic saying that poetry contains wisdom.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461/r5.anchor: والكتاب في هذه الآية اسم جنس، والحكم بمعنى الحكمة، ومنه قول النبي عليه السلام: إن من الشعر لحكما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461/r6.claim: Thumma heightens the gravity of the offense: the person would say this after a delay following such divine favor.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461/r6.anchor: وثم في قوله تعالى: ثم يقول معطية تعظيم الذنب في القول، بعد مهلة من هذا الإنعام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461/r7.claim: ʿIbādan is one plural of ʿabd, alongside ʿabīd and ʿabdā.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461/r7.anchor: وقوله عبادا هو جمع عبد، ومن جموعه عبيد وعبدى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461/r8.speaker: بعض اللغويين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461/r8.claim: Some linguists treat the plurals ʿibād, ʿabīd, and ʿabdā as synonymous.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461/r8.anchor: قال بعض اللغويين، هذه الجموع بمعنى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461/r9.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461/r9.claim: One view reserves ʿibād for God’s servants and uses ʿabīd or ʿabdā for human slaves; another restricts ʿabdā to descendants of slaves as an emphatic form.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461/r9.anchor: وقال قوم، العباد لله، والعبيد والعبدى للبشر، وقال قوم: العبدى، إنما تقال في العبيد بني العبيد، وكأنه بناء مبالغة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya’s usage survey finds ʿibād in elevated contexts of obedience without belittlement, citing several Qur’anic examples.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461/r10.anchor: والذي استقريت في لفظة العباد، أنه جمع عبد متى سيقت اللفظة في مضمار الترفيع والدلالة على الطاعة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461#2/r1.speaker: امرؤ القيس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461#2/r1.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays’s line addresses people as ʿabīd, illustrating the term’s belittling force.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461#2/r1.anchor: قولا لدودان عبيد العصى ... ما غركم بالأسد الباسل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461#2/r2.speaker: حمزة بن عبد المطلب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461#2/r2.claim: Ḥamza ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib likewise uses ʿabīd as an insult.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461#2/r2.anchor: ومنه قول حمزة بن عبد المطلب: وهل أنتم إلا عبيد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461#2/r3.claim: The Qur’anic phrase ‘not unjust to the slaves’ occurs in a context of compassion and their limited ability to defend themselves; ʿibād signals obedience, unlike the belittling ʿabīd.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461#2/r3.anchor: ومنه قول الله تعالى: وما ربك بظلام للعبيد [فصلت: 46] لأنه مكان تشفيق وإعلام بقلة انتصارهم ومقدرتهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461#2/r4.claim: He sees this lexical distinction as one of the remarkable ways Qur’anic eloquence follows sound Arabic usage.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461#2/r4.anchor: فهذا النوع من النظر يسلك به سبل العجائب في ميزة فصاحة القرآن العزيز على الطريقة العربية السليمة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461#2/r5.claim: ‘Be servants to me apart from God’ means worship me and make me a deity.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461#2/r5.anchor: ومعنى قوله: كونوا عبادا لي من دون الله اعبدوني واجعلوني إلها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461#2/r6.speaker: النقاش وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461#2/r6.claim: Al-Naqqāsh and others say the verse refers to Jesus and rebuts Christians who called him God and claimed his worship rested on his command.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461#2/r6.anchor: فقال النقاش وغيره: الإشارة إلى عيسى عليه السلام، والآية رادة على النصارى الذين قالوا: عيسى إله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس والربيع وابن جريج وجماعة من المفسرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Rabīʿ, Ibn Jurayj, and other exegetes say the verse refers instead to Muḥammad.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461#2/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والربيع وابن جريج وجماعة من المفسرين: بل الإشارة إلى محمد عليه السلام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461#2/r8.speaker: أبو رافع القرظي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461#2/r8.claim: Abū Rāfiʿ al-Quraẓī accused Muḥammad of wanting the Jews and Najran delegation to worship him as Christians worship Jesus; a Najran leader asked if that was his demand, and the Prophet denied it and said he had not been commanded or invited to it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461#2/r8.anchor: أن أبا رافع القرظي، قال للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، حين اجتمعت الأحبار من يهود والوفد من نصارى نجران: يا محمد إنما تريد أن نعبدك ونتخذك إلها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461#2/r9.speaker: بعض العلماء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461#2/r9.claim: Some scholars say the rabbis tried to pin this claim on Muḥammad after he recited 3:31, whose meaning was to follow him in obeying God; they distorted it by interpretation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461#2/r9.anchor: أرادت الأحبار أن تلزم هذا القول محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم، لما تلا عليهم قل إن كنتم تحبون الله فاتبعوني [آل عمران: 31] وإنما معنى الآية، فاتبعوني فيما أدعوكم إليه من طاعة الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461#2/r10.claim: This accusation is another example of twisting Scripture with the tongue.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p461#2/r10.anchor: فحرفوها بتأويلهم، وهذا من نوع ليهم الكتاب بألسنتهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r1.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r1.claim: One etymology derives rabbānī from rabb: a person who knows what God taught, obeys Him, and teaches people what He commanded; the extra alif and nūn intensify the relation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r1.anchor: فقال قوم: هو منسوب إلى الرب من حيث هو العالم ما علمه، العامل بطاعته، المعلم للناس ما أمر به، وزيدت الألف والنون مبالغة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r2.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r2.claim: Another derives rabbānī from rabbān, a teacher, scholar, and manager of people’s affairs, from the verb meaning to reform and nurture, with a nūn like ghaḍbān and ʿaṭshān.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r2.anchor: وقال قوم الرباني منسوب إلى الربان وهو معلم الناس، وعالمهم السائس لأمرهم، مأخوذ من رب يرب إذا أصلح وربى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r3.speaker: أبو رزين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r3.claim: Abū Razīn defines a rabbānī as a wise scholar.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r3.anchor: فقال أبو رزين: الرباني: الحكيم العالم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r4.claim: Mujāhid defines a rabbānī as a jurist.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r5.speaker: قتادة وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r5.claim: Qatāda and others define a rabbānī as learned and forbearing.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r5.anchor: وقال قتادة وغيره: الرباني العالم الحليم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās defines a rabbānī as wise and learned in jurisprudence.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: هو الحكيم الفقيه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r7.speaker: الضحاك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r7.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk defines a rabbānī as a jurist and scholar.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r8.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r8.claim: Ibn Zayd says a rabbānī is a ruler who tends and reforms people, encompassing governors, rabbis, and scholars.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r8.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: الرباني والي الأمر، يرب الناس أي يصلحهم، فالربانيون الولاة والأحبار والعلماء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r9.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r9.claim: Mujāhid places the rabbānī above the ḥabr: beyond knowledge, he combines jurisprudence with political judgment and care for subjects’ religious and worldly welfare.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r9.anchor: وقال مجاهد: الرباني فوق الحبر لأن الحبر هو العالم والرباني هو الذي جمع إلى العلم والفقه البصر بالسياسة والتدبير والقيام بأمور الرعية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r10.speaker: البخاري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r10.claim: Al-Bukhārī’s definition is one who teaches people small matters of knowledge before large ones.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r10.anchor: وفي البخاري: الرباني الذي يربي الناس بصغار العلم قبل كباره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya sums up a rabbānī as learned in God and the law, and sound in judging words and actions undertaken among people.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r11.anchor: فجملة ما يقال في الرباني إنه العالم بالرب والشرع المصيب في التقدير من الأقوال والأفعال التي يحاولها في الناس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r12.claim: Bimā kuntum means ‘because you know and study’: mā is a verbal noun, since no relative pronoun can be supplied with a valid antecedent after both verbs already have their complements.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r12.anchor: وقوله بما كنتم معناه: بسبب كونكم عالمين دارسين، فما مصدرية، ولا يجوز أن تكون موصولة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r13.claim: On the light reading, taʿlamūn means ‘know’ and takes one object; on the doubled reading it is causative, with ‘people’ understood as a second object.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r13.anchor: وتعلمون بمعنى تعرفون، فهي متعدية إلى مفعول واحد، وقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r14.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r14.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Nāfiʿ, and Abū ʿAmr read taʿlamūn with a still ʿayn and light lām.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r14.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو: «تعلمون» بسكون العين، وتخفيف اللام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r15.speaker: عاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r15.claim: ʿĀṣim, Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī read the verb with doubling, meaning ‘teach people the Book’ with an omitted second object.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p462/r15.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي «تعلمون» مثقلا، بضم التاء وكسر اللام، وهذا على تعدية الفعل بالتضعيف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p463/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p463/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p463/r1.claim: The light and doubled readings are close: the light reading is supported by light tadrusūn and by knowledge as the cause of becoming rabbānī, while the doubled reading is praised as fuller because teaching entails knowledge but knowledge does not entail teaching; Ibn ʿAṭiyya ultimately prefers the light reading.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p463/r1.anchor: ورجحت الأخرى بأن التعليم يتضمن العلم، والعلم لا يتضمن التعليم، فتجيء قراءة التثقيل أبلغ في المدح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p463/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p463/r2.speaker: مجاهد والحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p463/r2.claim: Mujāhid and al-Ḥasan read taʿallamūn with fatḥa on tāʾ and ʿayn and a doubled lām.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p463/r2.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد والحسن «تعلمون» بفتح التاء والعين، وشد اللام المفتوحة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p463/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p463/r3.speaker: جمهور الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p463/r3.claim: Most readers pronounce tadrusūn with ḍamma on rāʾ, from d-r-s: persistently reading and repeating a book.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p463/r3.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس، «تدرسون» بضم الراء، من درس إذا أدمن قراءة الكتاب وكرره

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p463/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p463/r4.speaker: أبو حيوة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p463/r4.claim: Abū Ḥaywa reads tadrusūn with kasra on rāʾ, following an alternative imperfect form of darasa.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p463/r4.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة «تدرسون» بكسر الراء، وهذا على أنه يقال في مضارع درس، يدرس ويدرس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p463/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p463/r5.speaker: أبو حيوة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p463/r5.claim: Another report from Abū Ḥaywa has ḍamma on tāʾ, a doubled rāʾ, and the sense ‘you teach others.’
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p463/r5.anchor: وروي عن أبي حيوة، أنه قرأ «تدرسون» بضم التاء، وكسر الراء وشدها، بمعنى تدرسون غيركم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413/r1.claim: One occasion report says Jewish and Christian leaders asked Muhammad whether he wanted them to take him as a lord; he denied that was his mission, and the verse was revealed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413/r1.anchor: أحدها أن قوما من رؤساء اليهود والنصارى قالوا يا محمد أتريد أن نتخذك ربا فقال معاذالله ما بذلك بعثني فنزلت هذه الآية قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413/r2.speaker: الحسن البصري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413/r2.claim: Hasan al-Basri reports that a man asked whether they should prostrate to the Prophet; he said no one should be prostrated to besides God, and the verse followed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413/r2.anchor: قاله الحسن البصري والثالث أنها نزلت في نصارى نجران حيث عبدوا عيسى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413/r3.speaker: الضحاك، مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413/r3.claim: Dahhak and Muqatil say the verse was revealed about the Christians of Najran who worshipped Jesus.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413/r3.anchor: والثالث أنها نزلت في نصارى نجران حيث عبدوا عيسى قاله الضحاك و مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413/r4.speaker: ابن عباس، عطاء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413/r4.claim: One view identifies the human addressed as Muhammad and the Book as the Quran.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413/r4.anchor: أحدهما محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم والكتاب القرآن قاله ابن عباس وعطاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413/r5.speaker: الضحاك، مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413/r5.claim: Another view identifies the human as Jesus and the Book as the Gospel.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413/r5.anchor: والثاني عيسى والكتاب الإنجيل قاله الضحاك و مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413/r6.claim: Al-hukm means jurisprudence and knowledge, according to Qatada and others.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413/r6.anchor: والحكم الفقه والعلم قاله قتادة في آخرين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413/r7.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413/r7.claim: Al-Zajjaj says prophethood cannot be combined with telling people to worship oneself, because God does not choose liars.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413/r7.anchor: لا يجتمع لرجل نبوة والقول للناس كونوا عبادا لي من دون الله لأن الله لا يصطفي الكذبة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413#2/r1.claim: In “but be,” the verb “he says to them” is omitted because the context makes it clear.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413#2/r1.anchor: أي ولكن يقول لهم كونوا فحذف القول لدلالة الكلام عليه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413#2/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413#2/r2.claim: Ali defines rabbaniyyun as people who nourish others with wisdom and train them in it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413#2/r2.anchor: فروي عن علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه أنه قال هم الذين يغذون الناس بالحكمة ويربونهم عليها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس، ابن جبير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ibn Jubayr say rabbaniyyun are jurists who teach.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413#2/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وابن جبير هم الفقهاء المعلمون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413#2/r4.speaker: قتادة، عطاء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413#2/r4.claim: Qatada and Ata define them as jurists, scholars, and wise people.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413#2/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة وعطاء هم الفقهاء العلماء الحكماء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413#2/r5.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413#2/r5.claim: Ibn Qutayba gives rabbani as the singular and defines the group as scholar-teachers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413#2/r5.anchor: قاله ابن قتيبة واحدهم رباني وهم العلماء المعلمون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413#2/r6.speaker: أبو عبيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413#2/r6.claim: Abu Ubayd suspects the word is Hebrew or Syriac rather than Arabic, since Abu Ubayda claimed Arabs did not know it and scholars did.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413#2/r6.anchor: وقال أبو عبيد أحسب الكلمة ليست بعربية إنما هي عبرانية أو سريانية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413#2/r7.speaker: رجل عالم بالكتب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413#2/r7.claim: A learned man in the scriptures defines rabbaniyyun as scholars of the lawful and unlawful, commands and prohibitions.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413#2/r7.anchor: وسمعت رجلا عالما بالكتب يقول هم العلماء بالحلال والحرام والأمر والنهي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413#2/r8.speaker: ابن الأنباري عن بعض اللغويين
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413#2/r8.claim: A linguistic explanation derives rabbani from “Lord”: knowledge serves obedience to God, and the ending intensifies the association, like lahyani for a large beard.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p413#2/r8.anchor: وحكى ابن الأنباري عن بعض اللغويين الرباني منسوب إلى الرب لأن العلم مما يطاع الله به

MAJAZ:v1p97/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p97/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p97/r1.claim: The people addressed had not recognized rabbānī scholars as such.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p65#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p65#2/r1.speaker: أبو رافع القرظي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p65#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas's report says that at a gathering of Jewish and Christian scholars from Najran, Abu Rafi asked whether Muhammad wanted them to worship him as Christians worship Jesus; a Najran Christian leader echoed the question.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p65#2/r1.anchor: قال أبو رافع القرظي، حين اجتمعت الأحبار من اليهود والنصارى من أهل نجران، عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p65#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p65#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p65#2/r2.claim: A person granted scripture, judgment, and prophethood cannot tell people to worship him alongside God; if even a prophet cannot do so, no other person can all the more.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p65#2/r2.anchor: ما ينبغي لبشر آتاه الله الكتاب والحكم والنبوة أن يقول للناس: اعبدوني من دون الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p65#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p65#2/r3.speaker: الحسن البصري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p65#2/r3.claim: Hasan says it is unsuitable for a believer to command people to worship him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p65#2/r3.anchor: قال الحسن البصري: لا ينبغي هذا لمؤمن أن يأمر الناس بعبادته.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p65#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p65#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p65#2/r4.claim: The People of the Book served their rabbis and monks as lords by obeying them, as in the verse about taking religious authorities as lords.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p65#2/r4.anchor: قال: وذلك أن القوم كان يعبد بعضهم بعضا -يعني أهل الكتاب- كانوا يتعبدون لأحبارهم ورهبانهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p65#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p65#2/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p65#2/r5.claim: When Adi ibn Hatim objected that people had not worshipped their religious authorities, the Prophet replied that they did so by obeying their declarations that the forbidden was lawful and the lawful forbidden.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p65#2/r5.anchor: وفي المسند، والترمذي -كما سيأتي-أن عدي بن حاتم قال: يا رسول الله، ما عبدوهم. قال: "بلى، إنهم أحلوا لهم الحرام

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p65#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p65#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p65#2/r6.claim: Misguided religious authorities are condemned, unlike messengers and practicing scholars who teach and prohibit only what God commanded; the messengers faithfully delivered their trust and counseled creation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p65#2/r6.anchor: فالجهلة من الأحبار والرهبان ومشايخ الضلال يدخلون في هذا الذم والتوبيخ، بخلاف الرسل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p66/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p66/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p66/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, Abu Razin, and others explain rabbaniyyun as people who are wise, learned, and forbearing.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p66/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس وأبو رزين وغير واحد، أي: حكماء علماء حلماء.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p66/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p66/r2.speaker: الحسن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p66/r2.claim: Hasan and others interpret rabbaniyyun as jurists; this is also reported from Ibn Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatada, Ata al-Khurasani, Atiyya al-Awfi, and al-Rabi ibn Anas.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p66/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن وغير واحد: فقهاء، وكذا روي عن ابن عباس، وسعيد بن جبير، وقتادة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p66/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p66/r3.speaker: الحسن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p66/r3.claim: Hasan also explains rabbaniyyun as people devoted to worship and piety.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p66/r3.anchor: وعن الحسن أيضا: يعني أهل عبادة وأهل تقوى.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p66/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p66/r4.speaker: الضحاك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p66/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak says anyone who learns the Quran must become learned in its jurisprudence, understanding its meaning.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p66/r4.anchor: وقال الضحاك في قوله: {بما كنتم تعلمون الكتاب وبما كنتم تدرسون} حق على من تعلم القرآن أن يكون فقيها:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p66/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p66/r5.speaker: قراءة بالتشديد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p66/r5.claim: An alternative reading vocalizes taallamuna with a doubled letter, meaning that they teach the Book.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p66/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p66/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p66/r6.claim: The phrase about studying the Book means memorizing its wording.

NAHHAS:v1p389/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p389/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p389/r11.claim: أن governs يؤتيه and ثم يقول is coordinated with it; the accusative is the stronger reading.
NAHHAS:v1p389/r11.anchor: نصب بأن ( ثم يقول ) عطف عليه وروى محبوب عن أبي عمرو ثم يقول بالرفع والنصب أجود

NAHHAS:v1p389/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p389/r12.speaker: أبو عمرو
NAHHAS:v1p389/r12.claim: Maḥbūb transmits Abū ʿAmr’s رفع reading ثم يقول, while al-Naḥḥās prefers the accusative.
NAHHAS:v1p389/r12.anchor: وروى محبوب عن أبي عمرو ثم يقول بالرفع والنصب أجود

NAHHAS:v1p389/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p389/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p389/r13.claim: ولكن كونوا ربانيين omits a verb of saying, understood as ولكن يقول; ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān instead supplies ليقل.
NAHHAS:v1p389/r13.anchor: ( ولكن كونوا ربانيين ) حذف القول والتقدير ولكن يقول وقال علي بن سليمان المعنى ولكن ليقل

NAHHAS:v1p389/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p389/r14.speaker: ابن كيسان
NAHHAS:v1p389/r14.claim: Ibn Kaysān says the wāw is the coordinating particle and لكن adds confirmation.
NAHHAS:v1p389/r14.anchor: قال ابن كيسان الواو هي العاطفة ولكن للتحقيق

NAHHAS:v1p389/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p389/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p389/r15.claim: Abū ʿAmr and Medinans read تعلمون; Ibn ʿAbbās and Kūfans read it with taḍamma and doubled lām, and Mujāhid reads it with fatḥa and doubled lām, meaning “you learn.”
NAHHAS:v1p389/r15.anchor: ( بما كنتم تعلمون الكتاب ) قراءة أبي عمرو وأهل المدينة وقرأ ابن عباس وأهل الكوفة ( تعلمون ) بضم التاء وتشديد اللام

NAHHAS:v1p389/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p389/r16.speaker: مجاهد
NAHHAS:v1p389/r16.claim: Mujāhid’s فتح form with a doubled lām means “you learn.”
NAHHAS:v1p389/r16.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد تعلمون ) بفتح التاء وتشديد اللام أي تتعلمون

NAHHAS:v1p389/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p389/r17.speaker: شعبة
NAHHAS:v1p389/r17.claim: Shuʿba transmits from ʿĀṣim, Zur, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd the gloss حكماء علماء for ربانيين.
NAHHAS:v1p389/r17.anchor: لأن شعبة روى عن عاصم عن زر عن عبد الله بن مسعود ولكن كونوا ربانيين قال حكماء علماء

NAHHAS:v1p389/r18.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p389/r18.speaker: الضحاك
NAHHAS:v1p389/r18.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk urges everyone to exert effort in memorizing the Qurʾān, citing this verse’s call to be learned scholars through studying and teaching the Book.
NAHHAS:v1p389/r18.anchor: قال الضحاك لا ينبغي لأحد أن يدع حفظ القرآن جهده فإن الله جل وعز يقول ولكن كونوا ربانيين

NAHHAS:v1p389/r19.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p389/r19.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p389/r19.claim: Al-Naḥḥās finds “be wise scholars by your teaching” unlikely and favors the sense “be wise scholars by your knowledge.”
NAHHAS:v1p389/r19.anchor: فقيل يبعد أن يقال كونوا حكماء علماء بتعليمكم والحسن كونوا حكماء علماء بعلمكم

JISHUMI:v2p1221/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1221/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1221/r1.claim: The apparent reading makes then he says accusative, treating it as coordinated with the preceding construction; Abu Amr reads it nominative as a new sentence.
JISHUMI:v2p1221/r1.anchor: القراءة الظاهرة ثم يقول بنصب اللام، وروي عن أبي عمرو برفعها، أما النصب فعلى تقدير لا تجتمع النبوة

JISHUMI:v2p1221/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1221/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1221/r2.claim: Most named readers use the light form of teach, while the remaining readers use the doubled form, which he says conveys more benefit by combining knowledge and teaching.
JISHUMI:v2p1221/r2.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ونافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو ويعقوب تعلمون بالتخفيف من علم يعلم

JISHUMI:v2p1221/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1221/r3.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v2p1221/r3.claim: Al-Hasan reads the verb with an open tāʾ and ʿayn and a doubled lām, meaning they learn.
JISHUMI:v2p1221/r3.anchor: وروي عن الحسن بفتح التاء والعين وتشديد اللام في معنى يتعلمون

JISHUMI:v2p1221/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1221/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1221/r4.claim: Abu Haywa reads يدرسون with a damma on yāʾ and no doubling; Saʿid b. Jubayr reads تدرسون as teaching, while the common reading is the light form from درس.
JISHUMI:v2p1221/r4.anchor: وعن أبي حيوة يدرسون بضم الياء والتخفيف من درس يدرس، وعن سعيد بن جبير تدرسون من التدريس

JISHUMI:v2p1221/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1221/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1221/r6.claim: Bashar derives from skin and names the visibly embodied human; like خلق, it can denote either one person or a group.
JISHUMI:v2p1221/r6.anchor: البشر من البشرة سمي بذلك لظهوره

JISHUMI:v2p1221/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1221/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1221/r7.claim: One derivation of rabbānī is from rabbān, a manager who orders and reforms people's affairs; a scholar is called rabbānī because knowledge lets him govern affairs.
JISHUMI:v2p1221/r7.anchor: وهو من يرب أمر الناس بتقديره لهم وإصلاحه إياه رب أمره يربه

JISHUMI:v2p1221/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1221/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1221/r8.claim: A second derivation links rabbānī to the Lord and His religious knowledge, expressed through a relational form like Najrānī or Liḥyānī.
JISHUMI:v2p1221/r8.anchor: وهو علم الدين الذي أمر به إلا أنه عبر بالإضافة

JISHUMI:v2p1221/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1221/r9.speaker: بعض قريش
JISHUMI:v2p1221/r9.claim: A Qurayshi saying illustrates rabbānī as managing or raising someone: the speaker would rather be managed by a Qurayshi than a man from Hawazin.
JISHUMI:v2p1221/r9.anchor: قول بعض قريش: لأن يربني رجل من قريش

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p404#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p404#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p404#3/r1.claim: The opening denies the belief that Jesus should be worshipped.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p404#3/r1.anchor: ما كان لبشر ﴾ تكذيب لمن اعتقد عبادة عيسى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p404#3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p404#3/r2.speaker: أبو رافع القرظي والسيد
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p404#3/r2.claim: Abu Rafiʿ al-Qurazi and al-Sayyid of Najran asked if the Prophet wanted them to worship him; he said God forbid, since he was sent neither to worship another nor to command that.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p404#3/r2.anchor: إن أبا رافع القرظي والسيد من نصارى نجران قالا لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أتريد أن نعبدك ونتخذك ربا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p404#3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p404#3/r3.speaker: النبي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p404#3/r3.claim: A man asked if people should prostrate to the Prophet when greeting him; the Prophet forbade prostrating to anyone besides God and told them to honor the Prophet and give each person their due.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p404#3/r3.anchor: قال لا ينبغي ان يسجد لأحد من دون الله ولكن اكرموا نبيكم واعرفوا الحق لأهله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p404#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p404#3/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p404#3/r4.claim: Here الحكم means wisdom, identified with the Sunnah.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p404#3/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p404#3/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p404#3/r5.claim: Rabbānī is formed from Rabb with the suffix alif-nūn and describes someone strongly attached to God's religion and obedience.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p404#3/r5.anchor: والرباني منسوب إلى الرب بزيادة الألف والنون كما يقال رقباني ولحياني وهو الشديد التمسك بدين الله وطاعته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p404#3/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p404#3/r6.speaker: محمد ابن الحنفية
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p404#3/r6.claim: When Ibn ʿAbbas died, Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya said that the rabbānī of this community had died that day.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p404#3/r6.anchor: وعن محمد ابن الحنفية أنه قال حين مات ابن عباس اليوم مات رباني هذه الأمة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p404#3/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p404#3/r7.speaker: الحسن
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p404#3/r7.claim: Al-Hasan defines rabbānī people as learned jurists.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p404#3/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p404#3/r8.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p404#3/r8.claim: Another view defines them as learned people who teach; the saying describes the rabbānī lawgiver as learned, practicing, and teaching.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p404#3/r8.anchor: وقيل علماء معلمين وكانوا يقولون الشارع الرباني العالم العامل المعلم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p405/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p405/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p405/r1.claim: Being knowledgeable and studying the scripture should produce firm obedience; learning unused in practice is futile, like a beautiful tree that gives no fruit.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p405/r1.anchor: أوجب أن تكون الربانية التي هي قوة التمسك بطاعة الله مسببة عن العلم والدراسة وكفى به دليلا على خيبة سعي من جهد نفسه وكد روحه في جمع العلم ثم لم يجعله ذريعة إلى العمل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p405/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p405/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p405/r2.claim: The reading تعلمون is explained either as teaching or as learning.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p405/r2.anchor: وقرىء ( تعلمون ) من التعليم ( وتعلمون ) من التعلم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p405/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p405/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p405/r3.claim: تدرسون means reciting or reading; it also has readings derived from teaching, from a verb synonymous with studying, or from studying oneself.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p405/r3.anchor: تقرؤن وقرىء ( تدرسون ) من التدريس وتدرسون على ان أدرس بمعنى درس كاكرم وكرم وانزل ونزل ( وتدرسون ) من التدرس

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p405/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p405/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p405/r4.claim: Both the light reading and the teaching reading may mean teaching the scripture to people, as in Qur'an 17:106.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p405/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون معناه ومعنى تدرسون بالتخفيف تدرسونه على الناس كقوله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p405/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p405/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p405/r5.claim: Those who learn and teach without acting sever their connection with God, since only those who adhere to His obedience are related to Him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p405/r5.anchor: وفيه ان من علم ودرس العلم ولم يعمل به فليس من الله في شيء وان السبب بينه وبين ربه منقطع حيث لم يثبت النسبة اليه الا للمتمسكين بطاعته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p406/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p406/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p406/r1.claim: A subjunctive reading of ولا يأمركم is coordinated with the preceding construction; in أيأمركم, the subject may be the human or God, and the interrogative hamza expresses denial.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p406/r1.anchor: ﴿ ولا يأمركم ﴾ و ﴿ أيأمركم ﴾ لبشر وقيل الله والهمزة في أيأمركم للإنكار

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p406/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p406/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p406/r2.claim: The phrase after you became Muslims proves the addressees were already Muslims, the people who had asked permission to prostrate to the Prophet.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p406/r2.anchor: ﴿ بعد إذ أنتم مسلمون ﴾ دليل على أن المخاطبين كانوا مسلمين وهم الذين استأذنوه ان يسجدوا له

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p406/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p406/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p406/r3.claim: The passage continues with the beginning of verses 81–83 of Al ʿImran.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p405/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p405/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p405/r1.claim: The verse was revealed after some Jews asked the Prophet whether he summoned them to worship him as Christians worship the Messiah.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p405/r1.anchor: أن قوما من اليهود قالوا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : أتدعونا إلى عبادتك كما دعا المسيح النصارى , فنزلت هذه الآية .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p405/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p405/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p405/r2.claim: Rabbaniyyun are jurists and learned scholars.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p405/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p405/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p405/r3.claim: Rabbaniyyun are wise and Godfearing people.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p405/r3.anchor: حكماء أتقياء , وهو قول سعيد بن جبير .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p405/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p405/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p405/r4.claim: Rabbaniyyun are governors who administer people's affairs.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p405/r4.anchor: أنهم الولاة الذين يربون أمور الناس , وهذا قول ابن زيد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p405/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p405/r5.speaker: الشاعر
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p405/r5.claim: One proposed root connects rabbani to managing people's affairs; the poet's words about “my stewardship” and “she governed me” support that derivation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p405/r5.anchor: وكنت امرءا أفضت إليك ربابتي … وقبلك ربتني - فضعت - ربوب

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p405/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p405/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p405/r6.claim: On this derivation, a scholar is called rabbani because knowledge enables him to govern affairs.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p405/r6.anchor: فسمي العالم ربانيا لأنه بالعلم يدبر الأمور .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p405/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p405/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p405/r7.claim: Another etymology derives rabbani from “the Lord's scholar,” meaning religious knowledge; its possessor is named for knowledge commanded by the Lord.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p405/r7.anchor: أنه مضاف إلى عالم الرب , وهو علم الدين , فقيل لصاحب العلم الذي أمر به الرب رباني .

MUJAHID:v1p129#4/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p129#4/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p129#4/r1.claim: Rabbānī people are jurists, learned scholars, and wise men.
MUJAHID:v1p129#4/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ ولكن كونوا ربانيين ﴾ قال كونوا فقهاء علماء حكماء

MUQATIL:3:79-81/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:3:79-81/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:3:79-81/r1.claim: The human in the verse is Jesus son of Mary.
MUQATIL:3:79-81/r1.anchor: يعنى عيسى ابن مريم صلى الله عليه وسلم

MUQATIL:3:79-81/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:3:79-81/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:3:79-81/r2.claim: The Book means the Torah and Gospel, and judgment means understanding.
MUQATIL:3:79-81/r2.anchor: يعنى التوراة والإنجيل، { والحكم } ، يعنى الفهم

MUQATIL:3:79-81/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:3:79-81/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:3:79-81/r3.claim: The people addressed are the Children of Israel.
MUQATIL:3:79-81/r3.anchor: ثم يقول للناس } ، يعنى بنى إسرائيل

MUQATIL:3:79-81/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:3:79-81/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:3:79-81/r4.claim: Rather than worship him, Jesus tells them to be devoted to God, teaching and studying the Torah and Gospel.
MUQATIL:3:79-81/r4.anchor: كونوا ربانيين } ، يعنى متعبدين لله عزوجل، { بما كنتم تعلمون الكتاب } ، يعنى التوراة والإنجيل

NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r1.claim: The verse denies that a human granted scripture, judgment, and prophethood could call people to worship him instead of God; this rebuts belief in Jesus's worship.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r1.anchor: تكذيب لمن اعتقد عبادة عيسى عليه السلام

NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r2.speaker: رجل
NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r2.claim: An unnamed man asked whether people should prostrate to the Prophet as they greeted one another; the Prophet forbade prostration to anyone besides God and urged honoring him and giving each person his due.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r2.anchor: قال رجل يا رسول الله نسلم عليك كما يسلم بعضنا على بعض أفلا نسجد لك قال لا ينبغي أن يسجد لأحد من دون الله ولكن أكرموا نبيكم واعرفوا الحق لأهله

NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r3.claim: Al-ḥukm is glossed as wisdom, meaning either the Sunna or the ability to judge decisively.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r3.anchor: والحكمة وهي السنة أو فصل القضاء

NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r4.claim: The clause then he says is syntactically coordinated with God granting the person these gifts.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r4.anchor: ﴿ والنبوة ثم يقول ﴾ عطف على يؤتيه

NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r5.claim: Rabbānī derives from rabb with the added alif and nūn and describes someone firmly attached to God's religion and obedience.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r5.anchor: والرباني منسوب إلى الرب بزيادة الألف والنون وهو شديد التمسك بدين الله وطاعته

NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r6.speaker: ابن الحنفية
NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r6.claim: At Ibn ʿAbbās's death, Ibn al-Ḥanafiyya called him the rabbānī of this community.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r6.anchor: قال ابن الحنفية مات رباني هذه الأمة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r7.speaker: الحسن
NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r7.claim: Al-Ḥasan explains rabbānī as learned scholars and jurists.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r8.claim: Another explanation calls rabbānīs scholars who teach; the source also defines a rabbānī as a learned person who acts on knowledge.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r8.anchor: وعن الحسن ربانيين علماء فقهاء وقيل علماء معلمين

NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r9.claim: Kufan and Syrian readers have the lightened form of taʿlīm, understood as teaching others.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r9.anchor: ﴿ بما كنتم تعلمون الكتاب ﴾ كوفى وشامى أى غيركم غيرهم بالتخفيف

NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r10.claim: The verb tadrusūn means that they read or study the scripture.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r11.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r11.claim: Firm adherence to obedience follows from being learned and studying; gathering knowledge without turning it into action is a failed effort.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r11.anchor: بسبب كونكم عالمين وبسبب كونكم دارسين للعلم كانت الربانية التي هي قوة التمسك بطاعة الله مسببة عن العلم والدارسة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r12.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r12.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r12.claim: He compares knowledge without practice to a beautiful tree admired for its appearance but yielding no fruit.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r12.anchor: فكان كمن عرس من شجرة حسناء تؤنقه بمظهرها ولا تنفق بثمرها

NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r13.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r13.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r13.claim: An alternative construes tadrusūn as teaching the scripture to people, as in the Qur'anic phrase about reciting it to them; Ibn Jubayr's reading supports the teaching derivation.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p162#3/r13.anchor: وقيل معنى تدرسون تدرسونه على الناس كقوله لتقرأه على الناس فيكون معناه معنى تدرسون من التدريس كقراءة ابن جبير

QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r1.claim: Mā kāna here means it is not fitting or proper, as in the cited verses.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r2.speaker: الضحاك والسدي
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r2.claim: Bashar can denote either one person or a group because it functions like a verbal noun; al-Ḍaḥḥāk and al-Suddī identify Jesus as the person intended here.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r2.anchor: والبشر يقع للواحد والجمع لأنه بمنزلة المصدر والمراد به هنا عيسى في قول الضحاك والسدي

QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r3.claim: Al-kitāb means the Qur'an; al-ḥukm means knowledge and understanding, or alternatively legal judgments.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r3.anchor: والكتاب: القرآن. والحكم: العلم والفهم. وقيل أيضا: الأحكام.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r4.claim: God does not choose liars for prophethood; if a prophet claimed people should worship him, God would strip away the signs and marks of prophethood.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r4.anchor: أي إن الله لا يصطفي لنبوته الكذبة، ولو فعل ذلك بشر لسلبه الله آيات النبوة وعلاماتها.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r5.claim: Thumma yaqul is coordinated with the granting of scripture, judgment, and prophethood: a prophet cannot receive prophethood and then tell people to worship him instead of God.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r5.anchor: ونصب «ثم يقول» على الاشتراك بين «أن يؤتيه» وبين «يقول» أي لا يجتمع لنبي إتيان النبوة

QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r6.claim: A prophet may instead tell people to become rabbāniyyūn.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r6.anchor: أي ولكن جائز أن يكون النبي يقول لهم كونوا ربانيين.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r7.claim: One account says this verse was revealed about the Christians of Najran; another says the whole sūra through 3:121 was occasioned by them, with Jews included because they acted with the same denial and obstinacy.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r7.anchor:
وهذه الآية قيل إنها نزلت في نصارى نجران. وكذلك روي أن السورة كلها إلى قوله:
وإذ غدوت من أهلك
[آل عمران: 121] كان سبب نزولها نصارى نجران ولكن مزج معهم اليهود لأنهم فعلوا من الجحد والعناد فعلهم.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains rabbānī as one who teaches people elementary knowledge before advanced knowledge, modeling God's gentle ordering of affairs.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r8.anchor: والرباني الذي يربي الناس بصغار العلم قبل كباره وكأنه يقتدي بالرب سبحانه في تيسير الأمور روي معناه عن ابن عباس

QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r9.claim: One derivation makes rabbānī come from rabbī with alif and nūn for intensification, like laḥyānī, jamānī, and raqbanī.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r9.anchor: قال بعضهم: كان في الأصل ربي فأدخلت الألف والنون للمبالغة كما يقال للعظيم اللحية لحياني

QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r10.speaker: المبرد
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r10.claim: Al-Mubarrad derives rabbāniyyūn from rabban, managers and reformers of people's affairs; the alif and nūn intensify the sense, then the yāʾ marks affiliation.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r11.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r11.claim: An unnamed poet uses rabbānī in a verse alongside ḥadīth and aḥbār as linguistic evidence for the form.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r11.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
لو كنت مرتهنا في الجو أنزلني
منه الحديث ورباني أحباري

QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r12.claim: A rabbānī is a scholar of God's religion who acts on his knowledge; without acting on it, a person is not truly a scholar.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r12.anchor: فمعنى الرباني العالم بدين الرب الذي يعمل بعلمه لأنه إذا لم يعمل بعلمه فليس بعالم

QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r13.speaker: أبو رزين
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r13.claim: Abū Razīn defines rabbānī as a learned, wise person.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r13.anchor: وقال أبو رزين: الرباني هو العالم الحكيم.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r14.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r14.claim: Ibn Masʿūd's gloss is that rabbāniyyūn are wise scholars.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r14.anchor: وروى شعبة عن عاصم عن زر عن عبد الله بن مسعود «ولكن كونوا ربانيين» قال: حكماء علماء.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r15.speaker: ابن جبير
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r15.claim: Ibn Jubayr defines rabbāniyyūn as wise and God-fearing.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r16.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r16.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says no one should neglect memorizing as much of the Qur'an as possible, citing the command to be rabbānī.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r16.anchor: وقال الضحاك: لا ينبغى لأحد أن يدع حفظ القرآن جهده فإن الله تعالى يقول: { ولكن كونوا ربانيين }.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r17.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r17.claim: Ibn Zayd says rabbāniyyūn are rulers, while aḥbār are scholars.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r17.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: الربانيون الولاة، والأحبار العلماء.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r18.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r18.claim: Mujāhid says rabbāniyyūn rank above the aḥbār; al-Naḥḥās calls this a good view because rabbānī combines scholarship with political insight and management of people's affairs.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r18.anchor: وقال مجاهد: الربانيون فوق الأحبار. قال النحاس: وهو قول حسن لأن الأحبار هم العلماء.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r19.speaker: العالم
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r19.claim: Abū ʿUbayda quotes a scholar defining rabbānī as one who knows lawful and forbidden matters, commands and prohibitions, and the community's reports, past and future.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r19.anchor: الرباني العالم بالحلال والحرام والأمر والنهي

QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r20.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r20.speaker: محمد بن الحنفية
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r20.claim: When Ibn ʿAbbās died, Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyya said that the rabbānī of this community had died that day.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79/r20.anchor: وقال محمد بن الحنفية يوم مات ابن عباس: اليوم مات رباني هذه الأمة.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:79#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79#2/r1.claim: A report transmitted by Ibn ʿAbbās says every believing person, man or woman, free or enslaved, owes God the duty to learn the Qur'an and understand religion; the Prophet then recited this verse.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79#2/r1.anchor:
وروي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:
" ما من مؤمن ذكر ولا أنثى حر ولا مملوك إلا ولله عز وجل عليه حق

QURTUBI-FULL:3:79#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79#2/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو وأهل المدينة
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79#2/r2.claim: Abū ʿAmr and the Medinese read taʿlamūn lightly, from knowledge; Abū Ḥātim prefers this form, and Abū ʿAmr cites the following tadrusūn rather than tudarrisūn as support.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79#2/r2.anchor: قرأه أبو عمرو وأهل المدينة بالتخفيف من العلم. واختار هذه القراءة أبو حاتم.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:79#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79#2/r3.speaker: ابن عامر وأهل الكوفة
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir and the Kufans read tuʿallimūn with gemination, from teaching; Abū ʿUbayd prefers it because it encompasses both teaching and learning.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وأهل الكوفة «تعلمون» بالتشديد من التعليم واختارها أبو عبيد.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:79#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79#2/r4.speaker: مكي
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79#2/r4.claim: Makkī says the geminated reading is more emphatic and praiseworthy: every teacher knows, but not every person who knows teaches; the light form expresses knowledge alone.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79#2/r4.anchor: قال مكي: التشديد أبلغ لأن كل معلم عالم بمعنى يعلم وليس كل من علم شيئا معلما

QURTUBI-FULL:3:79#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79#2/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79#2/r5.claim: Those favoring the light reading appeal to Ibn Masʿūd's gloss wise scholars, arguing it would be redundant to command people to be jurists, wise, and learned through teaching.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79#2/r5.anchor: احتج من رجح قراءة التخفيف بقول ابن مسعود «كونوا ربانيين» قال: حكماء علماء

QURTUBI-FULL:3:79#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79#2/r6.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79#2/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan explains the command as becoming wise scholars through one's knowledge.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79#2/r6.anchor: قال الحسن، كونوا حكماء علماء بعلمكم.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:79#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79#2/r7.speaker: أبو حيوة
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79#2/r7.claim: Abū Ḥaywa reads tadrusūn from adrasa, with the form meaning to study or teach.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة «تدرسون» من أدرس يدرس.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:79#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79#2/r8.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79#2/r8.claim: Mujāhid reads taʿallamūn with an open tāʾ and geminated lām, meaning that you learn.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:79#2/r8.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد «تعلمون» بفتح التاء وتشديد اللام، أي تتعلمون.

SAMIN-DURR:3:79/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:79/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:79/r1.claim: أن يؤتيه is the subject of كان and لبشر its predicate; ثم يقول is coordinated with يؤتيه, a necessary link because otherwise the denial would be false of the many people given scripture, judgment, and prophecy.
SAMIN-DURR:3:79/r1.anchor: وهذا العطف لازم من حيث المعنى، إذ لو سكت عنه لم يصح المعنى

SAMIN-DURR:3:79/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:79/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:79/r2.claim: Some coordinated complements are semantically obligatory, just like certain circumstantial and object phrases; this coordination is one such case.
SAMIN-DURR:3:79/r2.anchor: وهذا كما يقولون في بعض الأحوال والمفاعيل: إنها لازمة

SAMIN-DURR:3:79/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:79/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:79/r3.claim: The Arabic formula ما كان لزيد أن يفعل has two contextual senses: denial that the act can or does occur, or rejection that it is appropriate.
SAMIN-DURR:3:79/r3.anchor: وهو على قسمين: قسم يكون النفي فيه من جهة الفعل، ويعبر عنه بالنفي التام

SAMIN-DURR:3:79/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:79/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:79/r4.claim: Here the denial is complete: God does not grant scripture, judgment, and prophecy to someone who says such a blasphemous thing; 27:60 and 3:145 illustrate the form.
SAMIN-DURR:3:79/r4.anchor: لأن الله تعالى لا يعطي الكتاب والحكم والنبوة لمن يقول هذه المقالة الشنعاء

SAMIN-DURR:3:79/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:79/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:79/r5.claim: The second type denies propriety rather than occurrence, as in Abu Bakr’s statement that it was not fitting for Ibn Abi Quhafa to lead prayer before the Messenger; context distinguishes the types.
SAMIN-DURR:3:79/r5.anchor: وقسم يكون النفي فيه على سبيل الانتقاء كقول أبي بكر

SAMIN-DURR:3:79/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:79/r6.speaker: الجمهور
SAMIN-DURR:3:79/r6.claim: The common reading has يقول in the accusative, coordinated to يؤتيه.
SAMIN-DURR:3:79/r6.anchor: وقرأ العامة: " يقول " بالنصب نسقا على " يؤتيه "

SAMIN-DURR:3:79/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:79/r7.speaker: ابن كثير
SAMIN-DURR:3:79/r7.claim: In Shibl ibn Abbad’s transmission from Ibn Kathir, يقول is nominative and treated as a detached restart, which the author finds difficult because the preceding coordination is semantically required.
SAMIN-DURR:3:79/r7.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير في رواية شبل بن عباد، وأبو عمرو في رواية محبوب: " يقول " بالرفع

SAMIN-DURR:3:79/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:79/r8.speaker: أبو عمرو
SAMIN-DURR:3:79/r8.claim: Abu Amr likewise has a nominative يقول in Mahbub’s transmission, parsed as a detached restart; the author questions how the sentence can then be complete.
SAMIN-DURR:3:79/r8.anchor: وأبو عمرو في رواية محبوب: " يقول " بالرفع، وخرجوها على القطع والاستئناف

SAMIN-DURR:3:79#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#2/r1.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#2/r1.claim: Ibn Atiyya lists عبيد and عبدى as forms plural in meaning; grammarians disagree whether they are synonymous, whether عباد is reserved for God and عبيد/عبدى for humans, or whether عبدى intensifies servitude.
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#2/r1.anchor: ومن جموعه عبيد وعبدى. قال بعض اللغويين: هذه الجموع كلها بمعنى

SAMIN-DURR:3:79#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#2/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#2/r2.claim: Ibn Atiyya’s usage survey says عباد connotes elevation and obedience without contempt, citing 2:207, 21:26, 39:53, and 5:118; that positive sense explains its use in 39:53.
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#2/r2.anchor: والذي استقريت في لفظ العباد أنه

SAMIN-DURR:3:79#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#2/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#2/r3.claim: Ibn Atiyya says عبيد can be contemptuous, citing Imru al-Qays’s phrase عبيد العصا and Hamza’s وهل أنتم إلا عبيد لأبي; he reads 41:46 likewise as pitying the servants’ limited power.
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#2/r3.anchor: وأما العبيد فيستعمل في تحقيره، ومنه قول امرىء القيس

SAMIN-DURR:3:79#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#2/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#2/r4.claim: Ibn Atiyya says عباد is unsuitable here because it implies obedience, unlike its fitting use in قل يعبادي الذين أسرفوا.
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#2/r4.anchor: ولما كانت لفظة العباد تقتضي الطاعة لم تقع هنا، ولذلك أنس بها في قوله تعالى

SAMIN-DURR:3:79#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#2/r5.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#2/r5.claim: Al-Shaykh says عبيد is certainly a plural, while عبدى is a collective noun with a feminine ending; Ibn Atiyya may mean both are semantic plurals.
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#2/r5.anchor: فأما " عبيد " فالأصح أنه جمع. وقيل: اسم جمع، " وأما عبدى فاسم جمع

SAMIN-DURR:3:79#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#2/r6.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#2/r6.claim: Al-Shaykh rejects Ibn Atiyya’s semantic distribution: عباد is common because فِعال is the regular plural of this pattern, while فَعيل is rare, as Sibawayh notes.
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#2/r6.anchor: وإنما كثر استعمال " عباد " دون " عبيد " لأن فعالا في جمع فعل غير اليائي العين قياسي مطرد

SAMIN-DURR:3:79#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#2/r7.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#2/r7.claim: Al-Shaykh explains عبيد at 41:46 as chosen for rhyme with بعيد and شهيد, and its occurrence at 50:29 for rhyme with وعيد and مزيد.
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#2/r7.anchor: فحسن مجيئه بلفظ العبيد مراعاة هاتين الفاصلتين، ونظير هذا في سورة ق

SAMIN-DURR:3:79#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#2/r8.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#2/r8.claim: Al-Shaykh says عبيد and عباد have the same meaning and argues that the contempt in Imru al-Qays’s line and Hamza’s remark comes from context, not the word.
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#2/r8.anchor: وأما { وما ربك بظلام للعبيد } فحسن مجيئه هنا

SAMIN-DURR:3:79#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#2/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#2/r9.claim: The author says al-Shaykh’s dismissal of Ibn Atiyya’s usage survey is unfounded without a counterexample, and rejects assigning contempt only to context when the word itself is the better source.
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#2/r9.anchor: فحسن مجيئه بلفظ العبيد مراعاة هاتين الفاصلتين

SAMIN-DURR:3:79#2/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#2/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#2/r10.claim: لي modifies عباد, while من دون attaches to عباد through its verbal sense and may be a second adjective or a circumstantial phrase after the noun is specified.

SAMIN-DURR:3:79#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#3/r1.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#3/r1.claim: Al-Shaykh also cites 50:29, where عبيد suits the neighboring rhyme words وعيد and مزيد.
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#3/r1.anchor: لأن قبله: { وقد قدمت إليكم بالوعيد } وبعده: " وتقول: هل من مزيد "

SAMIN-DURR:3:79#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#3/r2.claim: The author rejects the claim that contempt in عبيد is supplied only by context, arguing that lexical wording takes precedence when either word or context could explain it.
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#3/r2.anchor: وأما ادعاؤه أن التحقير مفهوم من السياق دون لفظ عبيد فممنوع

SAMIN-DURR:3:79#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#4/r1.claim: كونوا requires an implied يقول; ربانيون is its plural subject complement.
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#4/r1.anchor: أي: ولكن يقول كونوا، فلا بد من إضمار القول هنا

SAMIN-DURR:3:79#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#4/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#4/r2.claim: One derivation relates رباني to الرب, with extra alif and nūn intensifying the relational adjective; ordinary, non-intensive forms are رقبي، شعري، and لحوي.
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#4/r2.anchor: أحدهما أنه منسوب إلى الرب، والألف والنون فيه زائدتان في النسب دلالة على المبالغة

SAMIN-DURR:3:79#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#4/r3.speaker: سيبويه
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#4/r3.claim: Sibawayh explains the extra letters in رباني as specifying mastery of knowledge of the Lord, analogous to شعراني، لحياني, and رقباني.
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#4/r3.anchor: زادوا ألفا ونونا في الرباني أرادوا تخصيصا بعلم الرب دون غيره من العلوم

SAMIN-DURR:3:79#4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#4/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#4/r4.claim: A second derivation relates رباني to ربّان, a teacher of good who governs people and teaches religion; its ending intensifies the quality as in عطشان and ريان.
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#4/r4.anchor: أنه منسوب إلى ربان والربان هو المعلم للخير ومن يسوس الناس ويعرفهم أمر دينهم

SAMIN-DURR:3:79#4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#4/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#4/r5.claim: On the second derivation the form can be an adjective-based nisba, like أحمري, illustrated by the anonymous verse أطربا وأنت قنسري.
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#4/r5.anchor: وتكون النسبة على هذا في الوصف نحو أحمري، قال

SAMIN-DURR:3:79#4/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#4/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#4/r6.claim: Exegetes gloss كونوا ربانيين as become jurists and learned scholars; after Ibn Abbas died, Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya called him the rabbi of this community.

SAMIN-DURR:3:79#5/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#5/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#5/r1.claim: The باء in بما كنتم is causal: become learned because you used to do the described acts.

SAMIN-DURR:3:79#5/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#5/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#5/r2.claim: The causal باء may attach to كونوا, to ربانيين because it carries verbal meaning, or to an omitted phrase as an adjective of ربانيين; the last analysis is unclear to the author.
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#5/r2.anchor: أحدها: أنه متعلقة بكونوا، كذا ذكره أبو البقاء

SAMIN-DURR:3:79#5/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#5/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#5/r3.claim: ما is a verbal noun particle; reading it as a relative pronoun is strained because it needs an omitted antecedent and fails the shared-governor condition.
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#5/r3.anchor: مصدرية، وظاهر كلام الشيخ أنه يجوز أن تكون غير ذلك

SAMIN-DURR:3:79#5/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#5/r4.speaker: نافع
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#5/r4.claim: Nafi, Ibn Kathir, and Abu Amr read تعلمون from علم يعلم, meaning know or learn; it takes one object.
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#5/r4.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو: " تعلمون " مفتوح حرف المضارعة

SAMIN-DURR:3:79#5/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#5/r5.speaker: باقي السبعة
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#5/r5.claim: The other canonical readers read تُعَلِّمون from the causative form, which takes two objects; the first is omitted as people or students, though no object may be intended if teaching the Book itself is the point.
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#5/r5.anchor: وباقي السبعة بضم حرف المضارعة وفتح العين وتشديد اللام مكسورة، فيتعدى لاثنين

SAMIN-DURR:3:79#5/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#5/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#5/r6.claim: The causative reading intensifies the praise: every teacher is learned, not every learned person teaches, and rabbani suggests teaching others rather than private knowledge alone.
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#5/r6.anchor: وذلك أن كل معلم عالم، وليس كل عالم معلما

SAMIN-DURR:3:79#5/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#5/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#5/r7.claim: Others prefer the simple reading because it avoids an unexpressed object and matches تدرسون; both readings are mass-transmitted, so the author refuses to rank them.
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#5/r7.anchor: والقراءتان متواترتان فلا ينبغي ترجيح إحداهما على الأخرى

SAMIN-DURR:3:79#5/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#5/r8.speaker: الحسن
