SAMIN-DURR:3:79#5/r8.claim: Al-Hasan and Mujahid read تَعَلَّمون from تعلم, originally تتعلمون with one of the two initial tāʾs deleted; the final clause بما كنتم تدرسون follows the same pattern.
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#5/r8.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ومجاهد: " تعلمون " فتح التاء والعين واللام مشددة من " تعلم "

RAZI-FULL:v8p96#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p96#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p96#2/r1.claim: After describing scriptural scholars' distortion, Razi says one altered claim was that Jesus asserted divinity and commanded people to worship him; the verse refutes that charge.
RAZI-FULL:v8p96#2/r1.anchor: اعلم أنه تعالى لما بين أن عادة علماء أهل الكتاب التحريف والتبديل أتبعه بما يدل على أن من جملة ما حرفوه

RAZI-FULL:v8p96#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p96#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v8p96#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse was revealed after Jews called Uzayr God's son and Christians called Christ God's son.
RAZI-FULL:v8p96#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس : لما قالت اليهود عزير ابن الله ، وقالت النصارى : المسيح ابن الله نزلت هذه الآية

RAZI-FULL:v8p96#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p96#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p96#2/r3.claim: An occasion report says Abu Rafi al-Qurazi and the head of the Najran delegation asked whether Muhammad wanted them to worship and take him as lord; he replied that he was sent neither to worship another nor to command other than God's worship.
RAZI-FULL:v8p96#2/r3.anchor: قيل إن أبا رافع القرظي من اليهود ورئيس وفد نجران من النصارى قالا لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : أتريد أن نعبدك ونتخذك ربا

RAZI-FULL:v8p96#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p96#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p96#2/r4.claim: Another occasion report says a man asked whether they might prostrate to the Prophet; he forbade anyone prostrating to another besides God and directed them to honor the Prophet and give each his due.
RAZI-FULL:v8p96#2/r4.anchor: قال رجل يا رسول الله نسلم عليك كما يسلم بعضنا على بعض ، أفلا نسجد لك ؟

RAZI-FULL:v8p96#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p96#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p96#2/r5.claim: Razi says the wording can address Jews who claimed no one reached their excellence: instead of enslaving people, they should direct them to obey God and acknowledge Muhammad's prophethood as his miracles require; 9:31 offers a parallel.
RAZI-FULL:v8p96#2/r5.anchor: إن اليهود لما ادعوا أن أحدا لا ينال من درجات الفضل والمنزلة ما نالوه ، فالله تعالى قال لهم

RAZI-FULL:v8p97/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p97/r1.speaker: الأصم
RAZI-FULL:v8p97/r1.claim: Al-Asamm reads the verse as saying that if prophets wanted to make this claim, the proof would prevent them, as 69:44–45 and 17:74–75 warn of punishment for fabricating revelation or nearly inclining to opponents.
RAZI-FULL:v8p97/r1.anchor: قال الأصم : معناه ، أنهم لو أرادوا أن يقولوا ذلك لمنعهم الدليل عليه قوله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v8p97/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p97/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p97/r2.claim: A second interpretation is that prophets' divinely chosen pure souls, complete knowledge, and purified character are incompatible with claiming divinity; scripture cites God's knowing where to place His message, choosing Israel knowingly, and selecting messengers (6:124; 44:32; 22:75).
RAZI-FULL:v8p97/r2.anchor: أن الأنبياء عليهم الصلاة والسلام موصوفون بصفات لا يحسن مع تلك الصفات ادعاء الإلاهية والربوبية منها أن الله تعالى آتاهم الكتاب والوحي

RAZI-FULL:v8p97/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p97/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p97/r3.claim: A third interpretation is that God grants prophethood only when He knows the recipient will not say this.
RAZI-FULL:v8p97/r3.anchor: أن الله تعالى لا يشرف عبده بالنبوة والرسالة إلا إذا علم منه أنه لا يقول مثل هذا الكلام

RAZI-FULL:v8p97/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p97/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p97/r4.claim: A fourth interpretation is that if a messenger who claims to transmit God's rulings ordered worship of himself, his miracles would cease to prove his truth.
RAZI-FULL:v8p97/r4.anchor: فلو أمرهم بعبادة نفسه فحينئذ تبطل دلالة المعجزة على كونه صادقا

RAZI-FULL:v8p97/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p97/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p97/r5.claim: Razi says the verse denies that a human granted scripture, judgment, and prophethood would make this claim; it does not merely prohibit speech already forbidden to everyone, which would not refute the charge against Jesus.
RAZI-FULL:v8p97/r5.anchor: واعلم أنه ليس المراد من قوله { ما كان لبشر } ذلك أنه يحرم عليه هذا الكلام لأن ذلك محرم على كل الخلق

RAZI-FULL:v8p97/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p97/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p97/r6.claim: The wording instead negates the claim, as 19:35 negates God taking a son and 3:161 negates a prophet committing fraud rather than merely forbidding those acts.
RAZI-FULL:v8p97/r6.anchor: ونظيره قوله تعالى : { ما كان الله * أن يتخذ من ولد } ( مريم : 35 ) على سبيل النفي

RAZI-FULL:v8p97#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p97#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p97#2/r1.claim: The order is apt: the heavenly book is revealed first, the prophet then understands it through judgment (which linguists and exegetes identify as knowledge), and finally conveys it to people through prophethood.
RAZI-FULL:v8p97#2/r1.anchor: لأن الكتاب السماوي ينزل أولا ثم إنه يحصل في عقل النبي فهم ذلك الكتاب وإليه الإشارة بالحكم

RAZI-FULL:v8p97#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p97#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p97#2/r2.claim: The common reading puts the verb after thumma in the subjunctive, indicating that prophethood and telling people to worship the prophet cannot coexist; it is governed by an implied an and coordinated with what came before.
RAZI-FULL:v8p97#2/r2.anchor: القراءة الظاهرة ، ثم يقول بنصب اللام

RAZI-FULL:v8p97#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p97#2/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو
RAZI-FULL:v8p97#2/r3.claim: Abu Amr's reported indicative reading begins a new sentence.
RAZI-FULL:v8p97#2/r3.anchor: وروي عن أبي عمرو برفعها ، أما النصب فعلى تقدير

RAZI-FULL:v8p97#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p97#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v8p97#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says ʿibādan is the Muzayna dialect word for slaves.
RAZI-FULL:v8p97#2/r4.anchor: حكى الواحدي عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أنه قال في قوله تعالى : { كونوا عبادا لى } إنه لغة مزينة

RAZI-FULL:v8p97#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p97#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p97#2/r5.claim: The phrase but become godly has an omitted verb, meaning but he says to them; Arabic permits such ellipsis when context makes it clear, as in 3:106.
RAZI-FULL:v8p97#2/r5.anchor: في هذه الآية إضمار ، والتقدير : ولكن يقول لهم كونوا ربانيين فأضمر القول على حسب مذهب العرب

RAZI-FULL:v8p98/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p98/r1.speaker: سيبويه
RAZI-FULL:v8p98/r1.claim: Sibawayh derives rabbānī from the Lord: it describes one devoted to knowing and obeying God; the added alif and nūn intensify the quality, as in words for abundant hair or a long beard.
RAZI-FULL:v8p98/r1.anchor: قال سيبويه : الرباني المنسوب إلى الرب ، بمعنى كونه عالما به ، ومواظبا على طاعته

RAZI-FULL:v8p98/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p98/r2.speaker: المبرد
RAZI-FULL:v8p98/r2.claim: Al-Mubarrad derives rabbānī from nurturing: a learned person who teaches, reforms, and manages people; alif and nūn intensify the sense before the nisba yāʾ is added.
RAZI-FULL:v8p98/r2.anchor: قال المبرد { الربانيون } أرباب العلم وأحدهم رباني ، وهو الذي يرب العلم ويرب الناس

RAZI-FULL:v8p98/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p98/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
RAZI-FULL:v8p98/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says rabbānīs are the community's rulers and scholars; on this reading the verse calls people to be learned leaders through God's commands and steady obedience.
RAZI-FULL:v8p98/r3.anchor: قال ابن زيد : الرباني . هو الذي يرب الناس ، فالربانيون هم ولاة الأمة والعلماء

RAZI-FULL:v8p98/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p98/r4.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v8p98/r4.claim: Al-Qaffāl suggests a ruler may be called rabbānī because people obey him as they obey the Lord.
RAZI-FULL:v8p98/r4.anchor: قال القفال رحمه الله : ويحتمل أن يكون الوالي سمي ربانيا ، لأنه يطاع كالرب تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v8p98/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p98/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
RAZI-FULL:v8p98/r5.claim: Abū ʿUbayda suspects the word is Hebrew or Syriac rather than Arabic; in either language it denotes someone who learns, acts on the knowledge, and teaches good ways.
RAZI-FULL:v8p98/r5.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة أحسب أن هذه الكلمة ليست بعربية إنما هي عبرانية ، أو سريانية

RAZI-FULL:v8p98#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p98#2/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن كثير وأبو عمرو ونافع
RAZI-FULL:v8p98#2/r1.claim: These readers read the verb as knowing: people become rabbānīs through their own knowledge of Scripture.
RAZI-FULL:v8p98#2/r1.anchor: قراءة عبد الله بن كثير ، وأبي عمرو ، ونافع والثانية : { تعلمون } من التعليم

RAZI-FULL:v8p98#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p98#2/r2.speaker: باقي السبعة
RAZI-FULL:v8p98#2/r2.claim: The other canonical readers read the verb as teaching; al-Rāzī says both readings are sound because the people knew Scripture and taught it to others.
RAZI-FULL:v8p98#2/r2.anchor: وهي قراءة الباقين من السبعة وكلاهما صواب ، لأنهم كانوا يعلمونه في أنفسهم ويعلمونه غيرهم

RAZI-FULL:v8p98#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p98#2/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو
RAZI-FULL:v8p98#2/r3.claim: Abū ʿAmr prefers the ungeminated reading because the following verb is also ungeminated and because the geminated form normally takes two objects, while this clause has one.
RAZI-FULL:v8p98#2/r3.anchor: واحتج أبو عمرو على أن قراءته أرجح بوجهين الأول : أنه قال : { تدرسون } ولم يقل

RAZI-FULL:v8p98#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p98#2/r4.speaker: الذين قرؤا بالتشديد
RAZI-FULL:v8p98#2/r4.claim: Advocates of the geminated reading answer that its second object, such as people or others, is omitted because objects are often left unexpressed.
RAZI-FULL:v8p98#2/r4.anchor: فزعموا أن المفعول الثاني محذوف تقديره : بما كنتم تعلمون الناس الكتاب

RAZI-FULL:v8p98#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p98#2/r5.speaker: الذين قرؤا بالتشديد
RAZI-FULL:v8p98#2/r5.claim: They argue that teaching includes knowledge, whereas knowledge does not necessarily include teaching, so teaching is the fuller sense.
RAZI-FULL:v8p98#2/r5.anchor: أن التعليم يشتمل على العلم ولا ينعكس فكان التعليم أولى

RAZI-FULL:v8p98#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p98#2/r6.speaker: الذين قرؤا بالتشديد
RAZI-FULL:v8p98#2/r6.claim: They also argue that rabbānīs must teach as well as know; the command to Muhammad to call with wisdom supports this, and Murra ibn Sharāḥīl called ʿAlqama one of the teachers of Qur'an.
RAZI-FULL:v8p98#2/r6.anchor: أن الربانيين لا يكتفون بالعلم حتى يضموا إليه التعليم لله تعالى ألا ترى أنه تعالى أمر محمدا

RAZI-FULL:v8p98#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p98#2/r7.speaker: أبو حيوة
RAZI-FULL:v8p98#2/r7.claim: Abū Ḥaywa reads tadrusūn with a damma on tāʾ, a still dāl, and a kasra on rāʾ; Ibn Jinnī says it may derive from studying oneself or another and include teaching others.
RAZI-FULL:v8p98#2/r7.anchor: عن أبي حيوة أنه قرأ { تدرسون } بضم التاء ساكنة الدال مكسورة الراء ، قال ابن جني

RAZI-FULL:v8p98#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p98#2/r8.speaker: ابن جني
RAZI-FULL:v8p98#2/r8.claim: Ibn Jinnī notes that most Arabs use darasa and darasa, from which the verbal noun tadrīs is formed.
RAZI-FULL:v8p98#2/r8.anchor: وأكثر العرب على درس ودرس ، وعليه جاء المصدر على التدريس

RAZI-FULL:v8p98#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p98#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p98#2/r9.claim: In either reading, mā plus the verb is a verbal noun: learning, teaching, and studying Scripture are the grounds for becoming rabbānī.
RAZI-FULL:v8p98#2/r9.anchor: ( ما ) في القراءتين ، هي التي بمعنى المصدر مع الفعل ، والتقدير : كونوا ربانيين بسبب كونكم عالمين

RAZI-FULL:v8p98#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p98#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p98#2/r10.claim: Because rabbānī status is distinct from knowing, teaching, and studying, these activities must be done for God's pleasure and to avoid His punishment, rather than for their own sake.
RAZI-FULL:v8p98#2/r10.anchor: ما ذاك إلا أن يكون بحيث يكون تعلمه لله ، وتعليمه ودراسته لله ، وبالجملة أن يكون الداعي له إلى جميع

RAZI-FULL:v8p98#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p98#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p98#2/r11.claim: A messenger who directs all hearts away from creation toward God cannot redirect people from obeying God to obeying himself; prophets therefore cannot command worship of themselves.
RAZI-FULL:v8p98#2/r11.anchor: الرسول هو الذي يكون منتهى جهده وجده صرف الأرواح والقلوب عن الخلق إلى الحق ، فمثل هذا الإنسان كيف يمكن

RAZI-FULL:v8p99/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p99/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p99/r1.claim: Learning, teaching, and studying make a person rabbānī only when pursued for this purpose; otherwise the work is wasted, like a beautiful tree with useless fruit.
RAZI-FULL:v8p99/r1.anchor: فمن اشتغل بالتعلم والتعليم لا لهذا المقصود ضاع سعيه وخاب عمله وكان مثله مثل من غرس شجرة حسناء

RAZI-FULL:v8p99/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p99/r2.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v8p99/r2.claim: The Prophet sought God's protection from knowledge that does not benefit and a heart that is not humble.
RAZI-FULL:v8p99/r2.anchor: قال عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( نعوذ بالله من علم لا ينفع وقلب لا يخشع )

SAMIN-DURR:3:79#6/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#6/r1.speaker: الجمهور
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#6/r1.claim: The standard tadrusūna has fatḥa on tāʾ and ḍamma on rāʾ, from triliteral darasa, matching taʿallamūna from triliteral ʿalima.
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#6/r1.anchor: بفتح التاء وضم الراء من الدرس وهو مناسب لتعلمون من علم ثلاثيا

SAMIN-DURR:3:79#6/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#6/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#6/r2.claim: A shadda on taʿallamūna does not require one on tadrusūna: the people first taught others, then studied, reciting the studied text to them.
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#6/r2.anchor: كنتم تعلمون غيركم ثم صرتم تدرسون، وبما كنتم تدرسونه عليهم أي

SAMIN-DURR:3:79#6/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#6/r3.speaker: أبو حيوة
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#6/r3.claim: In one transmission, Abū Ḥaywa reads the rāʾ with kasra, a weak dialect; darasa has two present-tense dialects.
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#6/r3.anchor: قرأ ابو حيوة في إحدى الروايتين عنه " تدرسون " بكسر الراء وهي لغة ضعيفة

SAMIN-DURR:3:79#6/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#6/r4.speaker: أبو حيوة
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#6/r4.claim: In another transmission, he reads the form with shadda: either intensively, like light taʿallamūna, or causatively with two understood objects, making others study.
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#6/r4.anchor: قرأ هو أيضا في رواية: " تدرسون " من درس بالتشديد، وفيه وجهان

SAMIN-DURR:3:79#6/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#6/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#6/r5.claim: A reading from adrasa is also reported, as in tukramūna from akrama; here afʿala means faʿʿala, as in adrasa/darrasa, akrama/karrama, and anzala/nazzala.
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#6/r5.anchor: وقرىء " تدرسون " من أدرس، كتكرمون من أكرم على أن أفعل بمعنى فعل بالتشديد

SAMIN-DURR:3:79#6/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#6/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#6/r6.claim: Dars means repetition and persistence; studying a book or Quran is repeating it, and studying a book can mean preserving its trace by memorization.
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#6/r6.anchor: والدرس: التكرار والإمان على الشيء ومنه: درس زيد الكتاب والقرآن يدرسه

SAMIN-DURR:3:79#6/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#6/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#6/r7.claim: Because Quran recitation is continuous, the verse calls its continuance dars; the same root describes a house whose trace has disappeared, with ṭalal ʿārif and dāris synonymous.
SAMIN-DURR:3:79#6/r7.anchor: عبر عن إدامة القرآن بالدرس، ودرس المنزل: ذهب أثره وطلل عارف ودارس بمعنى

STUDYQURAN:3:79/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:79/r1.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:3:79/r1.claim: One report says Jews asked the Prophet whether he wanted to be worshipped as Jesus was among Christians.
STUDYQURAN:3:79/r1.anchor: It is reported that the Prophet was asked by the Jews whether he wanted to be an object of worship, as Jesus was among the Christians (Ṭ),

STUDYQURAN:3:79/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:79/r2.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:3:79/r2.claim: Another report says he was asked whether people should prostrate to him instead of greeting him normally.
STUDYQURAN:3:79/r2.anchor: or that he was asked whether he thought people should prostrate themselves before him (an act associated with worship) rather than greet him normally (Z).

STUDYQURAN:3:79/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:79/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:3:79/r3.claim: Ḥukm, translated as judgment, can also mean rule.

STUDYQURAN:3:79/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:79/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:3:79/r4.claim: ʿIbād, singular ʿabd, means worshippers of something.
STUDYQURAN:3:79/r4.anchor: means to be worshippers of something.

STUDYQURAN:3:79/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:79/r5.speaker: most commentators
STUDYQURAN:3:79/r5.claim: Most commentators connect the verse to Islam’s rejection of Jesus’ worship; it also condemns other worship of humans, as in 9:31.
STUDYQURAN:3:79/r5.anchor: Although most commentators draw a connection between this verse and the Islamic rejection of the worship of Jesus, other types of worship directed at human beings are similarly deplored, as in 9:31

STUDYQURAN:3:79/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:79/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:3:79/r6.claim: The verse is thematically related to 5:116, where Jesus denies telling people to take him and his mother as gods apart from God.
STUDYQURAN:3:79/r6.anchor: It is related thematically to 5:116: And when God said, “O Jesus son of Mary! Didst thou say unto mankind

STUDYQURAN:3:79/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:79/r7.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:3:79/r7.claim: Rabbāniyyūn, translated “sages,” is variously understood as wise, knowledgeable, pious, or eminent religious scholars who know the lawful and forbidden.
STUDYQURAN:3:79/r7.anchor: a word interpreted variously as meaning those who are wise, knowledgeable, or pious (Ṭ) or the most eminent of religious scholars who understand the lawful and the forbidden (Q)

STUDYQURAN:3:79/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:79/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:3:79/r8.claim: The commentary directs readers to 5:43–44 for further discussion of rabbāniyyūn.

STUDYQURAN:3:79/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:79/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:3:79/r9.claim: The variant ribbiyyūn appears in 3:146 and is translated there as devoted men.
STUDYQURAN:3:79/r9.anchor: A variant of rabbānī, ribbiyyūn, appears in 3:146

STUDYQURAN:3:79/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:79/r10.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:3:79/r10.claim: An alternate reading renders the final phrase as knowing the Book and teaching it.
STUDYQURAN:3:79/r10.anchor: An alternate reading of the verse’s final phrase would give the translation, “from having known the Book and from having taught it” (Ṭ).

STUDYQURAN:3:146/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:146/r3.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:3:146/r3.claim: Some interpret ribbiyyūn as a form of rabbāniyyūn, translated as sages in 3:79.
STUDYQURAN:3:146/r3.anchor: Devoted men translates ribbiyyūn, which is interpreted by some as a form of rabbāniyyūn, rendered in this translation as sages (Z; see v. 79).

TAB-FULL:v5p524/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p524/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p524/r1.claim: The verse says no human should do this; بشر is a collective for Adam’s children, like قوم and خلق, though it can also be singular.
TAB-FULL:v5p524/r1.anchor: واحد له من لفظه مثل القوم والخلق، وقد يكون اسما لواحد

TAB-FULL:v5p524/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p524/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p524/r2.claim: God gives the person revelation of the Book, teaches him sound judgment, and grants him prophethood.
TAB-FULL:v5p524/r2.anchor: يقول: أن ينزل الله عليه كتابه، {والحكم} [آل عمران: 79] يعني: ويعلمه فصل الحكمة، {والنبوة} [آل عمران: 79] يقول: ويعطيه النبوة

TAB-FULL:v5p524/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p524/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p524/r3.claim: Such a recipient calls people to know God and His religious law, becoming leaders in knowledge, obedience, and worship by teaching and studying scripture.
TAB-FULL:v5p524/r3.anchor: فإنما يدعوهم إلى العلم بالله، ويحدوهم على معرفة شرائع دينه، وأن يكونوا رؤساء في المعرفة بأمر الله ونهيه

TAB-FULL:v5p524/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p524/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v5p524/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that at a gathering of Jewish and Christian scholars from Najrān, Abū Rāfiʿ and a Christian leader asked whether Muḥammad wanted them to worship him; he denied this, and the passage through 3:80 was revealed.
TAB-FULL:v5p524/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: قال أبو رافع القرظي حين اجتمعت الأحبار من اليهود والنصارى من أهل نجران عند رسول الله

TAB-FULL:v5p526/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p526/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v5p526/r1.claim: Qatāda says it is improper for someone given scripture, judgment, and prophethood to command people to take him as a lord besides God.
TAB-FULL:v5p526/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {ما كان لبشر أن يؤتيه الله الكتاب والحكم والنبوة ثم يقول للناس كونوا عبادا لي من دون الله} [آل عمران: 79]

TAB-FULL:v5p526/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p526/r2.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v5p526/r2.claim: Al-Rabīʿ gives the same interpretation: a prophet given these gifts should not tell people to worship him.

TAB-FULL:v5p526/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p526/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v5p526/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj says some Jews made people worship them by distorting scripture, then directing people contrary to what God revealed.
TAB-FULL:v5p526/r3.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قال: «كان ناس من يهود يتعبدون الناس من دون ربهم، بتحريفهم كتاب الله عن موضعه»

TAB-FULL:v5p527/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p527/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p527/r1.claim: In ‘but be rabbānī,’ the verb ‘he says to them’ is omitted because the surrounding words make it understood.
TAB-FULL:v5p527/r1.anchor: قوله: {ولكن كونوا ربانيين} [آل عمران: 79] قال: «كونوا فقهاء علماء»

TAB-FULL:v5p527/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p527/r2.speaker: أبو رزين
TAB-FULL:v5p527/r2.claim: Abū Razīn glosses rabbānī as wise and learned.
TAB-FULL:v5p527/r2.anchor: عن منصور، عن أبي رزين: {كونوا ربانيين} [آل عمران: 79] قال: «حكماء علماء»

TAB-FULL:v5p527/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p527/r3.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v5p527/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan glosses rabbānī as jurists and scholars.
TAB-FULL:v5p527/r3.anchor: عن الحسن، في قوله : {كونوا ربانيين} [آل عمران: 79] قال: «كونوا فقهاء علماء»

TAB-FULL:v5p527/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p527/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v5p527/r4.claim: Mujāhid calls them jurist scholars and says they rank above the aḥbār.
TAB-FULL:v5p527/r4.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، قال: " الربانيون: الفقهاء العلماء، وهم فوق الأحبار "

TAB-FULL:v5p527/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p527/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v5p527/r5.claim: Qatāda says people should be jurists and scholars.
TAB-FULL:v5p527/r5.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {ولكن كونوا ربانيين} [آل عمران: 79] قال: «كونوا فقهاء علماء»

TAB-FULL:v5p527/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p527/r6.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v5p527/r6.claim: Al-Suddī glosses rabbānī as wise jurists.
TAB-FULL:v5p527/r6.anchor: عن السدي، في قوله: {كونوا ربانيين} [آل عمران: 79] أما الربانيون: «فالحكماء الفقهاء»

TAB-FULL:v5p529/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p529/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v5p529/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains rabbānī as wise jurists.
TAB-FULL:v5p529/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {ولكن كونوا ربانيين} [آل عمران: 79] يقول: «كونوا حكماء فقهاء»

TAB-FULL:v5p529/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p529/r2.speaker: يحيى بن عقيل
TAB-FULL:v5p529/r2.claim: Yaḥyā ibn ʿAqīl glosses rabbānī and aḥbār together as jurists and scholars.
TAB-FULL:v5p529/r2.anchor: عن يحيى بن عقيل، في قوله: " الربانيون والأحبار، قال: الفقهاء العلماء "

TAB-FULL:v5p529/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p529/r3.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v5p529/r3.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says people should be jurists and scholars.
TAB-FULL:v5p529/r3.anchor: يقول في قوله: {كونوا ربانيين} [آل عمران: 79] يقول: «كونوا فقهاء علماء»

TAB-FULL:v5p529/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p529/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v5p529/r4.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr interprets rabbānī as wise and God-fearing.
TAB-FULL:v5p529/r4.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، قوله: {كونوا ربانيين} [آل عمران: 79] قال: «حكماء أتقياء»

TAB-FULL:v5p529/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p529/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v5p529/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says rabbānī refers to people’s governors and leaders, who take charge of and nurture them; he reads 5:63 as distinguishing governors from scholars.
TAB-FULL:v5p529/r5.anchor: سمعت ابن زيد، يقول في قوله: {كونوا ربانيين} [آل عمران: 79] قال: " الربانيون: الذين يربون الناس، ولاة هذا الأمر

TAB-FULL:v5p529/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p529/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p529/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers deriving rabbānī from rabbān, one who manages and improves people’s affairs, as the word’s root meaning.
TAB-FULL:v5p529/r6.anchor: وأولى الأقوال عندي بالصواب في الربانيين أنهم جمع رباني، وأن الرباني المنسوب إلى الربان: الذي يرب الناس

TAB-FULL:v5p529/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p529/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p529/r7.claim: As lexical evidence, ʿAlqama ibn ʿAbada’s verse uses ربتني to mean that someone previously managed the speaker’s affairs, though they neglected him.
TAB-FULL:v5p529/r7.anchor: ومنه قول علقمة بن عبدة: [البحر الطويل] وكنت امرأ أفضت إليك ربابتي … وقبلك ربتني

TAB-FULL:v5p529/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p529/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p529/r8.claim: The intensive rabbān follows a pattern such as نعسان; most nouns on فعْلان come from verbs with the cited past-tense pattern, with exceptions such as نعس and رب.
TAB-FULL:v5p529/r8.anchor: مثل قولهم: هو سكران وعطشان وريان، من سكر يسكر

TAB-FULL:v5p529/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p529/r9.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p529/r9.claim: Scholars of jurisprudence and wisdom, God-fearing sages, and just governors all qualify as rabbānī because each improves people’s religious and worldly affairs.
TAB-FULL:v5p529/r9.anchor: كانوا جميعا مستحقين أنهم ممن دخل في قوله عز وجل {ولكن كونوا ربانيين} [آل عمران: 79]

TAB-FULL:v5p531/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p531/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p531/r1.claim: Rabbānī people are pillars for others in religious and worldly knowledge and affairs.
TAB-FULL:v5p531/r1.anchor: فالربانيون إذا، هم عماد الناس في الفقه والعلم وأمور الدين والدنيا

TAB-FULL:v5p531/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p531/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v5p531/r2.claim: Mujāhid says rabbānī people stand above the aḥbār because the aḥbār are scholars.
TAB-FULL:v5p531/r2.anchor: ولذلك قال مجاهد: «وهم فوق الأحبار» ، لأن الأحبار هم العلماء

TAB-FULL:v5p531/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p531/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p531/r3.claim: A rabbānī combines knowledge and jurisprudence with political insight, administration, and care for subjects’ religious and worldly welfare.
TAB-FULL:v5p531/r3.anchor: والرباني: الجامع إلى العلم والفقه البصر بالسياسة والتدبير والقيام بأمور الرعية

TAB-FULL:v5p531#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p531#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p531#2/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī reports that the Hijaz majority and some Basrans read with light lām and fatḥa, arguing that a doubled lām and ḍamma would require a doubled rāʾ in تدرسون.
TAB-FULL:v5p531#2/r1.anchor: قراءة ذلك كذلك، بأن الصواب لو كان التشديد في اللام وضم التاء، لكان الصواب في {تدرسون} [آل عمران: 79] بضم التاء وتشديد الراء

TAB-FULL:v5p531#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p531#2/r2.speaker: قراء الكوفيين
TAB-FULL:v5p531#2/r2.claim: The Kufan majority reads the verb with ḍamma and a doubled lām, meaning teaching people the Book and studying it.
TAB-FULL:v5p531#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ ذلك عامة قراء الكوفيين: {بما كنتم تعلمون الكتاب} [آل عمران: 79] بضم التاء من «تعلمون» وتشديد اللام

TAB-FULL:v5p531#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p531#2/r3.speaker: قراء الكوفيين
TAB-FULL:v5p531#2/r3.claim: They argue that a teacher must already know, while a knowledgeable person need not teach others, so this reading praises the people more.
TAB-FULL:v5p531#2/r3.anchor: قالوا: ولا موصوف بأنه يعلم، إلا وهو موصوف بأنه عالم، قالوا: فأما الموصوف بأنه عالم فغير موصوف بأنه معلم غيره

TAB-FULL:v5p531#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p531#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v5p531#2/r4.claim: Mujāhid read the verb lightly with fatḥa, as the reading describing their own knowledge.
TAB-FULL:v5p531#2/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد، أنه قرأ: (بما كنتم تعلمون الكتاب وبما كنتم تدرسون) مخففة بنصب التاء

TAB-FULL:v5p531#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p531#2/r5.speaker: ابن عيينة
TAB-FULL:v5p531#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿUyayna remarks that people did not know the Book until they taught it.
TAB-FULL:v5p531#2/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عيينة: ما علموه حتى علموه

TAB-FULL:v5p531#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p531#2/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p531#2/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the Kufan reading ‘you teach,’ since the verse describes rabbānī people as leaders who improve and nurture others by teaching God’s Book.
TAB-FULL:v5p531#2/r6.anchor: وأولى القراءتين بالصواب في ذلك قراءة من قرأه بضم التاء وتشديد اللام

TAB-FULL:v5p531#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p531#2/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p531#2/r7.claim: For تدرسون, he prefers reciting and studying the Qurʾān over studying jurisprudence, because it is coordinated with teaching the Book and no other book was mentioned.
TAB-FULL:v5p531#2/r7.anchor: وأشبه التأويلين بالدراسة ما قلنا من تلاوة الكتاب؛ لأنه عطف على قوله: {تعلمون الكتاب} [آل عمران: 79]

TAB-FULL:v5p531#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p531#2/r8.speaker: أبو زكريا
TAB-FULL:v5p531#2/r8.claim: Abū Zakariyyā reports that ʿĀṣim read the teaching form, identified the Book as the Qurʾān, and interpreted تدرسون as jurisprudence.
TAB-FULL:v5p531#2/r8.anchor: قال أبو زكريا: كان عاصم يقرؤها: {بما كنتم تعلمون الكتاب} [آل عمران: 79] قال: القرآن، {وبما كنتم تدرسون} [آل عمران: 79] قال: «الفقه»

TAB-FULL:v5p531#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p531#2/r9.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p531#2/r9.claim: The verse calls people to become leaders in religion and worldly life by teaching the Book’s rulings and meanings and by reciting and studying it.
TAB-FULL:v5p531#2/r9.anchor: كونوا أيها الناس سادة الناس وقادتهم في أمر دينهم ودنياهم، ربانيين بتعليمكم إياهم كتاب الله

TABATABAI:3:64-78#4/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64-78#4/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:64-78#4/r6.claim: Tabatabai says the verses about no human recipient of scripture claiming worship fit Jesus more readily than Muhammad.
TABATABAI:3:64-78#4/r6.anchor: أوفق سياقا وأسهل انطباقا على عيسى ابن مريم عليه السلام منه برسول الله

TABATABAI:3:64-78#4/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:64-78#4/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:64-78#4/r7.claim: He suggests Ibn Abbas may have inferred and applied the verses about Muhammad, since the Qur'an often presents such statements as questions, answers, or narrated rebuttals.
TABATABAI:3:64-78#4/r7.anchor: فلعل ما في الرواية من نزول الآيات في حق رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم استنباط وتطبيق من ابن عباس

TABATABAI:3:79-80/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80/r1.claim: These verses form a second argument defending Jesus from Christian claims: he is neither God nor someone who claimed divinity, since he is a created human, born and raised by his mother, though fatherless like Adam.
TABATABAI:3:79-80/r1.anchor: بيان وقوع الآيات عقيب الآيات المرتبطة بأمر عيسى عليه السلام يفيد أنها بمنزلة الفصل الثاني

TABATABAI:3:79-80/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80/r2.claim: A human given scripture, judgment, and prophethood remains a servant; such a prophet cannot claim worship or give another creature a right to worship that belongs to God, nor deny a prophet's God-given right.
TABATABAI:3:79-80/r2.anchor: والنبي الذي هذا شأنه لا يعدو طور العبودية ولا يتعرى عن زي الرقية

TABATABAI:3:79-80/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80/r3.claim: Bashar is synonymous with insan and can denote either one human being or a group.
TABATABAI:3:79-80/r3.anchor: البشر مرادف للإنسان، ويطلق على الواحد والكثير

TABATABAI:3:79-80/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80/r4.claim: The lām in ma kāna li-bashar denotes ownership or entitlement: the human has no right to do this, as in the cited Qur'anic formulations.
TABATABAI:3:79-80/r4.anchor: اللام للملك أي لا يملك ذلك أي ليس له بحق

TABATABAI:3:79-80/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80/r5.claim: The phrase about God granting scripture, judgment, and prophethood is the subject of kāna and prepares for the following clause; its inclusion signals that divine grant itself is central.
TABATABAI:3:79-80/r5.anchor: اسم كان إلا أنه توطئة لما يتبعه من قوله { ثم يقول للناس }

TABATABAI:3:79-80#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#2/r1.claim: Jesus' denial that he could say what he had no right to say illustrates that God's prophetic gifts and education prevent their recipient from claiming worship.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#2/r1.anchor: قال سبحانك ما يكون لي أن أقول ما ليس لي بحق

TABATABAI:3:79-80#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#2/r2.claim: Saying only that a human may not claim worship would mean a legal prohibition despite possible sin; the wording that God grants him scripture and prophethood makes the claim impossible under divine guidance.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#2/r2.anchor: فإن العبارة الثانية تفيد معنى أصل التشريع كما تقدم بخلاف قوله { أن يؤتيه الله }

TABATABAI:3:79-80#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#2/r3.claim: God's nurturing purpose does not fail; those granted scripture, judgment, and prophethood are not abandoned even if others disbelieve, as another verse states.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#2/r3.anchor: فقد وكلنا بها قوما ليسوا بها بكافرين

TABATABAI:3:79-80#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#2/r4.claim: The verse means a human cannot receive these divine gifts and then call people to worship himself instead of God.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#2/r4.anchor: فمحصل المعنى أنه لا يسع لبشر أن يجمع بين هذه النعم الإلهية وبين دعوة الناس إلى عبادة نفسه

TABATABAI:3:79-80#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#2/r5.claim: The context resembles the statement that Christ and the angels are too exalted to disdain God's worship, since such arrogance merits punishment and God would not punish his honored prophets and angels.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#2/r5.anchor: فإن المستفاد من الآية أن المسيح وكذا الملائكة المقربون أجل شأنا وأرفع قدرا أن يستنكفوا

TABATABAI:3:79-80#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#2/r6.claim: Although thumma usually marks succession, ideas can be considered together even when their events occur successively, so it does not defeat the combined meaning.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#2/r6.anchor: وكما يصح اعتبار الاجتماع والمعية بين المتحدين زمانا كذلك يصح اعتباره بين المترتبين والمتتاليين

TABATABAI:3:79-80#2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#2/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#2/r7.claim: Ibad is a plural of abd like abid; ibad is commonly used for servants ascribed to God, while people are usually said to have abid.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#2/r7.anchor: فالعباد كالعبيد جمع عبد، والفرق بينهما أن العباد يغلب استعماله فيما إذا نسب إلى الله

TABATABAI:3:79-80#2/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#2/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#2/r8.claim: Min duni Allah necessarily excludes worship directed to another, since God accepts only worship sincerely devoted to him.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#2/r8.anchor: وتقييد قوله عبادا لي بقوله من دون الله تقييد قهري

TABATABAI:3:79-80#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#3/r1.claim: True worship presupposes assigning the worshiped some independence, even in partnership; because God's lordship is absolute, his worship requires denying all independence to everything else, so worshiping another alongside God is worship apart from him.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#3/r1.anchor: فإن الشريك من حيث إنه شريك مساهم ذو استقلال ما، والله سبحانه له الربوبية المطلقة

TABATABAI:3:79-80#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#4/r1.claim: Study is more specific than teaching and usually means learning from a book by reading.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#4/r1.anchor: والدراسة أخص من التعليم فإنه يستعمل غالبا فيما يتعلم عن الكتاب بقراءته

TABATABAI:3:79-80#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#4/r2.claim: Al-Tabataba'i cites Qur'anic descriptions of people studying a scripture and of earlier communities studying books given to them.

TABATABAI:3:79-80#4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#4/r3.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:3:79-80#4/r3.claim: Al-Raghib says study is more specific than teaching and usually means learning from a book by reading; dars involves taking up a trace through sustained reading and memorization.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#4/r3.anchor: قال الراغب درس الدار بقي أثرها، وبقاء الأثر يقتضي انمحائه في نفسه

TABATABAI:3:79-80#4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#4/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#4/r4.claim: The exhortation calls people to believe certainly in the divine teachings they study, embody their virtues, and practice the good works they teach, thereby becoming God-oriented scholars.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#4/r4.anchor: ومحصل الكلام أن البشر الذي هذا شأنه إنما يدعوكم إلى التلبس بالإيمان واليقين

TABATABAI:3:79-80#4/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#4/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#4/r5.claim: The past-tense wording hints at an indirect address to Christians: Israel possessed and studied scripture amid alteration, and Jesus came to clarify disputes, ease some prohibitions, and restore their proper teaching and study.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#4/r5.anchor: حيث اشتمل على الماضي الدال على التحقق لا يخلو عن دلالة ما على أن الكلام في الآية مسوق للتعريض بالنصارى

TABATABAI:3:79-80#4/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#4/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#4/r6.claim: The verse can also apply to Muhammad because his mission addressed scriptural People of the Book, but Jesus fits it first because his mission was specifically to Israel; it does not fit Noah, Abraham, or Moses.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#4/r6.anchor: لكن عيسى عليه السلام أسبق انطباقا عليه، وكانت رسالته خاصة ببني إسرائيل

TABATABAI:3:79-80#5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#5/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#5/r1.claim: The first clause alludes to Christians' worship of Jesus and their explicit claim that he called them to his divinity; other claims about angels and prophets imply divinity, so the verse says lords rather than gods.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#5/r1.anchor: كان ذلك نسبة منهم إليه أنه قال كونوا عبادا لي بخلاف اتخاذ الملائكة والنبيين أربابا

TABATABAI:3:79-80#5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#5/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#5/r2.claim: The first clause says people because its verb implies face-to-face speech and its original audience was absent; the second addresses you because commands can reach descendants through their shared community, unlike spoken words.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#5/r2.anchor: ولم يكن الحاضرون في زمن نزول الآية حاضرين إذ ذاك لا جرم قيل ثم يقول للناس

TABATABAI:3:79-80#6/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#6/r1.speaker: بعض المفسرين
TABATABAI:3:79-80#6/r1.claim: Some exegetes identify the verses with Muhammad, citing a report that Abu Rafi' al-Qurazi and a Christian from Najran asked whether he wanted them to worship him; they read the closing phrase as Islam brought by Muhammad.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#6/r1.anchor: وقد ذكر بعض المفسرين أن المراد بقوله تعالى { ما كان لبشر أن يؤتيه الله } إلى آخر الآيتين

TABATABAI:3:79-80#6/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#6/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#6/r3.claim: Mary's mother vowed her unborn child for service in the sanctuary, expected a boy, grieved at giving birth to a girl, and named her Mary, meaning the female servant; after Imran's death, the priests disputed her care and lots assigned her to Zechariah.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#6/r3.anchor: كانت أم المسيح مريم بنت عمران حملت بها أمها فنذرت أن تجعل ما في بطنها إذا وضعته محررا يخدم المسجد

TABATABAI:3:79-80#6/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#6/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#6/r4.claim: Zechariah kept Mary in a screened sanctuary where she worshiped; she was provided for miraculously and described as righteous, protected, purified, chosen, addressed by angels, and among the obedient.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#6/r4.anchor: فكانت تعبد الله سبحانه فيها، لا يدخل عليها إلا زكريا

TABATABAI:3:79-80#6/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#6/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#6/r5.claim: God sent the Spirit to Mary in human form and announced a son without a father, his future miracles and mission, his support by the Holy Spirit, and his teaching of scripture, wisdom, Torah, and Gospel; she then conceived.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#6/r5.anchor: ثم إن الله تعالى أرسل إليها الروح وهي محتجبة فتمثل لها بشرا سويا

TABATABAI:3:79-80#7/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#7/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#7/r1.claim: Jesus' pregnancy, birth, speech, and existence followed ordinary human patterns; his mother's pain and vow of silence are recounted, and her people accuse her before he speaks from the cradle.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#7/r1.anchor: وكان حمله ووضعه وكلامه وسائر شؤون وجوده من سنخ ما عند سائر الأفراد من الإنسان

TABATABAI:3:79-80#7/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#7/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#7/r2.claim: Jesus' cradle declaration that he is God's servant, given scripture and prophethood, blessed, prayerful, and dutiful to his mother foreshadows his struggle against injustice and restoration of Moses' law and knowledge.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#7/r2.anchor: فكان هذا الكلام منه عليه السلام كبراعة الاستهلال بالنسبة إلى ما سينهض على البغي والظلم

TABATABAI:3:79-80#7/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#7/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#7/r3.claim: Jesus and Mary grew up and lived as ordinary humans, eating and drinking and experiencing the conditions common to human life.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#7/r3.anchor: ثم نشأ عيسى عليه السلام وشب وكان هو وأمه على العادة الجارية في الحياة البشرية يأكلان ويشربان

TABATABAI:3:79-80#7/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#7/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#7/r4.claim: Jesus was sent to Israel with a new law that confirmed Moses while lifting some Torah restrictions, clarified disputes, and announced a later messenger named Ahmad.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#7/r4.anchor: وكان يدعوهم إلى شريعته الجديدة وهو تصديق شريعة موسى عليه السلام إلا أنه نسخ بعض ما حرم في التوراة

TABATABAI:3:79-80#7/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#7/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#7/r5.claim: Jesus performed the announced signs, including creating a bird, healing the blind and leprous, raising the dead, and revealing hidden matters, all by God's permission.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#7/r5.anchor: وأنجز عليه السلام ما ذكره لهم من المعجزات كخلق الطير وإحياء الموتى وإبراء الأكمه والأبرص

TABATABAI:3:79-80#7/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#7/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#7/r6.claim: After losing hope because of Israel's obstinacy, Jesus selected the disciples who believed as helpers for God.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#7/r6.anchor: فانتخب من الشرذمة التي آمنت به الحواريين أنصارا له إلى الله

TABATABAI:3:79-80#7/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#7/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#7/r7.claim: When Jews sought to kill Jesus, God took and raised him; the Jews were left to suppose that they had killed or crucified him.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#7/r7.anchor: فتوفاه الله ورفعه إليه، وشبه لليهود فمن زاعم أنهم قتلوه

TABATABAI:3:79-80#8/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#8/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#8/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī lists Jesus as God's servant and prophet, an Israelite messenger and one of five resolute messengers with a law and Gospel, Messiah, God's Word and Spirit, imam, witness, and herald of Muhammad.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#8/r1.anchor: كان عليه السلام عبدا لله وكان نبيا، وكان رسولا إلى بني إسرائيل

TABATABAI:3:79-80#8/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#8/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#8/r2.claim: He also describes Jesus as honored, near, chosen, elect, righteous, blessed, pure, a sign and mercy, dutiful to his mother, and taught scripture and wisdom.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#8/r2.anchor: وكان وجيها في الدنيا والآخرة ومن المقربين، وكان من المصطفين، وكان من المجتبين وكان من الصالحين

TABATABAI:3:79-80#8/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#8/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#8/r3.claim: These twenty-two marks of Jesus's spiritual rank divide into acquired qualities, such as servitude, nearness, and righteousness, and qualities bestowed by divine election.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#8/r3.anchor: وهي على قسمين اكتسابية كالعبودية والقرب والصلاح، واختصاصية

TABATABAI:3:79-80#8/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#8/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#8/r4.claim: The Qur'an portrays Jesus as God's servant and messenger; he never claimed the status attributed to him and spoke only what God commissioned him to say.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#8/r4.anchor: كان عبدا رسولا، وأنه لم يدع لنفسه ما نسبوه إليه، ولا تكلم معهم إلا بالرسالة

TABATABAI:3:79-80#8/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#8/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#8/r5.claim: Jesus understood himself as wholly obedient to God, called people only to worship God, and served as witness to their deeds; God's final treatment of them was God's alone to decide.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#8/r5.anchor: يرى نفسه بالنسبة إلى ربه عبدا لا شأن له إلا الامتثال

TABATABAI:3:79-80#8/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#8/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#8/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī recalls the claim that Jesus is among those who intercede and whose intercession is accepted.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#8/r6.anchor: عيسى عليه السلام من الشفعاء يوم القيامة يشفع فيشفع

TABATABAI:3:79-80#8/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#8/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#8/r7.claim: The Qur'an's account of Jesus and his mother includes the statement that the crucifixion only appeared so to its observers.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#8/r7.anchor: ولكن شبه لهم النساء 157، فهذه جمل ما قصه القرآن في عيسى ابن مريم وأمه

TABATABAI:3:79-80#9/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#9/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#9/r1.claim: Christians diverged into more than seventy broad sectarian positions, with many finer disputes among them.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#9/r1.anchor: بما ربما جاوز السبعين من حيث كليات ما اختلفوا فيه، وجزئيات المذاهب والآراء كثيرة جدا

TABATABAI:3:79-80#9/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#9/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#9/r2.claim: The Qur'an focuses on what Christians say about Jesus and his mother because those claims touch monotheism.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#9/r2.anchor: القرآن إنما يهتم بما قالوا به في أمر عيسى نفسه وأمه لمساسه بأساس التوحيد

TABATABAI:3:79-80#9/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#9/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#9/r3.claim: The Qur'an gives less attention to related details such as textual corruption and redemption.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#9/r3.anchor: وأما بعض الجزئيات كمسألة التحريف ومسألة التفدية فلم يهتم به ذاك الاهتمام

TABATABAI:3:79-80#9/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#9/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#9/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī reads Qur'an 43:86, Jesus's witness, and Qur'an 4:159 and 5:110 as supporting Jesus's intercession.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#9/r4.anchor: ولا يملك الذين يدعون من دونه الشفاعة إلا من شهد بالحق وهم يعلمون

TABATABAI:3:79-80#9/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#9/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#9/r5.claim: The account of Jesus's testimony at judgment neither establishes nor denies intercession; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī explains why its wording does not make either case.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#9/r5.anchor: وأما الشفاعة فالآية غير متعرضة لأمرها لا إثباتا ولا نفيا

TABATABAI:3:79-80#9/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#9/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#9/r6.claim: Christian redemption by substitution is distinct from intercession and would negate God's absolute sovereignty.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#9/r6.anchor: وهذا غير التفدية التي يقول بها النصارى، وهي إبطال الجزاء بالفدية والعوض فإنها تبطل السلطنة المطلقة الإلهية

TABATABAI:3:79-80#9/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#9/r7.speaker: النصارى
TABATABAI:3:79-80#9/r7.claim: The Qur'an reports Christians saying that the Messiah is God's son.

TABATABAI:3:79-80#9/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#9/r8.speaker: النصارى
TABATABAI:3:79-80#9/r8.claim: The Qur'an also cites the claim that the Merciful has taken a son.

TABATABAI:3:79-80#9/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#9/r9.speaker: النصارى
TABATABAI:3:79-80#9/r9.claim: The Qur'an reports the claim that God is the Messiah, son of Mary.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#9/r9.anchor: لقد كفر الذين قالوا إن الله هو المسيح ابن مريم

TABATABAI:3:79-80#9/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#9/r10.speaker: النصارى
TABATABAI:3:79-80#9/r10.claim: The Qur'an reports the claim that God is one of three.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#9/r10.anchor: لقد كفر الذين قالوا إن الله ثالث ثلاثة

TABATABAI:3:79-80#9/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#9/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#9/r11.claim: The Qur'an tells Christians to stop saying three.

TABATABAI:3:79-80#10/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#10/r1.speaker: الملكانية
TABATABAI:3:79-80#10/r1.claim: The Melkites held that Jesus was God's son in a literal sense.

TABATABAI:3:79-80#10/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#10/r2.speaker: النسطورية
TABATABAI:3:79-80#10/r2.claim: The Nestorians described descent and sonship as light shining on a transparent body like crystal.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#10/r2.anchor: والنسطورية القائلين بأن النزول والنبوة من قبيل إشراق النور على جسم شفاف كالبلور

TABATABAI:3:79-80#10/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#10/r3.speaker: اليعقوبية
TABATABAI:3:79-80#10/r3.claim: The Jacobites held that God transformed into flesh and blood.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#10/r3.anchor: واليعقوبية القائلين بأنه من الانقلاب، وقد انقلب الإله سبحانه لحما ودما

TABATABAI:3:79-80#10/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#10/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#10/r4.claim: Though Christian schools differ, the Qur'an targets their common claim of Jesus's divine sonship and the related doctrine of Trinity.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#10/r4.anchor: لكن الظاهر أن القرآن لا يهتم بخصوصيات مذاهبهم المختلفة، وإنما يهتم بكلمة واحدة مشتركة بينهم جميعا وهي البنوة

TABATABAI:3:79-80#10/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#10/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#10/r5.claim: The uniform Qur'anic argument shows that it addresses the shared doctrine rather than each sect's detailed formulation.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#10/r5.anchor: والدليل على ذلك وحدة الاحتجاج الوارد عليهم في القرآن لسانا

TABATABAI:3:79-80#10/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#10/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#10/r6.claim: The Torah and present Gospels affirm one God, while the Gospel also states sonship and identifies the son with the Father.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#10/r6.anchor: أن التوراة والأناجيل الحاضرة جميعا تصرح بتوحيد الإله تعالى، من جانب والإنجيل يصرح بالبنوة من جانب آخر

TABATABAI:3:79-80#10/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#10/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#10/r7.claim: Christians did not read Gospel sonship as merely honorific, even though some passages explicitly use it that way.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#10/r7.anchor: ولم يحملوا البنوة الموجودة فيه على التشريف والتبريك مع ما في موارد منه من التصريح بذلك

TABATABAI:3:79-80#11/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#11/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#11/r1.claim: Gospel passages apply the language of Father and children to Jesus's followers as well, supporting an honorific sense in some contexts.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#11/r1.anchor: تطلق لفظ الأب على الله تعالى وتقدس بالنسبة إلى عيسى وغيره جميعا كما ترى بعناية التشريف ونحوه

TABATABAI:3:79-80#11/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#11/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#11/r2.claim: Other Gospel declarations present Jesus as the way to the Father, as one in the Father, and as having come from God; together with the Word passage, these appear to affirm more than honorific sonship.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#11/r2.anchor: من رآني فقد رأى الأب فكيف تقول أنت أرنا الأب؟ أما تؤمن أني في أبي وأبي في

TABATABAI:3:79-80#12/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#12/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#12/r1.claim: The Christian doctrine described here preserves Jesus as God's son while affirming one God: one substance has three hypostases, existence (Father), knowledge or Word (Son), and life (Holy Spirit); the Word descends with the Spirit.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#12/r1.anchor: إن الذات جوهر واحد له أقانيم ثلاث، والمراد بالأقنوم هو الصفة التي هي نحو ظهور الشيء

TABATABAI:3:79-80#12/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#12/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#12/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī treats the Qur'an's several descriptions of Christian belief as one shared doctrine: unity understood through Trinity, the common element across the sects.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#12/r2.anchor: كل ذلك يرجع إلى معنى واحد وهو تثليث الوحدة هو المشترك بين جميع المذاهب المستحدثة في النصرانية

TABATABAI:3:79-80#12/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#12/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#12/r3.claim: The Qur'an refutes Trinity by two routes: generally, showing that divine sonship is impossible; specifically, showing that Jesus is a created servant rather than God's son.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#12/r3.anchor: يرد قول المثلثة من طريقين أحدهما الطريق العام، وهو بيان استحالة الابن عليه تعالى في نفسه

TABATABAI:3:79-80#12/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#12/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#12/r4.claim: Ordinary generation divides material substance and gradually raises a new member of the same kind, so it entails materiality and developmental processes incompatible with God.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#12/r4.anchor: حقيقة البنوة والتولد هو أن يجزأ واحد من هذه الموجودات الحية المادية

TABATABAI:3:79-80#13/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#13/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#13/r1.claim: Because every being depends on God, no independently existing being could match him as an equal offspring; divine generation would also imply gradual action under matter, motion, and time.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#13/r1.anchor: فكل شيء سواه مفتقر الوجود إليه قائم الوجود به فكيف يمكن فرض شيء غيره يماثله في النوعية

TABATABAI:3:79-80#13/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#13/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#13/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī reads Qur'an 2:116–117 as separate proofs: God is exalted above offspring, all creation belongs to and obeys him, and he originates creation and brings commands to be immediately.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#13/r2.anchor: فقوله سبحانه برهان، وقوله { له ما في السماوات والأرض كل له قانتون } برهان آخر

TABATABAI:3:79-80#13/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#13/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#13/r3.claim: Alternatively, “Originator of the heavens and earth” itself rules out generation because God creates without a prior model, whereas a child would reproduce its parent's likeness.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#13/r3.anchor: ويستفاد منه أن خلقه تعالى على غير مثال سابق فلا يمكن منه الإيلاد لأنه خلق على مثال نفسه

TABATABAI:3:79-80#13/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#13/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#13/r4.claim: Even if Christians mean a nonmaterial, non-temporal separation by sonship, father and son still entail real plurality: a dependent son is not God, while an independent equal would violate monotheism.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#13/r4.anchor: إثبات الابن والأب إثبات للعدد بالضرورة، وهو إثبات للكثرة الحقيقية

TABATABAI:3:79-80#14/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#14/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#14/r1.claim: Qur'an 4:171 states the general argument that God is one and has no offspring.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#14/r1.anchor: ولا تقولوا ثلاثة انتهوا خيرا لكم إنما الله إله واحد سبحانه أن يكون له ولد

TABATABAI:3:79-80#14/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#14/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#14/r2.claim: Jesus's gestation, birth, nursing, growth, aging, and ordinary bodily conditions show that he lived as a natural human and therefore was created like other people.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#14/r2.anchor: حملت به مريم، وربته جنينا في رحمها، ثم وضعته وضع المرأة ولدها

TABATABAI:3:79-80#14/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#14/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#14/r3.claim: Miracles and Jesus's birth without a father are extraordinary but possible events, not evidence of divinity; Adam and prophets also had miraculous origins or deeds without becoming divine.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#14/r3.anchor: فإنما هي أمور خارقة للعادة المألوفة والسنة الجارية في الطبيعة فإنها نادرة الوجود لا مستحيلته

TABATABAI:3:79-80#15/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#15/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#15/r1.claim: The Qur'an singles out eating because it clearly proves materiality and need: hunger and thirst relieved by food and drink show dependence incompatible with divine self-sufficiency.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#15/r1.anchor: وقد خص أكل الطعام من بين جميع الأفعال بالذكر لكونه من أحسنها دلالة على المادية واستلزاما للحاجة والفاقة المنافية للألوهية

TABATABAI:3:79-80#15/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#15/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#15/r2.claim: Jesus's human conditions were real, not appearance or imagination; the Gospels repeatedly call him human and recount ordinary bodily needs, so he could be harmed or killed like others.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#15/r2.anchor: بل كان على الحقيقة، وكان المسيح عليه السلام إنسانا ذا هذه الأوصاف والأحوال والأفعال

TABATABAI:3:79-80#15/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#15/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#15/r3.claim: The Qur'an's questions about who could prevent God from killing Jesus and his mother, and whether they can control harm or benefit, reinforce that Jesus is subject to God's dominion.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#15/r3.anchor: قل فمن يملك من الله شيئا إن أراد أن يهلك المسيح ابن مريم وأمه

TABATABAI:3:79-80#16/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#16/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#16/r1.claim: Jesus's worship of God proves that he is a servant rather than God; the angels' worship similarly shows they are not divine daughters, and the Holy Spirit is not God.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#16/r1.anchor: فعبادة المسيح أول دليل على أنه ليس بإله، وأن الألوهية لغيره لا نصيب له فيها

TABATABAI:3:79-80#16/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#16/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#16/r2.claim: The Gospels portray the Holy Spirit as obeying God and his messengers, which is incompatible with the Spirit being God commanding or obeying itself.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#16/r2.anchor: الروح طائع لله ورسله مؤتمر للأمر محكوم بالحكم

TABATABAI:3:79-80#16/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#16/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#16/r3.claim: Jesus calls the Israelites to worship God as his Lord and theirs; the Gospels likewise report that he acknowledged God as his Lord and never explicitly called people to worship himself.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#16/r3.anchor: وقال المسيح يا بني إسرائيل اعبدوا الله ربي وربكم إنه من يشرك بالله فقد حرم الله عليه الجنة

TABATABAI:3:79-80#16/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#16/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#16/r4.claim: Because Jesus never explicitly invited worship of himself, al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī interprets the Gospel saying “I and my Father are one” as meaning that obeying Jesus is obeying God.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#16/r4.anchor: فمن الواجب أن يحمل على تقدير صحته على أن المراد أن اطاعتي إطاعة الله

TABATABAI:3:79-80#17/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#17/r1.speaker: النصارى
TABATABAI:3:79-80#17/r1.claim: Christians teach that Adam's sin and its inheritance left humanity facing eternal punishment; Christ, both divine and human and sinless, incarnated through Mary and accepted cursed crucifixion as ransom for believers and the whole world.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#17/r1.anchor: ففدى الناس بنفسه ليخلصوا بذلك من عقاب الآخرة وهلاك السرمد وهو كفارة لخطايا المؤمنين به بل لخطايا كل العالم

TABATABAI:3:79-80#17/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#17/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#17/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says crucifixion and redemption form the core of Christian preaching, while the Qur'an makes monotheism the foundation of Islam's call.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#17/r2.anchor: وقد جعلت النصارى هذه الكلمة أعني مسألة الصلب والفداء أساس دعوتهم

TABATABAI:3:79-80#18/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#18/r1.speaker: المسيح
TABATABAI:3:79-80#18/r1.claim: The Gospels depict Jesus as making monotheism and love of God the first commandments.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#18/r1.anchor: مع أن المسيح على ما يصرح به الأناجيل، وقد تقدم نقله. كان يجعل أول الوصايا هو التوحيد ومحبة الله سبحانه.

TABATABAI:3:79-80#18/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#18/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#18/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī's aim is to show how the Christian account conflicts with Qur'anic teaching, then distinguish Qur'anic intercession from Christian redemption.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#18/r2.anchor: بيان جهات منافاته لأصول تعليم القرآن وختمه ببيان الفرق بين ما يثبته القرآن من الشفاعة وما يثبتونه من الفداء

TABATABAI:3:79-80#18/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#18/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#18/r3.claim: The Qur'an speaks in terms near human understanding so people can distinguish truth from falsehood, good from evil, and benefit from harm.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#18/r3.anchor: إنما يخاطب الناس ويكلمهم ببيان ما يقرب من أفق عقولهم ويمكن بياناته من فقههم وفهمهم

TABATABAI:3:79-80#18/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#18/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#18/r4.claim: Adam's tree prohibition was guidance for his welfare, not a legislative command; its breach brought loss of paradise and nearness, not afterlife punishment.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#18/r4.anchor: لا يترتب على امتثاله ولا تركه ثواب ولا عقاب مولوي

TABATABAI:3:79-80#18/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#18/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#18/r5.claim: The Qur'an and rational proof exonerate prophets from committing sins or violating God's command.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#18/r5.anchor: القرآن ينزه ساحة الأنبياء عليهم السلام ويبرئ نفوسهم الشريفة عن اقتراف المعاصي والفسق عن أمر الله سبحانه

TABATABAI:3:79-80#19/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#19/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#19/r1.claim: The Qur'an says God forgave Adam; reason likewise rejects the idea that guilt is ineradicable, since forgiveness removes sin's effects.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#19/r1.anchor: فتلقى آدم من ربه كلمات فتاب عليه إنه هو التواب الرحيم البقرة 37

TABATABAI:3:79-80#19/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#19/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#19/r2.claim: Inherited guilt would punish people for another's deed, which the Qur'an denies and reason deems unjust.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#19/r2.anchor: والقرآن يرد ذلك كما في قوله

TABATABAI:3:79-80#20/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#20/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#20/r1.claim: The Qur'an denies that one person bears another's sin, a principle reason supports because punishing the innocent is unjust.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#20/r1.anchor: ألا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى * وأن ليس للإنسان إلا ما سعى

TABATABAI:3:79-80#20/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#20/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#20/r2.claim: The Qur'an distinguishes major sins from lesser ones and says sins below polytheism may be forgiven; polytheism requires repentance for forgiveness.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#20/r2.anchor: إن تجتنبوا كبائر ما تنهون عنه نكفر عنكم سيئاتكم

TABATABAI:3:79-80#20/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#20/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#20/r3.claim: Reason rejects treating every sin alike: a slap differs from murder, and eating from the tree does not merit eternal punishment like disbelief.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#20/r3.anchor: فاللطم غير القتل والنظر المريب غير الزنا وهكذا

TABATABAI:3:79-80#20/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#20/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#20/r4.claim: The Christian solution to a supposed conflict between mercy and justice assumes a humanlike God governed by external interests and liable to error, ignorance, and change.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#20/r4.anchor: أنهم يرون أن الله تعالى وتقدس موجود خالق ينسب وينتهي إليه هذا العالم المخلوق بجميع أجزائه غير أنه إنما يفعل بإرادة وعلم في نفسه

TABATABAI:3:79-80#20/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#20/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#20/r5.claim: Such a being would be material, bodily, created, and human rather than the necessary Creator.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#20/r5.anchor: والذي هذا شأنه يكون موجودا ماديا جسمانيا واقعا تحت ناموس الحركة والتغير والاستكمال

TABATABAI:3:79-80#21/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#21/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#21/r1.claim: The Qur'an and decisive reason affirm God's absolute perfection and immutability, excluding bodily form and human frailties; the Two Testaments attribute such traits to God.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#21/r1.anchor: والقرآن في جميع هذه المعاني المذكورة ينزه الله تعالى عن هذه الأوهام الخرافية كما يقول تعالى سبحان الله عما يصفون الصافات 159

TABATABAI:3:79-80#21/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#21/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#21/r2.claim: Incarnation cannot unite the necessary, timeless, spaceless God with a human body that develops from embryo to fetus, whatever Christian group’s account of the union.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#21/r2.anchor: فكيف يمكن تعقل الإتحاد بينهما بوجه

TABATABAI:3:79-80#22/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#22/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#22/r1.claim: Paul's attacks on philosophy and reason serve propagation and preaching strategy, as the context of his letters shows.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#22/r1.anchor: وليست إلا لسياسة النشر والإذاعة والتبليغ والعظة

TABATABAI:3:79-80#22/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#22/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#22/r2.claim: Given their portrayal of God as prone to error, claiming divine immunity from mistakes is incoherent; rebellion is inapplicable to God, so divine impeccability is also inapplicable.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#22/r2.anchor: وأما الذنب والمعصية بمعنى التمرد فيما يجب فيه الطاعة والانقياد فهو غير متصور في حقه تعالى فالعصمة أيضا غير متصورة في حقه سبحانه

TABATABAI:3:79-80#22/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#22/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#22/r3.claim: If God can become human, he could become any species or several at once and perform incompatible acts or bear contradictory attributes.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#22/r3.anchor: أي يتصف بحقيقة كل نوع من هذه الأنواع الخارجية فتارة يكون إنسانا من الأناسي وتارة فرسا وتارة طائرا وتارة حشرة

TABATABAI:3:79-80#22/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#22/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#22/r4.claim: He questions the claim that Christ bore crucifixion and a curse because the crucified are cursed, asking what such a curse means.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#22/r4.anchor: وثامنا قولهم إنه تحمل الصلب واللعن أيضا لأن المصلوب ملعون

TABATABAI:3:79-80#23/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#23/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#23/r1.claim: The Qur'an calls human beings needy and God self-sufficient, whose nature excludes need, defect, abasement, or humiliation.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#23/r1.anchor: يا أيها الناس أنتم الفقراء إلى الله والله هو الغني فاطر 15

TABATABAI:3:79-80#23/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#23/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#23/r2.claim: If union makes God literally cursed, it entails the stated impossibility; if the curse is figurative, another's suffering cannot make God himself the ransom.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#23/r2.anchor: فإن كان الأول لزم المحذور الذي ذكرناه وإن كان الثاني عاد الإشكال

TABATABAI:3:79-80#23/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#23/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#23/r3.claim: The atonement claim shows that its proponents misunderstand sin, its connection to afterlife punishment, and its relation to religious law.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#23/r3.anchor: يدل ذلك على أنهم لم يحصلوا حقيقة معنى الذنوب والخطايا وكيفية استتباعها للعقاب الأخروي

TABATABAI:3:79-80#23/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#23/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#23/r4.claim: In ordinary human society, laws are conventional rules designed to protect communal interests, with punishment serving as deterrence.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#23/r4.anchor: أن الأحكام والقوانين التي يقع فيها المخالفة والتمرد ثم الذنب والخطيئة إنما هي أمور وضعية اعتبارية

TABATABAI:3:79-80#23/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#23/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#23/r5.claim: Qur'anic teaching goes further: obedience and disobedience form real inner virtues or vices that become afterlife bliss or torment, with Paradise and Hell representing nearness to or distance from God.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#23/r5.anchor: وهذه هي التي تهيئ للإنسان نعمة أخروية أو نقمة أخروية اللتين ممثلهما الجنة والنار وحقيقتهما القرب والبعد من الله

TABATABAI:3:79-80#24/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#24/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#24/r1.claim: Divine law completes God's creative guidance: it supports sound social life and afterlife happiness through law and worship that purify the person and bring divine honor.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#24/r1.anchor: شأنه تعالى إيصال كل نوع إلى كمال وجوده وهدف ذاته ومن كمال وجود الإنسان النظام النوعي الصالح في الدنيا

TABATABAI:3:79-80#24/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#24/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#24/r2.claim: If Adam's one sin doomed him and his descendants absent Christ's ransom, legislation before Christ could not help; Abraham, Moses, and earlier righteous people would have died saved or damned without a meaningful role for their laws.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#24/r2.anchor: فما فائدة تشريع الدين قبل المسيح؟ وما فائدة تشريعه معه؟ وما فائدة تشريعه بعده؟!

TABATABAI:3:79-80#24/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#24/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#24/r3.claim: The only way to explain pre-ransom legislation would be that God knowingly concealed its futility and misled people while hoping to solve the problem later.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#24/r3.anchor: إلا أن يقال إنه تعالى كان يعلم أن لو لم يرفع محذور خطيئة آدم لم ينفعه شيء من هذه التشريعات قط

TABATABAI:3:79-80#25/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#25/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#25/r1.claim: If ransom brings mercy to all without regard to belief or deeds, religious teaching and good works after it have no purpose.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#25/r1.anchor: فما هي الفائدة في الإيمان بالمعارف الحقة والإتيان بالأعمال الصالحة بعد ارتفاع محذور الخطيئة

TABATABAI:3:79-80#25/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#25/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#25/r2.claim: If ransom helps only believers in Christ, almost all people remain damned, including earlier prophets; this conflicts with the Gospels' affirmation of Torah and its mission.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#25/r2.anchor: إذ لا يبقى من الناس - آدم فمن دونه - في حظيرة النجاة والخلاص إلا شرذمة منهم وهم المؤمنون بالمسيح والروح

TABATABAI:3:79-80#25/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#25/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#25/r3.claim: The claim that earlier scriptures promised Christ is speculative before Moses, and a promise of salvation is not an instruction to believe in or worship Christ.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#25/r3.anchor: على أن البشارة لو فإنما هي بشارة بالخلاص وليست بدعوة إلى الإيمان والتدين به

TABATABAI:3:79-80#25/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#25/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#25/r4.claim: Appealing to a prophecy does not cure the uselessness of moral and practical law, including Christ's own teachings in the Gospels.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#25/r4.anchor: وثانيا إن ذلك لا يدفع محذور لغوية الدعوة في فروع الدين من الأخلاق والأفعال حتى من المسيح نفسه

TABATABAI:3:79-80#25/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#25/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#25/r5.claim: The doctrine still makes God's purpose of extending mercy and happiness to all fail, since all but a small group face eternal punishment.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#25/r5.anchor: وقد آل أمره إلى عقابهم والغضب عليهم وإهلاكهم للأبد إلا شرذمة منهم

TABATABAI:3:79-80#26/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#26/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#26/r1.claim: God gives every created thing its form and guides it to its end; this universal guidance includes religious guidance for human beings.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#26/r1.anchor: الذي أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى طه 50

TABATABAI:3:79-80#26/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#26/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#26/r2.claim: God's first religious guidance to Adam and his companions promised safety to followers and lasting punishment to rejecters, summarizing later legislation with its promises and warnings.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#26/r2.anchor: فمن تبع هداي فلا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون * والذين كفروا وكذبوا بآياتنا أولئك أصحاب النار هم فيها خالدون

TABATABAI:3:79-80#26/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#26/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#26/r3.claim: God neither wavers from nor reverses a settled decree; the cited verses say he does not forget, faces no superior obstruction, and carries out his purpose.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#26/r3.anchor: فبين أنه لا يتردد فيما جزم به من الأمر ولا ينقض ما أنفذه من الأمر

TABATABAI:3:79-80#26/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#26/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#26/r4.claim: God created and legislated purposefully, then repays each person according to deeds without being overruled by a partner, ransom, friendship, or unauthorized intercession; ransom itself is substitution to transfer harm from the liable person.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#26/r4.anchor: وإن شرا فشر من غير أن يغلبه تعالى غالب أو يحكم عليه حاكم من شريك أو فدية أو خلة أو شفاعة من دون إذنه

TABATABAI:3:79-80#26/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#26/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#26/r5.claim: Ransom is a transaction that transfers the right and authority over the liable person to a substitute, thereby sparing the liable person from harm.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#26/r5.anchor: فالتفدية نوع معاملة ينتزع بها حق صاحب الحق وسلطنته عن المفدي عنه إلى الفداء فيستنقذ به المفدي عنه من أن يلحق به الشر

TABATABAI:3:79-80#27/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#27/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#27/r1.claim: Divine sovereignty is real and cannot be transferred; unlike human legal sovereignty, which is conventional and alterable, all things and their effects exist through God.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#27/r1.anchor: فإن السلطنة الإلهية - على خلاف السلطنة الوضعية الاعتبارية الإنسانية - سلطنة حقيقية واقعية غير جائزة التبديل مستحيلة الصرف

TABATABAI:3:79-80#27/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#27/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#27/r2.claim: God explicitly rules out ransom on the Day of Judgment.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#27/r2.anchor: وقد نفى الله سبحانه الفدية بالخصوص في قوله فاليوم لا يؤخذ منكم فدية

TABATABAI:3:79-80#27/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#27/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#27/r3.claim: Jesus says his only role among people was the divinely assigned mission of conveying the message and witnessing their deeds while he remained with them.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#27/r3.anchor: لم يكن لي شأن فيهم إلا ما أنت وظفته علي وعينته وهو تبليغ الرسالة والشهادة على الأعمال ما دمت فيهم

TABATABAI:3:79-80#27/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#27/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#27/r4.claim: Jesus leaves their punishment and forgiveness entirely to God, which rules out ransom because he claims no power or connection to release them from divine punishment.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#27/r4.anchor: وفي ذلك نفي الفداء إذ لو كان هناك فداء لم يصح تبريه من أعمالهم وإرجاع العذاب والمغفرة معا إلى الله سبحانه

TABATABAI:3:79-80#28/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:79-80#28/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:79-80#28/r1.claim: The denied compensation in 2:48, the sale in 2:254, and protection from God in 40:33 each describe something akin to ransom, so their denial rejects ransom.
TABATABAI:3:79-80#28/r1.anchor: فإن العدل في الآية الأولى والبيع في الآية الثانية والعصمة من الله في الآية الثالثة مما ينطبق عليه الفداء
