THALABI:v3p101/r12.claim: In a report through ʿAṭāʾ ibn al-Sāʾib, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr defines rabbāniyyūn as wise and God-fearing.
THALABI:v3p101/r12.anchor: وروى الفضل بن عياض عن عطاء بن السائب عن سعيد بن جبير: حكماء أتقياء.

THALABI:v3p101/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p101/r13.speaker: ابن زيد
THALABI:v3p101/r13.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets them as people’s governors and leaders, including some who are devout and sincere.
THALABI:v3p101/r13.anchor: ابن زيد: ولاة الناس، وقادتهم بعضهم متعبدين مخلصين.

THALABI:v3p101/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p101/r14.speaker: عطاء
THALABI:v3p101/r14.claim: ʿAṭāʾ describes them as learned, wise people devoted to God among His creation.
THALABI:v3p101/r14.anchor: عطاء: علماء حكماء نصبا لله في خلقه.

THALABI:v3p101/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p101/r15.speaker: أبو عبيد
THALABI:v3p101/r15.claim: Abū ʿUbayd says he did not recognize the term rabbāniyyūn in Arabic usage.
THALABI:v3p101/r15.anchor: أبو عبيد: لم يعرف العرب الربانيين.

THALABI:v3p101/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p101/r16.speaker: أبو عبيد
THALABI:v3p101/r16.claim: Abū ʿUbayd transmits a scholar’s definition: one who knows lawful and unlawful matters, commands and prohibitions, and the history and future of the community.
THALABI:v3p101/r16.anchor: سمعت رجلا عالما يقول: الرباني: العالم بالحلال والحرام والأمر والنهي.

THALABI:v3p101/r17.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p101/r17.speaker: المؤرخ
THALABI:v3p101/r17.claim: Al-Muʾarrikh reads the word as “devoted to your Lord,” deriving it from lordship in a faʿlānī pattern.
THALABI:v3p101/r17.anchor: المؤرخ: كونوا ربانيين تدينون لربكم، كأنه فعلاني من الربوبية.

THALABI:v3p101/r18.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p101/r18.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v3p101/r18.claim: One etymology derives rabbānī from an original rabbī, enlarged with alif and then nūn; the account calls this Syriac and compares regional nisbas.
THALABI:v3p101/r18.anchor: وقال بعضهم: كان في الأصل ربي، فأدخلت الألف للتضخيم وهو لسان السريانية، ثم أدخلت النون

THALABI:v3p101/r19.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p101/r19.speaker: المبرد
THALABI:v3p101/r19.claim: Al-Mubarrad derives rabbāniyyūn from rabban, a master of knowledge who inherits learning, teaches and reforms people, with alif and nūn for emphasis and a later nisba yāʾ.
THALABI:v3p101/r19.anchor: المبرد: الربانيون: أرباب العلم واحدها ربان وهو الذي يرث العلم ويربب الناس أي يعلمهم ويصلحهم

THALABI:v3p102/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p102/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p102/r1.claim: بما carries a sense of what is or must be, like the clauses “my wife is barren” and “who is a child in the cradle.”
THALABI:v3p102/r1.anchor: بما كنتم: معناه الوجوب أي: بما أنتم. كقوله وكانت امرأتي عاقرا

THALABI:v3p102/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p102/r2.speaker: السلمي والنخعي وابن جبير والضحاك وأهل الكوفة
THALABI:v3p102/r2.claim: These readers use the doubled form تعلمون from teaching; Abū ʿUbayda prefers this reading.
THALABI:v3p102/r2.anchor: قرأ السلمي والنخعي وابن جبير والضحاك وأهل الكوفة: تعلمون بالتشديد من التعليم، واختاره أبو عبيدة

THALABI:v3p102/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p102/r3.speaker: أبو حاتم
THALABI:v3p102/r3.claim: Abū Ḥātim prefers the light form تعلمون, deriving it from knowing; Abū ʿAmr cites وبما كنتم تدرسون as confirmation, since it does not say يدرسون.
THALABI:v3p102/r3.anchor: وقرأ الباقون تعلمون بالتخفيف من العلم، واختاره أبو حاتم، وقال أبو عمرو: وتصديقها وبما كنتم تدرسون

THALABI:v3p102/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p102/r4.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v3p102/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads تعلمون with doubled lām as “you learn.”
THALABI:v3p102/r4.anchor: وقرأ الحسن تعلمون، التاء والعين وتشديد اللام على معنى تعلمون

THALABI:v3p102/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p102/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
THALABI:v3p102/r5.claim: Abū ʿUbayda reads تدرسون from the causative form adrasa.
THALABI:v3p102/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو عبيدة: تدرسون من أدرس يدرس.

THALABI:v3p102/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p102/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
THALABI:v3p102/r6.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr reads tadrusūn from the intensive form of teaching; the remaining readers derive yadrusūn from study, meaning to read, as in al-Aʿrāf.
THALABI:v3p102/r6.anchor: وقرأ سعيد بن جبير: تدرسون من التدريس. الباقون: يدرسون من الدرس أي يقرءون

THALABI:v3p102/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p102/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v3p102/r7.claim: A report through Juwaybir, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and Ibn ʿAbbās says every believing man and woman, free person or slave, must learn the Qurʾān and study its religion; the Prophet then recited this verse.
THALABI:v3p102/r7.anchor: جويبر عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم «ما من مؤمن ذكر ولا أنثى حر ولا عبد مملوك إلا ولله عز وجل عليه حق واجب

THALABI:v3p102/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p102/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p102/r11.claim: An unattributed poetic line uses rabbānī in the sense of a learned rabbi, supporting the lexical discussion.
THALABI:v3p102/r11.anchor: لو كنت مرتهنا في الحق أنزلني … منه الحديث ورباني أحباري

THALABI:v3p102/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p102/r12.speaker: علي
THALABI:v3p102/r12.claim: ʿAlī gathers the definitions: a rabbānī is someone whose knowledge is cultivated through practice.
THALABI:v3p102/r12.anchor: وقد جمع علي (رضي الله عنه) هذه الأقاويل أجمع فقال: هو الذي يربى علمه بعمله.

THALABI:v3p102/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p102/r13.speaker: محمد بن الحنفية
THALABI:v3p102/r13.claim: At Ibn ʿAbbās’s death, Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyya called him the rabbānī of this community.
THALABI:v3p102/r13.anchor: وقال محمد بن الحنفية يوم مات ابن عباس: مات رباني هذه الأمة.

ASAD-NOTES:3:79#n61/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:3:79#n61/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:3:79#n61/r1.claim: Asad identifies Jesus as the obvious referent and explains the sentence as saying that God grants a human revelation, judgment, and prophethood, after which he could not demand worship.
ASAD-NOTES:3:79#n61/r1.anchor: This obvious reference to Jesus reads, literally, "It is not [possible] for a human being that God should grant him

ASAD-NOTES:3:79#n61/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:3:79#n61/r2.speaker: Zamakhshari
ASAD-NOTES:3:79#n61/r2.claim: Zamakhshari treats hukm, judgment or sound judgment, as synonymous here with hikmah, wisdom.
ASAD-NOTES:3:79#n61/r2.anchor: Zamakhshari regards the term hukm ("judgment" or "sound judgment") occurring in the above sentence as synonymous

ASAD-NOTES:3:79#n62/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:3:79#n62/r1.speaker: Sibawayh (as quoted by Razi)
ASAD-NOTES:3:79#n62/r1.claim: A rabbani is one devoted exclusively to knowing the Sustainer and obeying Him, a meaning close to man of God.
ASAD-NOTES:3:79#n62/r1.anchor: According to Sibawayh (as quoted by Razi), a rabbani is "one who devotes himself exclusively to the endeavour to know the Sustainer (ar-rabb) and to obey Him"

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p376#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p376#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p376#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the verse followed the Jews’ and Christians’ claim to Abraham’s religion: when challenged, they asked whether Muḥammad wanted them to worship him; he refused and revelation followed.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p376#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p376#2/r2.speaker: الضحاك ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p376#2/r2.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Muqātil say Christians claimed Jesus was a worshipped god and alleged that Jesus had told them so; the verse was revealed about them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p376#2/r2.anchor: وقال الضحاك (¬2)، ومقاتل (¬3): كانت النصارى تقول: إن عيسى إله معبود

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p376#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p376#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p376#2/r3.claim: On Ibn ʿAbbās’s account, the human who could not call people to worship him is Muḥammad.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p376#2/r3.anchor: يعني: محمدا عليه السلام على قول ابن عباس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p376#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p376#2/r4.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p376#2/r4.claim: On Muqātil’s account, the human who could not call people to worship him is Jesus.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p376#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p376#2/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p376#2/r5.claim: Ḥukm means knowledge and jurisprudence in language and exegesis, as in the description of John in 19:12.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p376#2/r5.anchor: و (الحكم) (¬6) في اللغة وفي التفسير: العلم والفقه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p376#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p376#2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p376#2/r6.claim: Ḥukm can also mean judging with justice, as illustrated by al-Nābigha’s line “judge like the judgment of the clan’s young woman.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p376#2/r6.anchor: و (الحكم): القضاء بالعدل (¬7) أيضا؛ ومنه قول النابغة:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p378/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p378/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p378/r1.claim: The verse denies that a human could both receive prophethood and invite people to worship someone other than God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p378/r1.anchor: أي: ما كان لبشر أن يجمع بين هذين: بين النبوة، وبين دعاء الخلق إلى عبادة غير الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p378/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p378/r2.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p378/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj says God does not choose liars as prophets; if a human did this, God would remove the signs of prophethood, and ثم يقول is coordinated with أن يؤتيه.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p378/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج (¬1): أي: الله عز وجل لا يصطفي لنبوته الكذبة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p378/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p378/r3.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p378/r3.claim: The Author of the Arrangement construes يُؤتيه الله as an adjective of the indefinite بشر; the negative concerns telling people to worship the speaker, and the clause’s أن is displaced before ثم. He compares 48:25.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p378/r3.anchor: وقال صاحب النظم: {ما كان لبشر}: نفي، والنفي واقع غير موقعه؛ لأن التأويل ما كان لبشر يؤتيه الله الكتاب والحكم والنبوة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p379/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p379/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p379/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says ʿibād, “servants,” is the language of Muzayna for slaves.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p379/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬9): هذه لغة # مزينة (¬1)، تقول للعبيد: (عباد)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p379/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p379/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p379/r2.claim: In “but be rabbānī,” the verb “say” is omitted because the earlier command supplies it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p379/r2.anchor: أي: ولكن تقول: كونوا، فحذف القول؛ لدلالة الأولى عليه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p379/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p379/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p379/r3.claim: All agree that rabbānī means a learned person; al-Azharī’s report through al-ʿArūḍī and al-Mundhirī from Abū Ṭālib gives the same gloss, and Abū al-ʿAbbās calls rabbāniyyūn scholars.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p379/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p379/r4.speaker: سيبويه
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p379/r4.claim: Sībawayh derives rabbānī with an added alif and nūn to specify knowledge of the Lord, by analogy with forms denoting abundant hair, beard, or neck.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p379/r4.anchor: وقال سيبويه: زادوا ألفا ونونا في (الرباني)، إذا (¬2) أرادوا تخصيصا بعلم الرب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p379/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p379/r5.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p379/r5.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrābī defines a rabbānī as a learned teacher who starts people with elementary knowledge before advanced subjects.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p379/r5.anchor: وقال ابن الأعرابي: الرباني: العالم المعلم، الذي يغدوا الناس (¬4)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p379/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p379/r6.speaker: المبرد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p379/r6.claim: Al-Mubarrad derives rabbānī from nurturing: a scholar who teaches and improves people and manages their affairs; alif and nūn intensify the description before the nisba ending.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p379/r6.anchor: وقال المبرد (¬5): الربانيون: أرباب العلم، وأحدهما: رباني

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p379/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p379/r7.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p379/r7.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says the Arabs did not know the word rabbāniyyūn.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p379/r7.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة (¬1): لم تعرف العرب (ربانيين)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p379/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p379/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p379/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, in Saʿīd ibn Jubayr’s transmission, glosses rabbāniyyūn as teachers; Murra al-Hamdānī says likewise, and Ibn Muslim chooses this, supported by Ibn al-Aʿrābī and al-Mubarrad.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p379/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية سعيد بن جبير (¬5): ربانيين؛ أي: معلمين (¬6). وهو قول مرة الهمداني (¬7)، واختيار عبد الله بن مسلم (¬8)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p383/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p383/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p383/r1.claim: The bāʾ in “by what you used to know/teach” attaches to “be”; mā plus the verb is a verbal noun, yielding “be rabbānī by your knowing or teaching.” The same analysis applies to the next clause, with a parallel in 7:51.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p383/r1.anchor: في {بما}، متعلقة بقوله: {كونوا}. و (ما) في القراءتين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p383/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p383/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p383/r2.claim: The light reading taʿlamūn is from knowledge and means knowing; it takes one object, as in 2:65 and 2:220. A report from ʿAmr argues from tadrusūn, and the one-object construction favors lightening.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p383/r2.anchor: فأما قوله: {تعلمون الكتاب}، من قرأه (¬7) بالتخفيف؛ فهو من (العلم)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p383/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p383/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p383/r3.claim: The intensive reading has an omitted second object, “people” or “others”; it is more emphatic because teaching entails knowledge, while knowledge does not entail teaching.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p383/r3.anchor: ومن قرأ بالتشديد: فالمفعول الثاني محذوف، تقديره: بماكنتم تعلمون الناس الكتاب، أو غيركم الكتاب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p383/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p383/r4.speaker: مرة بن شراحيل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p383/r4.claim: Murra ibn Sharāḥīl cites ʿAlqama as a rabbānī who taught people the Qurʾān, supporting the emphasis on teaching.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p383/r4.anchor: يدل عليه: قول مرة بن شراحيل (¬2): كان علقمة من الربانيين الذي يعلمون الناس القرآن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p383/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p383/r5.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p383/r5.claim: Al-Zajjāj interprets the command as teaching and explaining scripture to people through one’s knowledge and study; alternatively, it means deserving the title learned through sincerity and fulfilling its duty.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p383/r5.anchor: قال الزجاج (¬3): معنى قوله: {كونوا ربانيين بما كنتم تعلمون الكتاب}: كونوا معلمي الناس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p385/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p385/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p385/r1.claim: Tadrusūn means “you read”; the source links the verb to 7:169 and defers fuller discussion of dars to 6:105.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p385/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {وبما كنتم تدرسون}. أي: تقرأون

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:78-79/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:78-79/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:78-79/r2.claim: When Jews claimed to follow Abraham's religion and God disproved them, they angrily said Muhammad wanted them to take him as a lord; the Prophet denied commanding worship of anyone but God, and the verse was revealed.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:78-79/r2.anchor: لما ادعت اليهود أنهم على دين إبراهيم عليه السلام وكذبهم الله تعالى غضبوا وقالوا: ما يرضيك منا يا محمد إلا أن نتخذك ربا،

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:78-79/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:78-79/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:78-79/r3.claim: A human cannot combine prophethood with calling people to worship someone other than God.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:78-79/r3.anchor: أن يجمع بين هذين: بين النبوة وبين دعاء الخلق إلى عبادة غير الله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:78-79/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:78-79/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:78-79/r4.claim: Being rabbaniyyun means becoming teachers through knowledge and study, teaching and explaining; the Prophet said this to Jews because they knew what the Arabs did not.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:78-79/r4.anchor: أي: يقول: كونوا معلمي الناس بعلمكم ودرسكم، علموا الناس وبينوا لهم،

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:78-79/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:78-79/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:78-79/r5.claim: The Prophet said this to Jews because they were People of the Book and knew what the Arabs did not.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:78-79/r5.anchor: وكذا كان يقول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لليهود؛ لأنهم كانوا أهل كتاب يعلمون ما لا تعلمه العرب.

SIBAWAYH:فالحروفالتيتشركالواووالفاءوثموأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فالحروفالتيتشركالواووالفاءوثموأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فالحروفالتيتشركالواووالفاءوثموأ.claim: The particles و، ف، ثم, and أو coordinate أن-clauses, as in wanting someone to come and then speak.
SIBAWAYH:فالحروفالتيتشركالواووالفاءوثموأ.anchor: فالحروف التي تشرك الواو والفاء وثم وأو

SIBAWAYH:فالحروفالتيتشركالواووالفاءوثموأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فالحروفالتيتشركالواووالفاءوثموأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فالحروفالتيتشركالواووالفاءوثموأ.claim: A following verb may instead be raised under these conjunctions when construed as an independent clause.
SIBAWAYH:فالحروفالتيتشركالواووالفاءوثموأ.anchor: ويجوز الرفع في جميع هذه الحروف التي تشرك

SIBAWAYH:فالحروفالتيتشركالواووالفاءوثموأ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:فالحروفالتيتشركالواووالفاءوثموأ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:فالحروفالتيتشركالواووالفاءوثموأ.claim: In 3:79, ثم يقول is coordinated with أن يؤتيه and follows the same subjunctive construction.

ELMALILI:3:83/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:83/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:83/r3.claim: Elmalılı derives rabbānī from rabb or rabbān, meaning a lord or educator; he points to the later description of many rabbiyyūn with a prophet.

QUSHAYRI:v1p155/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p155/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p155/r1.claim: A rabbanī is unaffected by changing turns of destiny.
QUSHAYRI:v1p155/r1.anchor: ويقال الرباني الذي لا تؤثر فيه تصاريف الأقدار على اختلافها

QUSHAYRI:v1p155/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p155/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p155/r2.claim: A rabbanī remains unchanged by affliction and unharmed by blessing, steady through changing events.
QUSHAYRI:v1p155/r2.anchor: ويقال الرباني الذي لا تغيره محنة ولا تضره نعمة - فهو على حالة واحدة في اختلاف الطوارق

QUSHAYRI:v1p155/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p155/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p155/r3.claim: A rabbanī is not shaken by incoming thoughts or events; one moved by tenderness, upheaval, or dangers does not meet the description.
QUSHAYRI:v1p155/r3.anchor: ويقال الرباني الذي لا يتأثر بورود وارد عليه ، فمن استنطقته رقة قلب ، أو استماله هجوم أمر

QUSHAYRI:v1p155/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p155/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p155/r4.claim: A rabbanī's inner self is indifferent to events, while his outward conduct never falls short of the Sacred Law.
QUSHAYRI:v1p155/r4.anchor: ويقال إن الرباني هو الذي لا يبالي بشيء من الحوادث بقلبه وسره ، ومن كان لا يقصر في شيء من الشرع بفعله

QUSHAYRI:v1p155/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p155/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p155/r5.claim: Teaching and studying scripture reflects God's successive beneficence; people should not attribute even an atom of good or evil independently to human teachers.
QUSHAYRI:v1p155/r5.anchor: من توالي إحساني إليكم ، وتضاعف نعمتي لديكم . أي لا تنسبون إليهم ذرة من الإثبات في الخير والشر

QUSHAYRI:v1p155/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p155/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p155/r6.claim: Another lesson is to know the limits of human creaturehood and the right of divine Lordship.
QUSHAYRI:v1p155/r6.anchor: ويقال يعرفكم حد البشرية وحق الربوبية

QUSHAYRI:v1p155/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p155/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p155/r7.claim: Another lesson is to honor prophets by the Law while recognizing creation's smallness before divine Lordship.
QUSHAYRI:v1p155/r7.anchor: ويقال يأمركم بتوقيرهم من حيث الأمر والشريعة ، وتحقير قدر الخلق

BURHAN:v3p81/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p81/r1.speaker: بعضهم
BURHAN:v3p81/r1.claim: One analysis takes لا as genuine negation and supplies an omitted coordinated clause, understood as and that they believe.
BURHAN:v3p81/r1.anchor: وقيل نافية وحذف المعطوف أي وأنهم يؤمنون

BURHAN:v3p81/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p81/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p81/r4.claim: With يأمركم in the accusative, one view coordinates it with يؤتيه and treats لا as extra, reinforcing the earlier negation.
BURHAN:v3p81/r4.anchor: على قراءة من نصب ﴿ يأمركم ﴾ 2 عطفا على ﴿ يؤتيه ﴾ ف لا زائدة مؤكدة لمعنى النفي السابق

BURHAN:v3p81/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p81/r5.speaker: بعضهم
BURHAN:v3p81/r5.claim: Another view coordinates يأمركم with يقول: one given scripture would not call people to worship him and then order worship of angels and prophets.
BURHAN:v3p81/r5.anchor: وقيل عطف على ﴿ يقول ﴾ والمعنى ما كان لبشر أن ينصبه الله للدعاء إلى عبادته

BURHAN:v3p81/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p81/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p81/r6.claim: A further view says لا is not extra: Muhammad forbade Quraysh and the People of the Book from worshipping angels, ʿUzayr, or Jesus.
BURHAN:v3p81/r6.anchor: وقيل ليست زائدة لأنه عليه الصلاة والسلام كان ينهى قريشا عن عبادة الملائكة وأهل الكتاب عن عبادة عزيز وعيسى

DAMGHANI:v1p410/r1.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p410/r1.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p410/r1.claim: Kāna can express what is proper or fitting: it is not fitting for a person given scripture and prophecy to ask people to worship him.
DAMGHANI:v1p410/r1.anchor: كان بمعنى ينبغي قوله تعالى في سورة آل عمران

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p517/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p517/r1.speaker: علي بن عبيد الله
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p517/r1.claim: Kāna is a past-tense verb whose basic sense is to occur or exist; it is complete without a predicate for existence and defective with a predicate for an attribute.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p517/r1.anchor: قال شيخنا علي بن عبيد الله : كان فعل ماض في قولك : كان يكون كونا فهو كائن . ومعناه في الأصل وقع ووجد .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p517/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p517/r2.speaker: علي بن عبيد الله
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p517/r2.claim: When kāna describes an attribute, it is defective and requires a predicate.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p517/r2.anchor: وإذا أريد بها الوصف كانت ناقصة تحتاج إلى خبر تقول من ذلك كان زيد قائما .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p517/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p517/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p517/r5.claim: Kāna can mean “ought” or “should,” expressing that something is not proper.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p517/r5.anchor: والثالث : بمعنى ينبغي . ومنه قوله تعالى في آل عمران :

NASHR:v2p240/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p240/r6.speaker: ابن عامر والكوفيون
NASHR:v2p240/r6.claim: Ibn Amir and the Kufans read تُعَلِّمُونَ with a doubled lām, meaning “you teach”; the other readers have the lighter تَعْلَمُونَ, “you know/learn.”
NASHR:v2p240/r6.anchor: (واختلفوا) في: تعلمون الكتاب فقرأ ابن عامر، والكوفيون بضم التاء وفتح العين

IBNHISHAM:v1p554/r1.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p554/r1.speaker: أبو رافع القرظي
IBNHISHAM:v1p554/r1.claim: At a meeting of Jewish scholars and Christians from Najran, Abu Rafi and a Najrani Christian asked whether Muhammad wanted them to worship him as Christians worship Jesus; Muhammad denied it, and the verses were revealed in response.
IBNHISHAM:v1p554/r1.anchor: وقال أبو رافع القرظي، حين اجتمعت الأحبار من يهود، والنصارى من أهل نجران عند رسول الله

IBNHISHAM:v1p554/r2.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p554/r2.speaker: ابن هشام
IBNHISHAM:v1p554/r2.claim: Ibn Hisham defines rabbaniyyun as learned jurists and leaders, with rabbani as the singular; he cites an anonymous poem using the word for a scholar of the rabbis.
IBNHISHAM:v1p554/r2.anchor: قال ابن هشام: الربانيون: العلماء الفقهاء السادة، واحدهم: رباني

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r1.claim: A warning against interpretation should prompt careful reflection and reject haste; scholars differ in this, and some carry scrupulous caution to excess.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r1.anchor: التسرع إلى ذلك ، وهذا مقام تفاوت العلماء فيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r2.speaker: الأصمعي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r2.claim: Al-Asma'i refused to explain Quranic vocabulary: he would not say أسرى and سرى or أعصفت and عصفت were equivalent, nor add to his heard definition of خليل as pure, firm affection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r2.anchor: وكان الأصمعي لا يفسر كلمة من العربية إذا كانت واقعة في القرآن ، ذكر ذلك في المزهر فأبى أن يتكلم في أن سرى وأسرى بمعنى واحد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r3.claim: Ibn Ashur says that outside the fundamentals of belief, God requires reasoned probability supported by evidence, with suitable evidence varying by subject; the principles of understanding speech are known.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r3.anchor: والحق أن الله ما كلفنا في غير أصول الإعتقاد بأكثر من حصول الظن المستند إلى الأدلة والأدلة متنوعة على حسب أنواع المستند فيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r4.claim: Ibn Ashur rejects the slogan that Quran interpretation must be confined to transmitted material because its advocates have not defined what counts as transmitted.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r4.anchor: أما الذين جمدوا على القول بأن تفسير القرآن يجب أن لا يعدو ما هو مأثور فهم رموا هذه الكلمة على عواهنها ولم يضبطوا مرادهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r5.claim: If transmission means only sound or fair Prophetic explanations, the restriction narrows Quranic meanings, contradicts their own tafsirs, and falsely implies early Muslim imams limited themselves to Prophetic reports.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r5.anchor: فإذا التزموا هذا الظن بهم فقد ضيقوا سعة معاني القرآن وينابيع ما يستنبط من علومه ، وناقضوا أنفسهم فيما دونوه من التفاسير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r6.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r6.claim: Umar asked learned people about the meanings of many verses without requiring them to cite a Prophetic explanation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r6.anchor: وقد سأل عمر بن الخطاب أهل العلم عن معاني آيات كثيرة ولم يشترط عليهم أن يرووا له ما بلغهم في تفسيرها عن النبي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r7.claim: If transmission includes only the Prophet and Companions, as al-Suyuti’s al-Durr al-Manthur appears to do, the material remains too scant to sustain tafsir.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r7.anchor: وإن أرادوا بالمأثور ما روى عن النبي وعن الصحابة خاصة وهو ما يظهر من صنيع السيوطي في تفسيره الدر المنثور ، لم يتسع ذلك المضيق إلا قليلا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r8.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r8.claim: Ibn Ashur says little tafsir is transmitted from most Companions; reports from Ali vary in soundness, and Ali said he had no extra text beyond the Book, only understanding God grants.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r8.anchor: لأن أكثر الصحابة لا يؤثر عنهم في التفسير إلا شيء قليل سوى ما يروى عن علي بن أبي طالب على ما فيه من صحيح وضعيف وموضوع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r9.claim: Reports from Ibn Masud, Ibn Umar, Anas, and Abu Hurayra are mentioned; what is transmitted from Ibn Abbas is mostly his own opinion, with differences among transmitters.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r9.anchor: وما يروي عن ابن مسعود وعبد الله بن عمر وأنس وأبي هريرة . وأما ابن عباس فكان أكثر ما يروي عنه قولا برأيه على تفاوت بين رواته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r10.claim: If transmission means early material from Ibn Abbas’s and Ibn Masud’s students, successors’ unattributed, differing interpretations still show they reasoned independently, as seen in al-Tabari and similar works.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r10.anchor: فقد أخذوا يفتحون الباب من شقه ، ويقربون ما بعد من الشقة ، إذ لا محيص لهم من الاعتراف بأن التابعين قالوا أقوالا في معاني القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r11.speaker: الطبري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r11.claim: Although al-Tabari sets out to restrict himself to Companion and Successor reports, he repeatedly selects and prefers interpretations using evidence from Arabic, thus going beyond that limit.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r11.anchor: وقد التزم الطبري في تفسيره أن يقتصر على ما هو مروي عن الصحابة والتابعين ، لكنه لا يلبث في كل آية أن يتخطى ذلك إلى اختياره منها وترجيح بعضها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r12.speaker: بقي بن مخلد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r12.claim: Baqi ibn Makhlad preceded al-Tabari’s approach, though Ibn Ashur says his tafsir has not been seen; Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Hakim followed a similar path.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r12.anchor: وقد سبقه إليه بقي ابن مخلد ولم نقف على تفسيره ، وشاكل الطبري فيه معاصروه ، مثل ابن حاتم وابن مردويه والحاكم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r13.claim: Ibn Ashur praises exegetes who did not confine themselves to transmitted material: al-Farra and Abu Ubayda, then al-Zajjaj and al-Rummani, and later al-Zamakhshari and Ibn Atiyya.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p31/r13.anchor: فلله در الذين لم يحبسوا أنفسهم في تفسير القرآن على ما هو مأثور مثل الفراء وأبي عبيدة من الأولين ، والزجاج والرماني ممن بعدهم

JISHUMI:v1p856/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p856/r6.speaker: نافع
JISHUMI:v1p856/r6.claim: Nafiʿ reads the prophets with hamza, while the other readers omit it; both forms occur in the Qurʾan.
JISHUMI:v1p856/r6.anchor: والنبيئين بالهمز وغير الهمز لغتان، وورد القرآن بهما فقرأ نافع بالهمز، والباقون بترك الهمز،

JISHUMI:v1p856/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p856/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p856/r7.claim: With hamza, nabīʾ derives from nabaʾ, news: a prophet is named for reporting from God; the source cites 78:1–2 and 38:67.
JISHUMI:v1p856/r7.anchor: فأما الهمز فأصله النبأ، وهو الخبر، والإنباء الإخبار، ومنه: (عم يتساءلون (1) عن النبإ العظيم (2)،

JISHUMI:v1p856/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p856/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p856/r8.claim: Omitting hamza is preferred because it is the language of Quraysh and the Hijaz.
JISHUMI:v1p856/r8.anchor: فأما ترك الهمز فهو الاختيار؛ لأنه لغة قريش وأهل الحجاز،

JISHUMI:v1p856/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p856/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p856/r9.claim: An unnamed man addressed the Prophet with hamza as “nabīʾ of God”; the Prophet rejected that form and said “nabī of God.”
JISHUMI:v1p856/r9.anchor: وروي أن رجلا قال: يا نبيء الله بالهمز، فقال: لست بنبيء الله، إنما أنا نبي الله بترك الهمز،

JISHUMI:v1p856/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p856/r10.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p856/r10.claim: One etymology derives the word from nabāwa, high ground, so the Prophet is exalted in rank and standing.
JISHUMI:v1p856/r10.anchor: ثم اختلفوا فقيل: أخذ من النباوة، وهي ما ارتفع من الأرض، فالنبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - هو الرفيع الشأن،

JISHUMI:v1p856/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p856/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p856/r11.claim: On the nabāwa derivation, the original form is nabiyw; waw becomes yāʾ and the two yāʾs assimilate.
JISHUMI:v1p856/r11.anchor: وأصله نبيو، فلما اجتمعت الياء والواو، والسابق ساكن أبدلت الواو ياء، وأدغمت الياء الأولى فيها،

JISHUMI:v1p856/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p856/r12.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p856/r12.claim: Another etymology links prophet to making matters clear and derives it from al-nabī, “road”; the cited poem uses the word in that sense.
JISHUMI:v1p856/r12.anchor: وقيل: سمي نبيا لبيان أمره، ووضوح خبره، أخذ من النبي، وهو عندهم الطريق، قال الشاعر:

JISHUMI:v1p856/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p856/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p856/r13.claim: The poet uses nabī to mean a road or track.
JISHUMI:v1p856/r13.anchor: فأصبح رثما دقاق الحصى ... مكان النبي من الكاثب

TIRMIDHI:3068/r1.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:3068/r1.speaker: عائشة
TIRMIDHI:3068/r1.claim: Masruq reports that ʿĀʾisha named three grave lies: that Muhammad saw God (she identifies the figure as Gabriel, seen in his created form only twice), concealed revelation, or knew the unseen; she cites revelation against each claim.
TIRMIDHI:3068/r1.anchor: عِنْدَ عَائِشَةَ فَقَالَتْ يَا أَبَا عَائِشَةَ ثَلَاثٌ مَنْ تَكَلَّمَ بِوَاحِدَةٍ مِنْهُنَّ فَقَدْ أَعْظَمَ عَلَى اللَّهِ الْفِرْيَةَ

TIRMIDHI:3068/r2.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:3068/r2.speaker: أبو عيسى
TIRMIDHI:3068/r2.claim: Tirmidhi grades the report hasan sahih.
TIRMIDHI:3068/r2.anchor: قال أبو عيسى هذا حديث حسن صحيح
